entry.summary: BlockLock makes LLM inference reproducible regardless of co-batched requests by pinning only the protected request's numerical path instead of constraining every operator. It offers two modes: fixed-width rows retaining batched decode, and terminal-anchored packing with KV-state extraction for target-only decode, avoiding the throughput costs of batch-invariant kernels or isolated prefill.

entry.title: GuidedWAM: Training-Free Energy Guidance for World Action Models in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Xiyan Su, Finn Rasmus Sch\"afer, Hojun Lim, Frank Diermeyer, Johannes Betz, Markus Lienkamp

entry.summary: GuidedWAM is a model-agnostic framework for injecting new driving objectives into frozen world action models at sampling time by constructing objectives as differentiable energies on the sampler's intermediate clean-action estimate, requiring only forward access. Stabilization comes from guidance scheduling, per-energy normalization, and velocity-bounded correction. On NAVSIM v2's hard split it improves multiple frozen models without retraining.

entry.title: Equivariant Deep Learning in Direct-Product Space for Electronic-Structure Hamiltonian Prediction

author.name: Shi Yin, Zujian Dai, Xinyang Pan, Lixin He

entry.summary: DP-Learner reformulates equivariant message passing for Hamiltonian prediction by operating in the direct-product representation over local orbital and spin bases, matching the natural structure of the Hamiltonian operator rather than direct-sum spherical tensor spaces. This improves alignment with orbital couplings, hardware execution, and memory management.

entry.title: InnerLogic-Surg: An Open Surgical Foundation Model via Continual Pretraining

author.name: Kun Yuan, Hao Ding, Yiqing Shen, Gasper Podobnik, Benjamin Killeen, Tito Porras, Axel Krieger, Mathias Unberath

entry.summary: InnerLogic-Surg is an open family of surgical vision encoders (21M-300M parameters) created by continually pretraining a transformer image encoder on millions of surgical images curated from 11,965 internet videos spanning about 2,900 hours and over fifteen procedure types. It aims to replace generic natural-image backbones with surgery-specific ones across the surgical image analysis stack. Open release of domain foundation models for surgery is a meaningful resource contribution to medical AI.

entry.title: Octopus: One Brain, Many Branches for Latent-KV Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Tianming Sha

entry.summary: Octopus is a single-model multi-agent RL framework where all threads share one backbone and coordinate over a GPU-resident DAG of KV states via five primitives (fork, read_thread, wait_threads, rewind, commit), eliminating duplicated prefix KV caches and text-summary re-prefilling of existing multi-agent LLM systems. Zero-Copy Radix Forking and co-designed RL mechanisms handle cross-branch dependencies.

entry.title: Canonical Correlation Neural Networks

author.name: Andrea Cavallo, Sundeep Prabhakar Chepuri, Charilaos Kanatsoulis, Elvin Isufi

entry.summary: The paper extends covariance neural networks (VNNs), which use the covariance matrix as a structure-free relational inductive bias, to multi-view data via canonical correlation analysis. The resulting networks incorporate in-view and cross-view covariance matrices, retaining theoretical grounding, stability, and parameter efficiency. This offers a principled architecture family for multi-view learning without requiring known graph or grid structure.

entry.title: Spectral symmetry fingerprints in equivariant representations

author.name: Jiacheng Cen, Anyi Li, Ning Lin, Zihe Wang, Ji-Rong Wen, Wenbing Huang

entry.summary: The authors show that singular-value spectra of equivariant representations serve as unified fingerprints of structural symmetry, enabling point-group identification via rank-template matching and continuous symmetry quantification. The SymFP method is orientation invariant and architecture agnostic, turning the expressivity constraints of equivariant GNNs into an analysis tool. This connects geometric deep learning with symmetry detection in physical structures.

entry.title: Optimal Learning in Games with Arbitrary Delays: Best-of-Both-Worlds for Self-Play and Adversarial Opponents

author.name: Emmanuel Esposito, Andrew Jacobsen, Hao Qiu, Alexander Ryabchenko, Mengxiao Zhang

entry.summary: The paper introduces MAO-OMD, a single online mirror descent algorithm for zero-sum games with delayed feedback that achieves optimal fast rates in self-play while remaining minimax optimal against arbitrary opponents. In smooth zero-sum games with unknown delays, it obtains O(sigma_max + 1) social and individual regret in self-play and O(sqrt(T + d_tot)) individual regret adversarially. This best-of-both-worlds guarantee for delayed feedback is a notable theoretical advance.

entry.title: Conformal Prediction for Time-Dependent PDEs

author.name: Joshua Stiller, Annika Schneider, Eyke H\"ullermeier

entry.summary: The paper studies conformal prediction for surrogate models of time-dependent PDEs, proving that in function space, distributions at arbitrarily close times can be mutually singular, making exact coverage guarantees impossible. It further shows that in discretized settings total-coverage-style guarantees break down, explaining systematic undercoverage observed in practice. This is an important caution and toolkit contribution for uncertainty quantification in scientific ML.

entry.title: User Embeddings are Superpositions of Interpretable Behavioral Modes

author.name: Jonathan Kozaczuk, Zheng Dong, Noyan Evirgen, Keivan Majidi, Eddie K. H. Ng, Chris Porter, Qi Zhao, Jia Geng, Changmao Li, Brandon R. Feng

entry.summary: The paper argues that user embeddings in recommender and behavioral modeling systems are sparse superpositions of interpretable behavioral modes, predicted by generative models of user behavior and recoverable via sparse dictionary learning such as sparse autoencoders. Recovered modes can be automatically named and queried, improving interpretability of personalization systems.

entry.title: Latency-Aware Adaptive Best-of-$N$

author.name: Alon Jacobson, Qian Xie, Peter I. Frazier

entry.summary: The paper proposes a two-stage adaptive Best-of-N sampling algorithm for test-time compute that accounts for latency as a real cost that varies with server load, rather than a fixed token or generation count, using observed rewards and batch statistics to decide further sampling. This corrects systematic under- or over-spending by fixed-threshold methods in online serving.

entry.title: La-JEPA: Compact Robot Policies with Latent World Modeling

author.name: Mateo Cl\'emente, George Z. Xue, Amin Abyaneh, Liheng Ma, Rui Heng Yang, Tongtong Cao, Zhanguang Zhang, Yingxue Zhang

entry.summary: La-JEPA is a compact world-action model that trains a policy transformer from scratch in the feature space of a pretrained V-JEPA 2.1 encoder, jointly predicting future features and actions during training while generating only actions at inference. Among policies without embodied pretraining, it achieves state-of-the-art performance with a much smaller architecture.

entry.title: Cognitive Bias Signatures in Search-Equipped LLM Agents: A Stage-Resolved Analysis

author.name: Yanru Xiao, Yingwei Yu

entry.summary: This study examines whether LLM search agents' starting conditions shape which evidence they find and use, adapting cognitive-bias paradigms in a controlled search harness that manipulates result order, records of prior work, and initial hypotheses. Across 10 models and 1,000 synthetic search worlds with matched controls, final answers were more sensitive to initial evidence order during active search than when all evidence was supplied, with dead-end effects separable from context length. It matters for understanding and debiasing agentic search systems.

entry.title: Twists and Turns: A Graph-Based Benchmark and Framework for Long-Term Memory in Exploration Tasks

author.name: Chongyuan Dai, Yaling Shen, Zirui Song, Junfeng Liao, Jinpeng Hu, Xiuying Chen

entry.summary: Introduces LExMem, a graph-guided benchmark for long-term memory in exploration tasks—long trial-and-error endeavors like research and software development—where attempts branch, get revised, and are revived. It argues existing memory research over-focuses on factual recall and provides a framework evaluating graph-structured exploration memory.

entry.title: Challenge-Aware Knowledge Recruitment with Meta-Agent Supervision for Medical Multi-Agent Reasoning

author.name: Riccardo Riccio, Haitz S\'aez de Oc\'ariz Borde, Pietro Li\`o

entry.summary: The paper proposes challenge-aware adaptive recruitment for medical multi-agent reasoning: an external CHALLENGER agent inspects the evolving reasoning trace to identify factual or expertise gaps, triggering targeted retrieval or mid-discussion specialist recruitment. On the MEDAGENTSBENCH hard subset, upfront retrieval provides little benefit while gap-driven recruitment improves performance over standard multi-agent debate.

entry.title: Turns Matter: Advancing Streaming Video RL via Turn-Level Credit

author.name: Shuai Dong, Kanghui Tian, Linghan Chen, Wenqi Shao, Hongrui Wu, Haowen Hou, Yongfu Zhu, Xuehui Wang, Ziyue Wang, Wenpu Liu, Weichu Xie, Yuqi Xu, Congcong Wang, Kaiwen Tuo, Caoyuan Ma, Taiqiang Wu, Ji Zhao, Wenzheng Chang, Dianyi Wang, Siyuan Wang, Zhongyu Wei, Yu Qiao, Jiaqi Wang

entry.summary: TurnWise is a turn-level GRPO framework for streaming video understanding, where models repeatedly decide whether to respond or keep observing, replacing shared trajectory-level advantage with turn-level credit assignment. This corrects a mismatch that reinforces redundant replies after successes and discourages useful follow-ups after failures. The large author team suggests a substantial engineering effort on an increasingly important setting.

entry.title: Rotation Is Token-Blind: A Structural Criterion for Post-Training Quantization of Feed-Forward Geometry Transformers

author.name: Huanfei He, Bohao Zhang, Jiaxin Zhang, Wei Sui, John See, Zeyd Boukhers, Cong Yang

entry.summary: The paper analyzes post-training quantization of feed-forward 3D geometry transformers (predicting pose, depth, structure in one pass), showing that heterogeneous token types sharing one activation quantization grid create degradation that token-blind transforms like standard rotations cannot remove. It proposes a structural criterion for when rotation-based PTQ helps and a token-aware alternative. This addresses deployment efficiency for models like VGGT-style geometry transformers.

entry.title: SM4RT: Cascaded Feed-forward Model for 4D Reconstruction

author.name: Pang-Chi Lo, Jhao-Syun Lai, Tsung-Wei Ke

entry.summary: Introduces a multi-task cascade feed-forward model for dynamic scene reconstruction that first reconstructs 3D geometry, then bootstraps motion estimation from predicted structure, expressing each pixel's 3D motion in its own camera frame to reduce camera-motion ambiguity. A weakly supervised loss regularizes unlabeled point motions using labeled points to handle label sparsity.

entry.title: Symmetry-Aware Surrogate-Assisted Testing of UAVs

author.name: Anas Shrinah, Chris Bennett, Kerstin Eder

entry.summary: The authors exploit geometric symmetries between flight missions, transforming obstacle configurations into a shared canonical frame so a neural surrogate trained on one reference mission can be reused across arbitrary missions. The surrogate predicts minimum clearance and guides test generation toward safety-critical UAV scenarios, evaluated on the Aerialist benchmark against prior techniques. Exploiting symmetry for test-data efficiency is an elegant idea for autopilot validation.

entry.title: Prior-data fitted networks for variable selection

author.name: Omar Melikechi

entry.summary: This paper extends prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) beyond tabular prediction to Bayesian variable selection, introducing CD-PFN and PC-PFN that estimate posterior inclusion probabilities for conditional dependencies and parent-child relations in causal graphs without posterior sampling or data-specific modeling. Experiments on semi-synthetic and real data show they often outperform existing methods, with open-source software released.

entry.title: Goal Revelation as a Bridge Between Information-Theoretic Empowerment and Capability-Based Human Power

author.name: Jaime Ruiz-Serra, Tom\'a\v{s} Gaven\v{c}iak, Jobst Heitzig

entry.summary: The paper connects two formal power measures in Markov games: information-theoretic empowerment and capability-based individual power, showing via Fano's inequality that individual power yields a floor that lower-bounds a goal-revelation quantity linking the two. This supports quantitative analysis of instrumental convergence and human disempowerment risks.

entry.title: Circe: Training-Free LLM Self-Evaluation via Component Interaction Consistency

author.name: Shuyi Miao, Zheng Li, Xu Xie, Linrui Xu, Fei Shen, Xiaoyu Du, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: Circe is a training-free method for reference-free evaluation of LLM response correctness that exploits internal computation: rather than analyzing only hidden-state trajectories across layers, it examines how attention and FFN components interact, extracting consistency signals that complement output-based methods. This addresses the problem that output-signal-based scorers can assign high confidence to wrong answers. It targets reliable self-evaluation in deployment where references are unavailable.

entry.title: Learning the Task or Learning the Verifier? Rethinking Criteria Exposure in Embodied Self-Improvement

author.name: Wenbo Huang, Jianxin Bi, Shunyu Yang, Ruiyang Si, Rui Ni, Qiang Wang, Shulong Jiang, Yintianrun Zhang, Feixiang Ruan, Kewei Zhang, Ye Huang, Shukai Gong, Daquan Zhou

entry.summary: The paper identifies Criteria Exposure (CE), the practice of exposing embodied coding agents to benchmark success criteria during self-improvement, and asks whether this produces code that better performs the instructed task or merely optimizes the verifier. Because benchmark criteria often demand more than the language instructions, verifier scores may not faithfully reflect instruction completion. This is an important validity critique of robot benchmark progress.

entry.title: Learning a patient world model for health system simulation in intensive care

author.name: Yingtai Li, Ruoyan Wang, Yu Li, Shaohua Kevin Zhou

entry.summary: The authors propose learning a patient world model from longitudinal electronic health records that provides a shared clinical representation of patient trajectories, reusable across simulation questions in intensive care settings. This contrasts with conventional approaches that build compact, question-specific state transitions and must be redefined for each new policy question.

entry.title: FisherDistill: Diffusion Distribution Distillation via Closed-Form Fisher Critics

author.name: Mahesh Bhosale, Yuanhao Zhai, Siwei Lyu, Junsong Yuan, David Doermann, Defang Chen

entry.summary: FisherDistill replaces learned adversarial discriminators in few-step diffusion distillation with a closed-form Fisher linear discriminant computed from frozen teacher representations, using estimated first- and second-order statistics of real and generated samples. This simplifies adversarial refinement for one- to few-step image generation while retaining distribution-matching benefits.

entry.title: Masked diffusion as random sequential adsorption: an exactly solvable model for parallel decoding

author.name: Adrian Baule

entry.summary: This theoretical paper maps the error of parallel token generation in masked diffusion LLMs onto statistical physics: the error equals the entropy production of the generation process, and for Markov data generation becomes a random sequential adsorption process that is solved exactly. In the many-step limit, the unmasking error corresponds to dissipation of a slowly driven system. This provides the first exactly solvable analytical model for the parallel-decoding accuracy-speed trade-off in diffusion language models.

entry.title: Scaling Neural Motor Decoding via Decoupled Behavioral Pretraining

author.name: Divyansha Lachi, Vinam Arora, Shivashriganesh P. Mahato, Alexandre Andre, Eva L. Dyer

entry.summary: BEEMO is a multi-session neural decoding framework that decouples behavioral and neural representation learning, allowing training on arbitrary mixtures of paired neural-behavioral recordings and abundant unpaired behavioral data. A behavior decoder learns movement dynamics from trajectories alone, with neural activity injected via cross-attention when available, reducing dependence on expensive invasive paired datasets.

entry.title: XStack: A Benchmark for ML Repo Migration

author.name: Linrong Cai, Taiming Lu, Haozhe Chen, Zhuang Liu

entry.summary: XStack is a benchmark evaluating coding agents on migrating entire ML repositories from PyTorch on NVIDIA GPUs to JAX on TPUs, with verifiable pass criteria via building and testing. It offers a practical, long-horizon agentic task spanning frameworks and hardware, unlocking cross-ecosystem portability as both a need and a natural evaluation surface.

entry.title: Structural Conditional Independence Test via Neural Quantile Resolution

author.name: Khoa Nguyen, Bao Duong, Thin Nguyen

entry.summary: The authors propose QRCIT, a conditional independence test that compares conditional distributions through a quantile deformation learned by a shared residual quantile-flow model. Unlike scalar p-value tests, it localizes where the conditional law changes and provides an inspectable deformation, calibrated via conditional randomization. This handles weak, localized, or distributional (non-mean-shift) dependence that standard tests miss.

entry.title: Provably Efficient Representation Learning for Low-Rank CMDPs

author.name: Kaixuan Liu, Guojun Xiong, Shengpu Tang, Wanyun Si, Jian Li

entry.summary: The paper introduces MFRLC, a model-free primal-dual algorithm for representation learning in low-rank Constrained MDPs, balancing reward regret against constraint violations using least-squares value iteration. The authors claim it is the first representation-learning method for low-rank CMDPs with such guarantees. It advances the theory of safe/constrained reinforcement learning with function approximation.

entry.title: Binding Paraphrased Instructions to Encountered Objects in sLLM Agents under Partial Observability

author.name: Chanyoung Kim, Harim Song, Byoungchan Ko, Keonyoung Lee, Myungwon Lee, Dahuin Jung

entry.summary: The paper introduces ALFWorld-Para, a benchmark showing that RL-finetuned small LLM agents suffer 21-52% success-rate declines when instructions are paraphrased, mostly due to object synonyms. It identifies a gap between referential knowledge and object binding under partial observability, where agents know what a synonym means but fail to act on the corresponding object they have encountered.

entry.title: Same Answer, Different Future: Matched Predictions Do Not Imply Matched Belief Updating in Language Models

author.name: Weihan Li, Junhao Wu, Xinlei Chen, Tianshi Zheng

entry.summary: This study asks whether language models that produce the same probabilistic prediction via different routes—reading outcomes, summaries, instructions, or activation interventions—hold equivalent belief states. Using a Bernoulli inference task with an analytic Bayesian reference across three open-weight models, the authors append identical new evidence to each prepared state and measure how the initial belief persists. The findings show matched predictions do not imply matched belief updating, revealing hidden state differences beneath behavioral agreement.

entry.title: From What Is Used to What Is Missing: Rethinking Dynamic Rank in LoRA

author.name: Peng Xue, Guodong Fan, Guang-Yong Chen, Xing Chen

entry.summary: The paper gives a geometric characterization of dynamic rank allocation in LoRA, showing that factor gradients cannot distinguish under-optimization within the current adaptation subspace from task-relevant directions outside it, since the unobservable subspace is the normal space of the low-rank manifold. This motivates rank evolution methods that probe normal-space information to detect missing capacity.

entry.title: Editing Large Language Models with Geometry-Aware Regularization

author.name: Bingqing Liu, Wei Liu, Jun Wang, Xiaobo Sun, Yuhua Li, Ruixuan Li

entry.summary: Proposes GEdit, a geometry-aware knowledge editing framework using a Low-Rank Plus Diagonal factor model of FFN hidden representations to distinguish core knowledge worth preserving from easy versus hard edits. It combines low-rank regularization protecting a core subspace with difficulty-aware edit handling to reduce collateral damage.

entry.title: Before You Continue: Evaluating Time-Sensitive Safety Awareness in Conversational Assistants

author.name: Peidi Dong, Yunze Xiao, Yu-Lin Tsai, Yichen Zheng, Heyuan Huang, Weihao Xuan, Mark Dredze, Jen-tse Huang

entry.summary: TASC is a benchmark of 3,418 inputs from 128 templates, plus 33 comparison scenarios, evaluating whether LLM assistants apply time-dependent constraints (e.g., expired medication, operating hours) when users omit them in later requests. Across 13 models, it separates models' ability to compute elapsed time from their ability to act on that information.

entry.title: Who Pays for the Knowledge Models Copy? Model Collapse as Rogers' Paradox

author.name: Nam H. Le

entry.summary: This theoretical paper reinterprets model collapse through Rogers' paradox from cultural evolution: a population relying on copying gains no benefit unless some members keep learning independently, since copied knowledge goes stale. Fitting Rogers' model to synthetic training predicts model collapse within a few percentage points across a three-step test. It matters by importing a mature evolutionary theory to explain why external data supply, not just copying, determines degradation.

entry.title: Householder Motion Embedding: Noise Modulation for Motion-Controllable Video Generation

author.name: Tao Jun Lin, Jinhong Ni, Ruyi Zha, Yifu Wang, Xibin Song, Pan Ji, Hongdong Li

entry.summary: The paper proposes encoding user-provided motion into video diffusion noise via Householder reflections forming an orthogonal per-location channel transformation. Unlike standard warping, this exactly preserves the Gaussian noise structure, eliminating costly Jacobian-based distribution correction. This offers an efficient route to motion-controllable video generation.

entry.title: Generator-Aligned Reward Modeling with Target-Aware Bounded Optimization for Visual Generation

author.name: Ziqiao Weng, Yuanzhi Liang, Haibing Huang, Weidong Cai, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: The paper proposes GARM plus TABO: reward modeling that aligns supervision with the generator's output distribution and reduces content confounding via content-matched real contrasts, combined with bounded optimization to prevent reward overoptimization during post-training of visual generators. It addresses two chronic failure modes of reward-guided post-training. Co-author Xuelong Li adds credibility.

entry.title: IDPrior: Decoupling Identity Generation from Facial Image Synthesis

author.name: Fadi Boutros, Meri\c{c} Demir\"ors, Darian Toma\v{s}evi\'c, Vitomir \v{S}truc, Naser Damer

entry.summary: IDPrior is a two-stage framework for synthetic face data generation that first learns a diffusion prior in the embedding space of a pretrained face recognition model to sample novel identity embeddings, then conditions image synthesis on them. This explicitly models the distribution of facial identities, unlike label-derived or unconditional approaches, and addresses privacy and cost issues of large identity-labeled face datasets. It aims to improve training data for face recognition models.

entry.title: Spatiotemporal Dynamics-Aware Industrial Anomaly Detection and Reasoning

author.name: S-Wei Chen, Siangyu Yang, Yi-Chen Jan, Chun-Yi Lee, Shao-Yuan Lo

entry.summary: Introduces MUSTARD, a framework that gives multimodal LLMs fine-grained spatiotemporal awareness for detecting dynamic industrial anomalies such as irregular movements that static-image methods miss. It addresses the limited temporal modeling of current MLLM-based anomaly detection approaches in manufacturing quality control.

entry.title: Reinforcing End-to-End Autonomous Driving Safety via Negative-Aware Planning in a Unified World-Action Model

author.name: Zihao Zhang, Xinyu Zhang, Bing Zeng, Xingyu Chen, Zhenning Li, Bin Yu, Ziyuan Pu

entry.summary: NegWAM is a safety post-training framework for world-action models in autonomous driving that learns from near-expert failure trajectories: it constructs negative trajectories geometrically close to expert behavior but carrying safety risk, and uses them as repulsive anchors to steer predictions away from dangerous actions. This addresses the limitation that imitation learning under-constrains unsafe alternatives near expert trajectories.

entry.title: A Unified Fractal Impedance Control Framework

author.name: Adnan Takriti, Mahmoud Sadeq, Quentin Rouxel, Daniele Cafolla, Michael Mistry, Carlo Tiseo

entry.summary: This paper presents the robotic implementation and experimental validation of the Harmonic-Passive Motion Paradigm built on the Fractal Impedance Controller, which guarantees bounded, safe physical interaction by design. It also releases an open-source deployment framework integrating ROS2, MuJoCo, and physical hardware, validated on a Kinova Gen3 across tracking and interaction tasks. Intrinsically safe interaction control with open tooling is valuable for pHRI research.

entry.title: Near-Minimax Sample Complexity for Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning under Generative Models

author.name: Yue Wang

entry.summary: This paper establishes the constant-confidence minimax sample complexity for multi-objective RL in finite discounted MDPs with a generative model, where one dataset must support an epsilon-optimal policy for every convex combination of m reward functions. The resulting Theta-tilted bound of SAH^3/eps^2 times min{S, log(em)} matches upper bounds and resolves how the number of objectives enters the complexity.

entry.title: Efficient Lempel-Ziv Prediction with the Run-Length BWT

author.name: OhadA

entry.summary: The author presents new published work from the PIBBSS 2026 fellowship under Vanessa Kosoy's mentorship, using run-length Burrows-Wheeler transform techniques to reduce the runtime of Kosoy's polynomial-time algorithm for predicting repetitive sequences. The post informally explains the ideas and situates the work in the tradeoff between predictor power, efficiency, and formal guarantees.

entry.title: Adapting the Process of Adaptation: Darwinian, Lamarckian, and Agent-Directed Evolution in AI

author.name: Andrew W. Lo, Chaoyi Zhao

entry.summary: The authors build a theoretical framework comparing Darwinian, Lamarckian, and agent-directed evolution in AI agents that can modify and evaluate their own behavior after environmental change. They show these mechanisms differ progressively in improvement speed and derive safety-relevant conditions on how self-directed improvement scales with learning effectiveness.

entry.title: Adaptive Semantic Branching: Disagreement-Localized Cross-Trajectory Regeneration for Reasoning Candidate Expansion

author.name: Jeong-Yoon Kim, Tae-Yoon Lee

entry.summary: ASB is a training-free inference procedure that exploits disagreements between independently sampled reasoning trajectories: it groups trajectories by final answer, aligns reasoning steps with a monotonic dynamic program, identifies persistent divergence points, and regenerates targeted candidates from those points. This converts cross-trajectory conflict into efficient candidate expansion for reasoning. It aims to improve inference-time compute efficiency without training.

entry.title: More Agents, More Reliable? System-Level Reliability of Multi-Agent LLMs under Operational-Profile Uncertainty

author.name: Burkay Tun\c{c}t\"urk, Koorosh Aslansefat, Yiannis Papadopoulos, Bao Nguyen

entry.summary: Proposes a framework combining hierarchical imprecise-probability assessment of individual LLMs with a Bayesian network of system failure logic to produce reliability envelopes for multi-agent LLM systems under operational-profile uncertainty. A chemical-hazard extraction case study shows majority voting over three models can produce safety-critical degradation, challenging the assumption that more agents means more reliability.

entry.title: Permanent and Transient Representations for Continual Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Nishanth Anand, Doina Precup

entry.summary: The paper extends complementary learning systems for continual RL by using different representation types for each system: parametric representations for slow long-term learning and non-parametric representations for fast transient adaptation. Anand and Precup provide both theoretical and empirical support for this asymmetry, building on their earlier permanent/transient value function work. It addresses the stability-plasticity trade-off in continual RL.

entry.title: IMUDINO: Self-distilled Foundation Model for Inertial Sensing

author.name: Zhoutong Ye, Chengwen Zhang, Zixuan Wang, Xufeng Jian, Zhe He, Qingyang Wan, Xutong Wang, Jiaqi Liu, Mingze Sun, Yu Mei, Chun Yu, Yuanchun Shi

entry.summary: IMUDINO is presented as the first foundation model for inertial sensing to achieve competitive performance across diverse tasks including human activity recognition, health monitoring, motion capture, and odometry. It adapts the DINO self-supervised paradigm to IMU data using semantics-preserving motion augmentations, and handles variable input lengths, sampling rates, and unseen sensor locations better than prior narrow inertial models. This narrows the gap between inertial sensing and vision/language foundation models.

entry.title: GraspBench: Execution-Aware Cross-Robot Evaluation of 6-DoF Grasp Generation in MuJoCo

author.name: Abdul Basit, Bibek Poudel, Muhammad Shafique

entry.summary: GraspBench is a controlled MuJoCo protocol that evaluates full grasp-generation pipelines end-to-end after robot-specific inverse-kinematics filtering, motion planning, and execution, rather than scoring grasp proposals in isolation. It covers six pipelines, four robot embodiments, and 3,240 method-scenario evaluations with conservative failure accounting.

entry.title: THG-Omni: Traceable Human-Centric Graph Supervision for Video Reasoning

author.name: Jisheng Dang, Kai Wei, Ronghao Lin, Bimei Wang, Hong Peng, Wei-Shi Zheng, Bin Hu, Qi Tian, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: THG-Omni constructs traceable human-centric graph supervision for omni-modal video reasoning by linking SAM 3 participant tracks with temporally grounded Qwen3-VL annotations, verifying candidate claims against source video and audio before use. This teaches models to cite which participant, event, and interval supports an answer, addressing the traceability gap in video question answering. It matters for trustworthy multimodal reasoning with structured evidence supervision.

entry.title: Machine Learning for Live-Birth Prediction After IVF/ICSI From Structured Clinical Data: A Systematic Review, Meta-Analysis, and Critical Appraisal

author.name: Abdul Raheem Shahzad, Muhammad Zaheer Khan, Umar Ajaib, Asad Ur Rehman, Juan Deng, Ming Zhang

entry.summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 48 studies using machine learning to predict live birth after IVF/ICSI from structured clinical data, appraised with PRISMA 2020, PROBAST+AI, and TRIPOD+AI standards. The authors pool discrimination metrics and define standardized semantics for model outputs, decision points, and validation designs. It exposes wide performance variability and likely methodological weaknesses in this clinical ML literature.

entry.title: Loopback Transformer: Towards a Unified View of Residual Looped Transformers

author.name: Xuan Ouyang, Zefan Cai, Chenlong Zhang, Cheng Luo, Ke Wan, Junjie Hu

entry.summary: The Loopback Transformer analyzes residual looped transformers through a depth-memory lens, separating how repeated computation results are stored and re-read. By keeping the shared stack's input on a separate path and reading individual updates with geometric decay, it gains independent control over input strength, total update weight, and allocation across updates. This offers both a conceptual unification and a parameter-efficient architecture variant.

entry.title: AtlasULP: Domain-aware Universal Link Prediction via Relation Atlas

author.name: Yujing Liu, Yixin Liu, Yu Zheng, Lianhua Chi, Alan Wee-Chung Liew, Heng Tao Shen, Shirui Pan

entry.summary: AtlasULP addresses universal link prediction, enabling training-free inference on unseen graphs, by replacing subgraph sampling with a relation atlas that captures higher-order structural information without exponential neighborhood growth. This improves performance on graphs where long-range signals matter, such as biological networks. It reduces the cost of per-graph model training at scale.

entry.title: EnergyBench: a live, gate-aligned benchmark of day-ahead forecasts for European power markets

author.name: Evgenii Genov, Ander Martinez Alonso, Christoph Bergmeir

entry.summary: EnergyBench evaluates day-ahead energy forecasting models live rather than on backtests: each day at 11:30 CET, thirty minutes before the day-ahead market gate closes, participating models forecast next-day price, wind, solar, and load across six European bidding zones on a 15-minute grid. Unlike existing live benchmarks, it runs the models itself on a frozen, published information set, eliminating look-ahead leakage and benchmark overfitting. This addresses fundamental flaws in how energy forecasting is usually compared.

entry.title: A Proxy-Based Method for Measuring Racial Disparities in~Text-to-Image~Generators

author.name: Nia Mucher, Ngan Pham, Jason Chin, Aaron Brown, David Evans

entry.summary: The paper presents an automated auditing method for representational bias in text-to-image generators, adapting racial proxy variables from U.S. antidiscrimination law to compare generated-image demographics against ground-truth benchmarks. It additionally measures skin tone via CIELAB values and image-group similarity to capture quality and homogeneity biases beyond demographic counts.

entry.title: TACT-KV: Tri-Axis Cosine Transform for Compressing Volumetric KV Caches in Medical VLMs

author.name: Chongyu Qu, Ritchie Zhao, Yufan He, Dong Yang, Zhengyi Lu, Junchao Zhu, Tianyuan Yao, Juming Xiong, Junlin Guo, Yanfan Zhu, Yuechen Yang, Daguang Xu, Bennett Allan Landman, Yucheng Tang, Yuankai Huo

entry.summary: TACT-KV is a calibration-free KV cache compression method for vision-language models processing 3D medical scans, exploiting spatial correlations along all three anatomical axes via a separable 3D discrete cosine transform in the frequency domain. This targets the memory wall caused by tens of thousands of vision tokens per CT or MRI volume.

entry.title: Unifying Central Flow, Rod Flow, and the Edge Coupling

author.name: Eric Regis, Sinho Chewi

entry.summary: This theory paper unifies continuous-time models of gradient descent at the edge of stability, showing that central flow and rod flow can both be derived from a common object called the edge coupling, a functional on consecutive iterates whose critical points capture fixed points and period-two orbits. This clarifies how oscillatory training dynamics, which gradient flow cannot capture, should be modeled. It matters for the theoretical understanding of why deep networks train stably despite sharp curvature.

entry.title: Adapting Qwen3 to Tajik from 0.6B to 8B: Lower Text Loss Did Not Mean Better Understanding

author.name: Tohir Saidzoda, Madina Abdusalomzoda, Nasimjon Rajabov, Akhrorkhon Ikromov, Komron Giyosiev, Abubakr Abdullozoda, Amin Jalilov, Jonibek Kishvarov, Rahmonali Sharipov, Mariyamkhon Shodyeva

entry.summary: A systematic study adapting Qwen3 models (0.6B to 8B) to Tajik with LoRA adapters, showing reduced Tajik text loss did not improve reading comprehension on Belebele, while continued pretraining plus supervised fine-tuning yielded an 11.4-point gain. It demonstrates that loss reduction from cheap adapters is a misleading proxy for capability.

entry.title: Zuse: A Decision Model for European Languages

author.name: Umair Mehmood Imam

entry.summary: Describes Zuse, three decision models (4B, 9B, 27B) that attach a low-rank adapter and pointer head to frozen open-weight bases to output probabilities over fixed options instead of generating text, targeting 27 European languages. The 27B model reaches 87.5% accuracy with very low calibration error on an 11-source, 9-task European suite.

entry.title: Replicability, Reproducibility, and Robustness in Political and Social Science Research with Large Language Models

author.name: Joan C. Timoneda, Sebasti\'an Vallejo Vera

entry.summary: This chapter tackles the reproducibility crisis in social science research using LLMs, distinguishing replicability, reproducibility, and robustness and proposing a probabilistic standard based on distributions of results rather than identical outputs. It introduces a standardized prompt script and error-structure analysis, showing that measurement choice can reverse the sign of downstream regression coefficients.

entry.title: PAYWORTHY: Can LLMs Predict Which Freelance Jobs an AI Agent Will Complete?

author.name: Mohammad Reza Rezaei, Dingxian Wang, Brett Levert, Celeste Fejzo, Andrew Rabinovich, Zhao Chen

entry.summary: PAYWORTHY is a benchmark of 1,494 real freelance job postings on which an AI agent attempts work and an LLM judge acting as client accepts or rejects it, with 18 forecasting models predicting success. Forecasting quality is measured by AUC and depends strongly on how the agent is described. The benchmark addresses a novel and economically relevant question: whether frontier LLMs can estimate agent task success before an attempt.

entry.title: CoGenRec: A Unified Generative Framework for Complementary Vision Reconstruction

author.name: Yapeng Meng, Yuguo Chen, Xiangru Chen, Shaojun Xu, Xuezhen Wang, Lijian Wang, Zheyu Yang, Yihan Lin, Luping Shi, Rong Zhao

entry.summary: CoGenRec addresses the Complementary Vision Sensor (CVS), a hardware design that splits capture between a dense long-exposure RGB pathway and a temporally dense short-exposure spatiotemporal difference pathway, to overcome frame camera trade-offs in motion blur, dynamic range, and SNR. The paper proposes a unified generative reconstruction framework that fuses the two complementary measurements into high-quality video. This is notable as co-design of sensing hardware and neural reconstruction.

entry.title: ProQuant: Progressive Quantization-aware Training for Edge MLLMs

author.name: Yufei Xue, Yushi Huang, Jiawei Shao, Pingcheng Dong, Yonghao Tan, Shiyao Li, Kwang-Ting Cheng, Jun Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes ProQuant, a weight-activation quantization-aware training method for multimodal LLMs that addresses severe degradation of post-training quantization at low bit-widths like W4A8, especially for small edge-suitable models. It enables real-world deployment of MLLMs on resource-constrained devices.

entry.title: T3R: Training-Free Two-Stage Token Refinement Towards Efficient and Robust VLA Models

author.name: Mohammed Hassan (Celine), Zhenyang Chen (Celine), Zheng Wang (Celine), Zhixin Zhu (Celine), Tianlong Chen (Celine), Yingyan (Celine), Lin, Chaojian Li

entry.summary: T3R is a training-free framework that reduces Vision-Language-Action model inference cost by first pruning spatially irrelevant visual tokens via segmentation and then reallocating attention among remaining tokens. This tackles both compute cost and distraction from background content under distribution shift, addressing two forms of redundancy in VLA visual processing.

entry.title: Not Losing Your Way: Mitigating Visual-Inertial Odometry Drift through On-Demand Visual Feature Creation

author.name: Simone D'Angelo, Gianmarco Corrado, Federico Esposito, Vincenzo Scognamiglio, Fabio Ruggiero

entry.summary: Inspired by Tom Thumb, this work proposes a UAV framework that actively modifies the environment to fight VIO drift in poorly textured scenes by releasing ground markers or marking walls on demand, triggered by an information-based indicator with temporal confirmation and hysteresis. Evaluation spans three simulated environments and a 900-run factorial campaign. Actively creating features rather than passively seeking them is a fresh angle on the localization problem.

entry.title: H-TRIP: Exact Many-to-Many Distance Index for Multi-Robot Exploration

author.name: Elif A. \"Ozaslan, Tolga \"Ozaslan

entry.summary: H-TRIP provides an exact many-to-many geodesic distance index for frontier-based multi-robot exploration, addressing stale cache entries when newly discovered free space creates global shortcuts. Grounded in Kleene algebra over the min-plus semiring, it maintains a spatial hierarchy with incremental propagation over monotonically growing occupancy grids.

entry.title: Balance-Guided Forest for Causal Effect Estimation

author.name: Feiyang Yi, Jelena Bradic

entry.summary: The paper proposes Balance-Guided Forest (BGF), which closes the loop between tree learning and covariate balancing by using current balancing weights to guide subsequent tree splits via a score combining residual imbalance with outcome contrast. This avoids wasting tree capacity on already well-balanced features, improving causal effect estimation from observational data.

entry.title: J-lens preferentially reads from coordinate-aligned subspaces

author.name: Caleb Briggs

entry.summary: A short interpretability follow-up showing that in Gemma-4-31B, two small coordinate-aligned subspaces account for 80-95% of the J-lens readout, identifiable by a distinctive small post-norm diagonal weight pattern that protects the coordinates from edits across layers. The author also notes that semantically valuable information exists outside these spaces, complicating a clean isolated workspace story.

entry.title: Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning via Epigraph-Form Guided Exploration

author.name: Sungil Son, Hoseong Jung, Dahyun Oh, H. Jin Kim

entry.summary: EFXPLORER is a constrained exploration framework for cooperative MARL that maximizes intrinsic exploration objectives subject to preserving established task performance, solved via an epigraph reformulation with adaptive exploration budgets. This separates intrinsic rewards from task objectives, avoiding the signal distortion of naive reward combination.

entry.title: Towards Generalist Graph-Level Anomaly Detection

author.name: Junjun Pan, Yixin Liu, Yu Zheng, Fuyi Li, Alan Wee-Chung Liew, Shirui Pan

entry.summary: This work formalizes generalist graph-level anomaly detection: a single unified model that detects anomalous graphs across multiple domains with minimal target supervision, departing from dataset-specific training paradigms. The paper identifies the key challenges of cross-domain generalization for GLAD and presumably proposes a corresponding approach. It pushes anomaly detection toward the foundation-model-style generality seen in other areas.

entry.title: BabyTheorist: A Benchmark for Learning to Theorize the World from Observation Alone

author.name: Doojin Baek, Junyeob Baek, Mingyu Jo, Hosung Lee, Taegu Kang, Gyubin Lee, Sungjin Ahn

entry.summary: BabyTheorist is a benchmark for observational theory learning: acquiring reusable theories from pure before-after visual observation streams without program labels or support sets, then applying them to new situations. It generates continual observation streams from hidden compositional programs, enabling controlled training and evaluation. The benchmark targets whether machines can truly build world theories rather than solve few-shot rule puzzles.

entry.title: NPCBench: A Clinical Apprenticeship Benchmark for Multimodal Care-Pathway Reasoning in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma

author.name: Pengkai Wang, Wei-Wei Zhang, Yan Li, Min Tang, Zhitian Hou, Zeyu Liu, Guanghao Zhu, Yuanyi Wang, Yanggan Gu, Wenjun Wang, Minheng Ni, Congkai Xie, Zhijie Sang, Jianmin Wu, Ying Sun, Hongxia Yang

entry.summary: NPCBench is a new medical benchmark evaluating whether multimodal models can perform longitudinal care-pathway reasoning for nasopharyngeal carcinoma, mimicking the full arc of specialist training rather than isolated question answering. It includes 4,777 component and consultation items plus a 100-patient CarePath cohort with 417 scored diagnostic and care decisions.

entry.title: ReproBridge: Building Reproducibility into ML Research Artifacts

author.name: Yubo Wang, Rui Meng, Jaehyun Nam, Tomas Pfister, Jinsung Yoon

entry.summary: ReproBridge defines a standardized artifact design (refined codebase, environment setup, launchers, reproduction guide) and an agent workflow for constructing reproducible ML research artifacts. ReproBridge-Bench provides 1,029 tasks from 387 experiments across 36 papers to evaluate whether coding agents can independently reproduce experiments. The work targets whether reproduction success depends on artifact quality versus agent improvisation.

entry.title: Oscillatory Phase Coding Emerges in Adaptive RNNs for Flexible Working Memory

author.name: Kehan Lu, Tianhao Chu, Aiersi Tuerhong, Yiwen Sun, Huan Luo, Fang Fang, Si Wu

entry.summary: Trains RNNs with neural adaptation on sequence working-memory tasks with variable delays and finds oscillatory phase coding emerges spontaneously: oscillation amplitude encodes item identity while phase encodes serial order. Ablations identify adaptation dynamics, variable delay, and flexible readout as the minimal ingredients, connecting recurrent network models to a known biological phenomenon.

entry.title: TileQuant: Tile as the Precision-Allocation Unit for LLM Mixed-Precision Post-Training Quantization

author.name: Hanzhi Zhang, Qiao Zhang, Qinglei Cao, Heng Fan, Yan Huang, Kewei Sha, Yunhe Feng

entry.summary: Introduces TileQuant, a training-free mixed-precision post-training quantization framework that allocates precision at the level of hardware-aligned 2D weight tiles rather than whole columns, using offline input-activation-aware scoring from forward statistics. This addresses sensitivity variation within columns and avoids the decoding overhead of runtime outlier detection, reducing LLM deployment costs.

entry.title: Archetypal contexts in the neurons of language models: an architecture for intelligence?

author.name: David Nordfors

entry.summary: This paper validates a prior hypothesis that language models store domain-independent relational patterns, called archetypal contexts (e.g., tipping point, winner-takes-all), separately from topic and language. Using Qwen3.8-27B, the authors show disentangled neuron sets encode archetype, topic, and language respectively, and silencing each set selectively removes that component of model behavior. This offers evidence for compositional, human-recognizable abstractions inside LLM internals.

entry.title: Adaptive Experimentation Can Hide Model Error:Detection Limits and Falsification Budget

author.name: Ramnarayan Choudhary

entry.summary: This theory paper shows that adaptive experimental design can systematically avoid regions where a working model fails, making model misspecification invisible to adequacy tests. The authors bound the power of any valid adequacy test in terms of the experimenter's sampling distribution and propose a training-free rule that reserves part of the design budget specifically for falsification, plus a computable diagnostic for unresolved model error.

entry.title: CAMP: Context-Aware Mapping and Placement for LLMs on 3D-IMC Arrays

author.name: Orhun G\"orkem, Athanasios Vasilopoulos, Georgios Pagonis, Victoria Clerico, Hadjer Benmeziane, Irem Boybat, Hsinyu Tsai, Abu Sebastian, William Andrew Simon

entry.summary: CAMP tackles weight mapping on 3D analog in-memory computing arrays for LLM inference, where vertical stacking increases capacity but placement determines which matrix-vector multiplications can run concurrently. The paper develops context-aware mapping and placement strategies to improve utilization, latency, and throughput, addressing KV cache and weight-loading overheads.

entry.title: O$^2$PD: Overlap-Gated On-Policy Distillation on Reliable Prefix

author.name: Shuaishuai Zu, Jihao Zhao, Pengfei Li, Guanghuan Fang, Ben Feng, Yuhan Liu, Biao Qin, Baochuan Yang

entry.summary: This paper addresses two gaps in on-policy distillation of language models: which student-generated tokens the teacher should supervise, and how to compute the alignment divergence. It proposes an overlap-gated scheme that distills only on reliable prefixes and reconsidered top-k reverse KL support, improving on standard on-policy distillation setups. The work matters because distillation from stronger to weaker models is a core efficiency technique for deploying capable small models.

entry.title: Value or Attention: Investigating Layer-wise Relevance Propagation for Graph Attention Networks

author.name: Ken Schreiber, Ren\'e P. Klausen, Sebastian Lapuschkin, Wojciech Samek, Jonas Naujoks

entry.summary: This paper develops a unified LRP-based explanation method for Graph Attention Networks that explicitly separates content relevance flowing through the value path from routing relevance through the attention path. The authors present a single product rule with free weights that recovers prior approaches as special cases, addressing why existing explainers mishandle attention layers.

entry.title: Uncertainty calibration in Bayesian M/EEG source imaging

author.name: Ismail Huseynov, Mohammad Orabe, Srikantan Nagarajan, Stefan Haufe

entry.summary: This paper introduces a simulation-based framework for assessing whether uncertainty estimates in Bayesian M/EEG source imaging methods are empirically well calibrated. It compares Bayesian minimum norm (BMN) with sparse Bayesian learning using sparse basis field expansions (S-FLEX), deriving joint source- and noise-variance updates and showing S-FLEX avoids degenerate zero variances at voxel level. Reliable calibrated uncertainty matters for clinical neuroscience applications of brain source localization.

entry.title: Graph Neural Networks for Resource Allocation in Integrated Sensing and Communication

author.name: Junyu Liao, Lili Chen, Tian Han, Jamie Evans

entry.summary: This paper proposes GNN-ISAC, a graph neural network that solves nonconvex power allocation in vehicular integrated sensing and communication networks by modeling inter-provider interference and intra-provider power sharing as distinct edge types. The learned amortizer replaces costly per-layout iterative optimization, maximizing communication sum-rate under sensing SINR constraints. It matters because ISAC is a key enabler of next-generation wireless systems.

entry.title: Monotone Viability Learning for Offline Safe Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Ziqian Wang, Zhen Zhang

entry.summary: MoViL learns viable (safe) sets from offline data via monotone finite-horizon Hamilton-Jacobi set recursion that preserves safety semantics and converges to the infinite-horizon viability kernel, with binary supervision avoiding discount-induced numerical attenuation. It establishes conditions for recovering behavior-supported viable subsets. This strengthens the foundations of offline safe RL.

entry.title: $O(1/n)$ Convergence Rate for RVI $Q$-Learning

author.name: Avik Kar, Siddharth Chandak, Rahul Singh, Shalabh Bhatnagar

entry.summary: This paper establishes finite-time convergence guarantees for synchronous relative value iteration Q-learning on finite weakly communicating MDPs. Using stochastic Krasnoselskii-Mann iteration analysis under martingale-difference noise, the authors derive last-iterate mean-squared residual bounds and show polynomial stepsizes yield an O(n^-1) convergence rate. This provides some of the tightest known finite-time guarantees for average-reward Q-learning.

entry.title: Gabor Gabor: E-Gaborformer, a Strictly Causal Speech Recognizer with Gabor-Dictionary Convolutions and Delta-Rule Memory

author.name: Nir Krakowski, Tamir Cohen, Ohad Zohar, Chen Zarfati

entry.summary: E-Gaborformer is a strictly causal streaming speech recognizer combining Gated DeltaNet-2 recurrent layers with sliding-window attention in a 3:1 ratio, using convolutions built from a fixed dictionary of causal Gabor atoms. Its streaming state is constant at roughly 19 MB per call versus over 1 GB for causal-attention encoders after ten minutes, and it reaches target accuracy up to 18 percent sooner on LibriSpeech. This is relevant to real-time voice agents with long-duration calls.

entry.title: Do sEMG Foundation Models Improve Cross-Subject Generalisation?

author.name: William Raftery, Dario Farina

entry.summary: This paper systematically evaluates three surface electromyography (sEMG) foundation models across three gesture classification datasets, comparing intra-session and inter-subject data splits with three fine-tuning strategies to isolate the effect of pretraining. The key finding is that pretraining gains largely evaporate under cross-subject conditions, exposing that current sEMG foundation models overfit to individual recording sessions rather than learning truly generalizable representations. This matters for wearable robotics, prosthetics, and HCI applications where models must generalize to new users without per-user recalibration.

entry.title: Interpretable many-body interaction laws for collective motion from few trajectories

author.name: Timon S. Gutleb

entry.summary: The paper introduces dACE, an adaptation of the atomic cluster expansion to self-propelled agents, providing an exactly equivariant, systematically improvable expansion of an agent's acceleration that uniquely splits into one-, two-, three-body and higher interaction contributions. On simulated collectives with known rules, dACE recovers interaction laws body order by body order from little data, outperforming the neural baseline Social-Implicit in interpretability. This enables scientific discovery of many-body collective behavior.

entry.title: Data-driven discovery of intrinsic Lie point symmetries of differential equation systems

author.name: Ilker Gurcan, Kadir Ustun, Ramazan Gokberk Cinbis

entry.summary: The authors formulate intrinsic Lie point-symmetry discovery from differential-equation data as an operator-theoretic problem on sampled jet-space data, identifying admissible generators and separating them from redundant and geometrically trivial directions. The framework combines prolongation, sequential subspace restrictions, and a fixed nonlinear dictionary, with a rank-stabilization preflight test diagnosing degenerate systems. It enables model reduction and scientific ML without closed-form governing equations.

entry.title: Adversarial Training with Large Step Sizes: Implicit Bias, Optimization, and Sharpness

author.name: Yi Feng, Andrea Paudice

entry.summary: This theoretical work analyzes gradient descent dynamics in adversarial training with large constant step sizes, unlike most prior analyses that assume vanishing steps. It establishes results on implicit bias and loss convergence for adversarial linear logistic regression and characterizes loss sharpness evolution during neural network adversarial training.

entry.title: FastAFD: When Does Attention-FFN Disaggregation Pay on Rack-Scale NVLink?

author.name: Yichao Fu, Yuxuan Zhang, Minshen Zhang, Ruitian Wang, Junda Chen, Hao Zhang

entry.summary: This paper builds FastAFD, an engine for attention-FFN disaggregation (AFD) of MoE models on GB200 NVL72 rack-scale NVLink hardware, overlapping the MoE computation of one microbatch with the attention of another. It rigorously tests whether the previously reported decode-throughput benefits of AFD hold against strong wide expert-parallel vLLM baselines, finding only a modest advantage of up to 1.17x. The work matters because it gives system builders clear empirical guidance on when disaggregated serving architectures are actually worth the added complexity on modern rack-scale clusters.

entry.title: Asymptotic-Preserving Tensor Neural Networks for 3D High-Field Kinetic Equations with Applications to Uncertainty Quantification

author.name: Shi Jin, Tian-ai Zhang

entry.summary: The authors propose an asymptotic-preserving tensor neural network method for high-dimensional, multiscale kinetic equations such as Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck in the high-field regime, using CP decomposition of tensor neural networks to cut cost and memory. The approach retains asymptotic limits across scales and extends to uncertainty quantification for plasma and semiconductor simulation.

entry.title: Statistical and Privacy Guarantees for Deep M-Regression via Stochastic Gradient Langevin Dynamics

author.name: Yeheng Ge, Jian Huang, Shuyuan Wu

entry.summary: The authors provide PAC-Bayesian excess-risk bounds for deep nonparametric regression trained with stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics, jointly accounting for approximation error, statistical complexity, and algorithmic noise along the SGLD trajectory. The analysis shows the estimator retains minimax-optimal regression rates while the injected Gaussian noise yields privacy guarantees.

entry.title: Series-wise Cross-validation for Global Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Vitor Cerqueira, Mariana Oliveira, Luis Roque

entry.summary: This paper formalizes series-wise cross-validation for global deep learning forecasting models, which can partition data across both time and series rather than only temporally. The authors benchmark K-fold, bootstrapping, and Monte Carlo CV variants on 11 datasets with 10 neural architectures, evaluating performance estimation, overoptimism, and model selection accuracy. This matters because CV methodology directly affects model evaluation and selection in forecasting practice.

entry.title: CARTBench: Rubric-Based Evaluation of Shopping Advice for Complex and Ambiguous Requests with Timelines

author.name: Yuqin Dai, Zhanwei Zhang, Honghui Yang, Zhouheng Yao, Yueqi Zhang, Jingyu He, Chaoyang Shi, Fanding Wei, Boyuan Pan, Kai Xu, Yao Hu, Yongliang Shen

entry.summary: Introduces CARTBench, a benchmark for evaluating LLM shopping assistants on complex, ambiguous, time-constrained requests, built from real commercial dialogues across 17 retail domains with 1,603 product records. It proposes case-specific rubrics distilled from successfully completed orders and a Principle-Guided CART Prompting strategy for structured recommendations.

entry.title: LibriSpeech-Real-QA: A Benchmark for Streaming Question Answering

author.name: Zewen Zhan, Hui Lu, Xueyuan Chen, Huimeng Wang, Yikai Huang, Xixin Wu, Shiyin Kang, Bin Xia, Zhiyong Wu

entry.summary: This paper introduces LibriSpeech-Real-QA, a dataset and benchmark for real-time streaming speech interaction, where models must answer questions using only the audio chunks received so far rather than complete utterances. It fills a gap since most speech LLMs operate offline, and real applications require continuous streaming responses.

entry.title: SAUCE: Summary Analysis Using Conversation Entailment

author.name: Man-Ling Sung, Hemanth Kandula, Jeff Ma, William Hartmann, Matthew Snover

entry.summary: This paper introduces SAUCE, a reference-free evaluation pipeline for cross-lingual conversational speech summarization that measures summary accuracy and fact coverage via entailment between the conversation and the summary text. It captures information loss from transcription and translation errors and offers explainability, unlike black-box LLM judges or embedding-based metrics. This matters because evaluating open-ended conversational summaries remains a persistent weakness in LLM and speech application assessment.

entry.title: AGORA: Reliability-Aware Aggregation of LLM Judges via Item-Response Theory

author.name: Junhyung Ahn

entry.summary: AGORA is an item-response-theory aggregator for LLM-as-a-judge pools that places items on a latent quality scale and models each judge with a sensitivity parameter and ordered rating thresholds, learning reliability from all data. It targets the small-validation-set regime where per-item means over-weight weak judges and Dawid-Skene error tables are underdetermined.

entry.title: SVGFaith: A Two-Layer Meta-Evaluation of Faithfulness Metrics for Text-to-SVG Generation

author.name: Guotao Liang, Haitao Zhou, Biao Liu, Huanxuan Liao, Lingfeng Qiao, Qian-Wen Zhang, Qian Yu, Di Yin, Xing Sun

entry.summary: SVGFaith is a meta-evaluation framework showing that raster-image metrics applied to rasterized SVG outputs poorly capture prompt faithfulness. It includes 1,842 controlled contrastive pairs across eight capability axes and 1,327 human-annotated comparisons of real generator outputs, with faithfulness determined by construction or human judgment. The finding that CLIP-like embedding metrics score near chance is a significant caution for how text-to-SVG systems are evaluated.

entry.title: T$^2$-Splat: Adaptive Topology Mesh Splatting with Texture Residuals

author.name: Zhihao Tang, Youjia Zhang, Mingbo Zhao, Wei Yang

entry.summary: T2-Splat is a mesh-based splatting method for novel view synthesis that decouples topology adaptation from appearance refinement: Safe Restricted Delaunay Triangulation initializes connectivity, Dynamic Topology Evolution adapts triangles via edge collapse and vertex split, and per-face Mip-texture residuals refine appearance. It improves PSNR by 0.71dB over MeshSplatting on Mip-NeRF 360 with compact meshes across three standard datasets. It bridges neural rendering with conventional graphics pipelines.

entry.title: Wide View Synthesis from Overlapping Perspective Cameras in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Kaixuan Zhang, Zhipeng Xiong, Minxian Li, Mingwu Ren, Xiatian Zhu

entry.summary: The paper formulates wide view synthesis (WVS), generating a geometrically consistent wide view from multiple spatially separated automotive cameras, handling depth-dependent parallax and occlusions that defeat simple stitching. It adapts 3D Gaussian Splatting to avoid per-scene optimization for driving scenes. This is practically relevant for surround perception in autonomous vehicles.

entry.title: OptIMerge: Optimization-Based Merging of Diffusion Models

author.name: Viraj Shah, Ashwini Pokle, Peyman Milanfar, Mauricio Delbracio, Hossein Talebi

entry.summary: OptIMerge studies merging image-to-image diffusion models fine-tuned for dense restoration tasks, where naive model souping causes destructive parameter interference. It proposes an optimization-based merging method for this underexplored setting. Google-affiliated authors (Milanfar, Delbracio, Talebi) lend credibility.

entry.title: Deformable Contact-Aware 3D Object Placement

author.name: Songhe Wang, David Miller, Charles A. Kamhoua

entry.summary: Proposes DCAP, which reframes language-guided 3D object placement as a drop-to-equilibrium process instead of predicting a rigid 6-DoF pose. A semantic release state (drop location, scale, deformable components) is fed to a coupled rigid-deformable simulator so objects settle under gravity and friction, avoiding floating or interpenetrating placements. Evaluated on a benchmark of over 2,000 prompt-asset cases.

entry.title: Kinematic Hypothesis Context: Embodiment-Conditioned Learned Video Coding for Bandwidth-Limited Robot Policy Uplinks

author.name: Yuze Lu

entry.summary: This paper introduces a zero-rate conditioning signal built from robot joint states, the robot model, and camera calibration that lets both ends of a remote-policy video link predict ego-motion, dramatically improving learned video codec efficiency. The authors prove that history-only or global-pose conditioning cannot access this information under large motion, and show coding gains translate into task gains for bandwidth-limited robot teleoperation.

entry.title: Real-Time Event-Based LED Tracking and Pose Estimation with PWM-Encoded Markers

author.name: Junkai Niu, Sheng Zhong, Delei Kong, Xin Wang, Kaizhen Sun, Yusen Zhang, Mingzhen Gan, Yi Zhou

entry.summary: The authors present a real-time event-camera framework for LED tracking and 6-DoF relative pose estimation using PWM-encoded markers, where LEDs share a blinking frequency and encode identity via duty cycles. A dual-rate asynchronous tracking scheme reduces frequency-resource and computational demands. This enables robust high-speed pose estimation under motion blur and HDR conditions.

entry.title: H-BRICK: Hierarchical Boundary Reachability Index with Compressed Kleene Closure for Directed Grid Graphs

author.name: Tolga \"Ozaslan, Elif A. \"Ozaslan

entry.summary: H-BRICK is a hierarchical index for answering exact cell-to-cell reachability queries on directed grid graphs, common in online path planning and swarm control where full transitive closure is too large to store. It tiles the graph, computes local Boolean Kleene closures projected onto boundary ports, and composes these summaries recursively, with algebraic proofs of exactness.

entry.title: Exact signal recovery from generative priors with sigmoid output activation

author.name: Matthew S. Scott, Yaniv Plan, \"Ozg\"ur Y{\i}lmaz

entry.summary: The authors prove exact uniform signal recovery in generative compressed sensing for ReLU networks with a final sigmoid activation, removing the common expansivity assumption. They derive sample complexity in terms of network depth and the geometric mean of layer widths, showing recovery with roughly k(d log(K/k)) measurements.

entry.title: Clearing up a robot’s fuzzy memory

author.name: Adam Zewe | MIT News

entry.summary: MIT researchers present UQ-DAAAM, a robot memory system that quantifies uncertainty in object descriptions by comparing multiple viewpoint-dependent captions, actively selecting additional views to reduce uncertainty, and saving corrected descriptions to memory. This addresses mislabeled object memory that could cause robots to fail tasks like retrieving a defibrillator in an emergency.

entry.title: Embedding-Space Fingerprinting of LoRA Fine-Tunes: Recovering the Training-Data Domain from the Model Artifact Alone

author.name: Shivesh Rane

entry.summary: This privacy study asks whether a classifier can recover the training-data domain of a LoRA fine-tune from the artifact alone, using Qwen3.5-0.8B (an existing model) fine-tuned on 18 datasets across five domains with white-box, gray-box, and black-box feature families. A leave-one-dataset-out protocol frozen before evaluation tests generalization to unseen datasets.

entry.title: ChemE-as-Code: An Open-Source Platform for Agentic AI in Chemical Engineering

author.name: Artur M. Schweidtmann

entry.summary: ChemE-as-Code is an open-source environment where LLM-based agents perform chemical engineering work — catalysis, process simulation, plant layout, HAZOP, life cycle assessment — with calculations executed outside the LLM, provenance tracked per value, and automated consistency checks. An illustrative ammonia case has an agent produce a preliminary basic-engineering package including simulation files, P&IDs, HAZOP, and datasheets. It emphasizes verifiable, auditable agentic engineering rather than free-form generation.

entry.title: The Gold Rush in AI4Math, II: What are signatures of AI-assisted Proofs?

author.name: Yuanchuan Guo, Jiashun Jin, Zheng Tracy Ke, Bingcheng Sui

entry.summary: This empirical study asks whether AI involvement in mathematical proofs can be detected separately from AI-assisted writing, building five cohorts totaling 8,281 papers that span varying levels of AI involvement, including matched case-control pairs and manuscripts from OpenAI. The work constructs features capturing proof-level signals and addresses disclosure-incompleteness challenges.

entry.title: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization

author.name: Qile Jiang, George Em Karniadakis

entry.summary: SwarmEvolve speeds up LLM-guided evolutionary search by running hundreds of low-cost agents per round that reason in latent space without decoding text, sharing information via KV caches. Swarms attack problems from different angles, a novelty filter keeps distinct ideas by measuring hidden-state distances, and crossover combines promising candidates. This targets the latency and cost bottlenecks of function-evaluation-style evolutionary LLM search such as FunSearch-style systems.

entry.title: BrainPFN: Amortized Brain-Behaviour Prediction via Prior-Data Fitted Networks

author.name: Carlo Alberto Barbano (MIND), Demian Wassermann (MIND)

entry.summary: Introduces BrainPFN, a Prior-Data Fitted Network for predicting behavioral phenotypes from fMRI functional connectivity, replacing per-cohort kernel ridge regression with an amortized in-context model that transfers across datasets and works with few subjects. The paper notes that existing brain foundation models have not consistently beaten KRR on continuous behavioral scores, which this approach targets directly.

entry.title: ReferClaw: Disambiguating User Intent for Egocentric Assistance

author.name: Hangyu Qin, Junbin Xiao, Angela Yao

entry.summary: ReferClaw formulates egocentric streaming video QA as an interactive process in which the assistant asks cost-aware clarifying questions to resolve ambiguous referents before answering, using three cooperating agents for candidate identification, clarification, and grounded answer generation. This avoids committing to a single plausible but intention-misaligned interpretation.

entry.title: Same Behavior, Different Mechanism: What Finite Experiments Can Certify About Integrated Information

author.name: Linqian Wu, Diaoxuan He

entry.summary: This theory paper asks when mechanism-level quantities - functionals of a system's causal transition law such as integrated information phi - are identifiable and certifiable from finite, noisy interventions, answering exactly for small stochastic networks with known ground truth. It demonstrates that behavior can be silent about mechanism: recurrent and feedforward networks with identical input-output laws can differ in integrated information.

entry.title: Beyond Quadratic Attention: Separable Gaussian Operators for ODE Vision Transformers

author.name: Carlos Boned Riera, David Romero Sanchez, Oriol Ramos Terrades

entry.summary: SSoG replaces dense self-attention in Vision Transformers with a separable sum-of-Gaussians spatial operator, reducing per-layer cost from quadratic to subquadratic in token count. Unlike dot-product attention, the fixed-kernel operator is globally Lipschitz continuous, which guarantees unique solutions for its continuous-depth ODE variant via Picard-Lindelof. It shows competitive results on CIFAR-scale benchmarks and links attention efficiency with neural-ODE well-posedness.

entry.title: English Calibration Erodes Lithuanian in Expert-Pruned Mixture-of-Experts Language Models

author.name: Tomas Rasymas, Povilas Kvedaras

entry.summary: This study tests whether English calibration data transfers to Lithuanian when pruning MoE language models with REAP, finding strong asymmetry: at 25% expert pruning, English comprehension dropped 1.7 points while Lithuanian dropped 21.4 points, whereas Lithuanian calibration preserved Lithuanian without significantly hurting English. The result challenges assumptions that English calibration transfers across languages for MoE compression.

entry.title: Detecting Silent Faults at the Environment-Trainer Boundary in Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zuo Gou, Chenhao Lu

entry.summary: The paper treats the environment-trainer boundary in distributed robot RL as a wire protocol and systematically injects up to 23 fault types across Pendulum, HalfCheetah, Hopper, and Pusher, finding that learning-curve thresholds and seed comparisons catch at most 10-21% of silent faults. Of 728 boundary-fault runs passing both checks, 723 scored within three standard deviations in clean evaluation.

entry.title: When Every Choice Is Correct: A Causal Study of Numerical Preference in Language Models

author.name: Hongnian Huang, Hongliang Liu

entry.summary: Uses numerical choice (where every integer in 1-30 is valid) as a probe of how preference is computed across layers and tokens in language models. Combining perturbation probing, activation edits, and attention-head interventions in a Qwen3-4B case, it traces how an edit's influence propagates to later digit decisions.

entry.title: How Far Can You Steer? Behavior-Capability Frontiers in Contrastive Activation Addition

author.name: Deepanshu Raj

entry.summary: The paper studies activation steering via Contrastive Activation Addition through a behavior-capability frontier, selecting interventions that maximize behavioral change subject to explicit budgets (1-5%) on degradation of unrelated capabilities. Evaluated across four instruction-tuned models and seven behaviors, validation-selected effects generalize strongly. It reframes steering safety as a quantified tradeoff rather than a binary success or failure.

entry.title: TRiST: Topology-Reinforced Swin Transformer for Medical Image Analysis

author.name: Pengfei Gu, Huimin Li, Guangyu Meng, Hao Zheng, Haoteng Tang, Bin Fu, Danny Z. Chen

entry.summary: TRiST integrates persistent homology (H0 and H1) computed at each Swin Transformer stage into feature construction, refinement, and attention for medical image analysis, so topological patterns like connected components and loops inform multiscale representations. Topology-aware medical segmentation can better preserve lesion and organ-boundary structure. From an experienced medical imaging group (Chen lab).

entry.title: OcTreeMamba: Topology-Aware Mamba for 3D Medical Segmentation via Octree Sparsification

author.name: Kaixiang Mai, Jiaqi Yu, Yuzhu Ji, Yiqun Zhang, Zhijie Wang, Haijun Zhang, Yiu-ming Cheung

entry.summary: OcTreeMamba integrates octree structures into state-space models for 3D medical segmentation, using anatomy-adaptive sparsification to respect the intrinsic spatial hierarchy and sparsity of anatomical structures. It addresses the problem that heuristic selective-scan strategies in Mamba-based segmenters disrupt spatial hierarchy and add computational redundancy. The result is topology-aware long-range context propagation with linear-time complexity.

entry.title: ProtoGestalt: Interpretable Prototypes for Facial Phenotyping and Diagnosis of Rare Genetic Disorders

author.name: Ranga Baminiwatte, Alexander Hustinx, Fabio Hellmann, Aaron J Masino

entry.summary: Presents an interpretable prototype-based framework for facial phenotyping and rare genetic disorder screening that constrains learned features to select facial regions, so predictions are explained via localized additive evidence. It is evaluated for distinguishing syndromic from unaffected faces across multiple control datasets and prevalence settings.

entry.title: Message-passing graph persistence

author.name: Jorge Luiz Franco, Arthur Queiroz Moura, Moacir Ponti, Amauri Souza

entry.summary: The paper introduces Message-Passing Graph Persistence (MGP), topological descriptors that weave message passing into graph filtrations, updating node embeddings at each filtration step and tying them to persistence events. The authors prove MGP is more expressive than the 1-Weisfeiler-Leman test that bounds standard GNNs, integrating persistent homology into representation learning.

entry.title: Better honeypots, fewer tries: training an optimizer to make PPO cheat

author.name: Aniket Ghosh

entry.summary: A course project that reframes the construction of reward-hacking honeypots as a black-box optimization problem, training an optimizer with evolution strategies on synthetic functions to find gridworld levels where PPO cheats. The learned optimizer found cheating-inducing levels 79% of the time versus 70% for CMA-ES, and found strong levels in a median of 6 PPO runs versus 46 for GP Bayesian optimization.

entry.title: When Verification Is Not Agreement: Cross-Agent LLM-to-Dafny Formalization

author.name: Priyanath Maji

entry.summary: This paper introduces a cross-agent protocol where a Specifier model translates clinical trial criteria into Dafny predicates and an Implementer model writes code checked against them, showing that even same-model independent re-extraction agrees only 59.3% of the time. Across four configurations on 96 clinical trial documents, agreement is highly sensitive to how capability is allocated between the two roles.

entry.title: CST-Bench: Benchmarking Counterfactual Spatial Transition Reasoning with Causal Transition On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Ying Li, Yongle Cheng, Jing Li, Xingquan Cai, Yawei Luo

entry.summary: CST-Bench is a 7,082-example benchmark for counterfactual spatial reasoning in multimodal LLMs, covering 6 intervention types and 12 transformation operators with dense causal annotations (sources, affected relations, expected effects, invariants). The authors benchmark general MLLMs and compare post-training strategies including on-policy self-distillation against standard spatial reasoning data.

entry.title: How Finite Brains Generalize Without Bound: Spatial Memory as a Universal Computer

author.name: Yuhang He, Si Wu

entry.summary: This theoretical paper distinguishes learners that read coordinates (positions, counts, times, which take novel values as inputs grow) from learners that read coincidences (same/not-same relations, whose answers are size-invariant), arguing this determines whether finite experience yields unbounded generalization. It frames spatial memory as carrying input size while the rule stays finite, connecting to why children extrapolate arithmetic but LSTMs and Transformers trained on short sequences fail on longer ones. It offers a conceptual account of length generalization.

entry.title: LeanContext: Disentangling Mathematical Resources from Local Formal Context in Lean Whole-Proof Generation

author.name: Hang Zhang, Qihao Ye, Litong Liu, Yunbei Zhang, Yugyung Lee, Yue Zhou, Bowen Liu, Emily First, Cheng Han, Qiao Zhuang

entry.summary: LeanContext is a benchmark of 129,826 Lean whole-proof generation problems designed to measure the advantage of target-selected mathematical declarations over comparable alternatives and how training affects this. It separates Mathematical Context from Environment Context across four aligned input views for crossed training and inference evaluations with original Lean verification. It covers both diffusion- and autoregressive-based models.

entry.title: RM-VLM: From Natural-Language Task Descriptions to Vision-Grounded Reward Machines

author.name: Roko Parac, Christos Ziakas, Leo Ardon, Alessandra Russo
