entry.title: FedReason: Large Language Models as Weight-Space Meta-Aggregators for Heterogeneous Federated Learning

author.name: Ali Mohammadi Ruzbahani, Abbas Yazdinejad, Hadis Karimipour

entry.summary: FedReason uses an LLM, invoked every ten rounds in a sandboxed server-side loop, to analyze federated learning client weights via code execution and select or author the aggregation rule, with privacy preserved by keeping weight tensors on the server and falling back to FedAvg on invalid output. Evaluations used Claude Opus 5.5, an established frontier model, as the meta-aggregator.

entry.title: SteelAgent: LLM-Orchestrated, Physics-Informed Steel Property Prediction with Audited Generalization and Calibrated Uncertainty

author.name: Aleksandr Volkov, Roman Sultimov, Mikhail Kuzin, Yury Maximov

entry.summary: SteelAgent couples metallurgical descriptors and ML models with an LLM interface for steel property prediction, uncertainty reporting, and inverse design, and critically audits how held-out unit choice changes conclusions: gradient boosting R-squared falls from 0.859 on random splits to 0.113 with steel families held out, and nominal 90% prediction interval coverage drops to 37.6% on held-out sources.

entry.title: Robust Stream Classification using Time Neutralising Decision Trees

author.name: Brandon Gower-Winter, Georg Krempl

entry.summary: The authors propose time-neutralising decision trees for data stream classification, addressing concept drift without relying on the usual detect-and-retrain paradigm. The approach builds on prior work showing batch learners can handle stored stream instances, offering robustness to non-stationarity by construction. This could reduce the operational cost of perpetually retraining deployed stream models.

entry.title: Teaching Agents the "Principle", Not the "Reward"

author.name: Shan Yang

entry.summary: The paper argues that RL struggles in complex tasks because agents must decode designer knowledge from scalar reward sequences, and proposes prescriptive policy learning (PPL) that teaches agents explicit principles of behavior such as how to maintain balance or accumulate energy. This shifts the interface from reward hacking-prone scalars toward direct knowledge transfer. It connects to current interests in reward design and instruction-following agents.

entry.title: RLGPA: A Reinforcement Learning-Guided Granularity Planning Attack for Decision-Based Sparse Adversarial Examples

author.name: Chao Zhou, Shenghua He, Jiaxin Mo, Qiangguo Yu, Fengchuang Xing

entry.summary: RLGPA uses online reinforcement learning (a masked Dueling Double DQN) to schedule support-reduction strategies at varying granularities for decision-based sparse adversarial attacks under a hard query budget, switching from coarse to history-aware fine moves as perturbation support contracts. The method improves attack efficiency against label-only oracles. It is relevant primarily as an adversarial robustness stress test.

entry.title: Non-Parametric Mutual Information Estimation with Vine Copulas

author.name: Sigurd Holmsen, Berit Omli {\O}ksnes, Ingrid Hob{\ae}k Haff, Sylvia Richardson, Ali Ramezani-Kebrya

entry.summary: The authors introduce VINE, a mutual information estimator based on simplified D-vine copulas that reduces the density ratio to a product of pair copulas estimable non-parametrically. VINE achieves accuracy competitive with state-of-the-art neural MI estimators at lower computational cost on low- to medium-dimensional datasets. This offers a practical alternative to expensive neural estimation methods.

entry.title: Towards Multiscale Molecular Representation Learning through Geometry-Based Fragmentation for Polymer Property Prediction

author.name: Makoto Takamoto, Chaitanya Sampara, Viktor Zaverkin, Daniel O\~noro-Rubio, Mathias Niepert

entry.summary: The paper formulates molecular fragmentation as a learned, geometry-based process rather than relying on predefined chemical rules, building multiscale molecular representations for polymer property prediction. Fragment-based inductive biases let specific motifs contribute unequally to predicted chemical and physical properties. This improves robustness on chemically unfamiliar structures where rule-based fragmentation fails.

entry.title: Detecting Weather Fronts from Satellite Observations: What Does Reanalysis Add?

author.name: Ioannis Dravilas, Miruna Stoicescu, Roope Tervo, Carlos Horn, Oriol Hinojo Comellas, Sina Montazeri, Andrea Meraner, Ana Lucic

entry.summary: This study trains an ML model for pixel-wise weather front classification over the North Atlantic and Europe, comparing satellite-only infrared input against adding 28 ERA5 reanalysis fields. The satellite-only model achieves a CSI@150 of 0.402, within the range of agreement between different meteorological analyses, and the paper quantifies the incremental value of reanalysis data. It is a careful application study with meteorological grounding relevant to operational forecasting.

entry.title: Geometric Relevance Is Not Sufficient: Evaluating Focused Post-Training Supervision in Diffusion Docking

author.name: Michael Brown, Maryam Rahimimovassagh, Mehdi Yazdani-Jahromi, Sanjeda Sara Jennifer, Ivan Garibay

entry.summary: Using DiffDock as a testbed, this fixed-budget study compares broad post-training continuation against focused torsional supervision for diffusion-based molecular docking, evaluating score fidelity, pose quality, best-of-10 sampling, and confidence-selected Top-1 performance. Findings indicate that concentrating supervision on geometrically relevant corrections does not necessarily improve docking outcomes. The work provides useful guidance on post-training data selection for generative scientific models.

entry.title: Module-Aware Optimization for Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Guy Hadad, Haggai Roitman, Moshe Eliasof, Bracha Shapira

entry.summary: GraphMuon adapts the Muon matrix-aware optimizer to graph neural networks by accounting for the covariance structure of graph-propagated features, which shape the effective geometry of weight-matrix updates beyond learned channel-mixing weights. The observation that well-normalized matrix updates can be amplified by graph propagation motivates the graph-aware correction. It extends the growing literature on module-aware optimizers.

entry.title: Approximating the Euclidean Ball by Polytopes: Surprising Rates in High Dimensions

author.name: Yegor Gorodzha, Steven Hoehner, Gil Kur

entry.summary: The paper gives sharp asymptotic estimates for the number of vertices needed to approximate the Euclidean unit ball in high dimension under symmetric-difference volume error, showing exp(O(sqrt(d)/eps)) vertices suffice while a fixed error requires exponentially many facets in dimension. Results extend to Gaussian error metrics.

entry.title: Bayesian Tensor Train Kernel Machines with Automatic Model Complexity Inference

author.name: Afra Kilic, Kim Batselier

entry.summary: This work extends Bayesian tensor-network kernel machines from the CP decomposition to the tensor train format, using hierarchical ARD-type priors on TT cores to automatically infer ranks and feature dimensions from data. The neighbor coupling of TT cores requires careful posterior propagation, yielding a scalable supervised learning method without manual complexity tuning.

entry.title: Using Transformers to Generate 3-Manifold Triangulations

author.name: Daniel Bruwel, Ashvni Narayanan, Jonathan Spreer

entry.summary: The authors train GPT-2-style transformers to generate triangulations of 3-manifolds using dehydration-signature encodings, spanning roughly 3 exaFLOPs of training compute and models from 11M to 200M parameters. The best model generates valid closed-manifold signatures at a 6.9% rate, and IsoFLOP curve analysis reveals neural scaling behavior for this topology generation task.

entry.title: Transformer-Based Trajectory Prescription for sEMG-Optimizing Robot-Mediated Rehabilitation

author.name: Gabriel Parra, Kimia Khoshnami, Daniel S. Brown, Laura A. Hallock

entry.summary: The authors build a personalizable transformer encoder-decoder with rotary positional embeddings that maps a patient's muscle activations from surface EMG to prescribed contact-force trajectories for an end-effector rehabilitation robot. Unlike prior systems that prescribe kinematic trajectories, this targets neuromotor activations thought to support recovery. It matters as an applied step toward individualized, activation-aware robotic therapy.

entry.title: Matching the Training-Time Weight Rule in Inference-Time Expert Deactivation

author.name: Hao Cheng (Zhejiang Gongshang University), Zhiyu Yang (Chang'an University), Bo Ma (Zhejiang Gongshang University), Hanzhang Jia (University of Sussex)

entry.summary: This paper analyzes inference-time expert deactivation in mixture-of-experts models, comparing removal, freezing, renormalization, and unnormalized re-routing across five checkpoints from four model families plus OLMoE, and develops a weight-sum model tying performance loss to the weight rule used during training. With half the experts deactivated, the best weight rule depends on whether models were trained with raw router probabilities. It provides actionable guidance for MoE compression and editing.

entry.title: Information-Matched Auditing of Conversational Emotion-Shift Forecasting: A Leakage-Safe Evaluation Protocol

author.name: Bin Wen, Dai-Qiao Zhang, Tien-Ping Tan

entry.summary: Presents an information-matched, leakage-safe auditing protocol for conversational emotion-shift forecasting that controls for feature asymmetry, hyperparameter budgets, and target-turn information leakage. Applied to six causal model families on four corpora, it shows apparently large reported gains can shrink or disappear under fair comparisons.

entry.title: AssameseLM-E2B: An Open-Weight Assamese Language Model for Efficient Consumer-Grade Deployment

author.name: Pragyan Phukan

entry.summary: Presents AssameseLM-E2B, a 2B-parameter open-weight model for the low-resource Assamese language, built on Gemma-3-class architecture with an expanded byte-level BPE vocabulary reducing tokenization overhead and a continual pre-training plus SFT pipeline using Hybrid LoRA. It targets consumer-grade deployment efficiency.

entry.title: Balancing hierarchical representation and quantization: A performance trade-off in text embeddings

author.name: Kai Ponel, Marco Polignano, Erasmo Purificato, Aylin Julia Temizkan, Marco Levantesi, Giovanni Semeraro, Ernesto William De Luca

entry.summary: An empirical benchmark of how hierarchical (variable-length) embedding representations interact with quantization, evaluating 168 configurations per task across 38 MTEB tasks and four transformer embedding models. Using Friedman tests with Nemenyi post-hoc analysis, it finds int8 quantization statistically indistinguishable from full precision, reporting storage and end-to-end time separately.

entry.title: Text-Only Domain Adaptation for Low-Resource Medical ASR: Shallow Fusion and Density Ratio Rescoring for Hausa

author.name: Oche David Ankeli, Hassan Adelani Luqman, Theodora Ngozi Egbunike, Joshua Gottschalk, Bonaventure F. P. Dossou

entry.summary: The paper adapts a fixed MMS-1B acoustic model for Hausa medical speech recognition using only text: decoding-time fusion of a small medical KenLM via shallow fusion and density ratio rescoring. Evaluation uses 250 physician-reviewed recordings from six northern Nigerian states under prompt-disjoint cross-validation. It matters as a low-cost recipe for improving specialized ASR where domain speech data is unavailable.

entry.title: Perceptual Distortion for Overfitted Video Coding: Sliced Matching in Space, Error Alignment in Time

author.name: Tianyi Yang, Ge Gao, Fan Zhang, David Bull

entry.summary: This work extends Wasserstein Distortion to neural video coding, addressing its limited expressiveness from independent Gaussian approximations and temporal inconsistency from unconstrained texture resampling. The method uses sliced matching in space and error alignment in time to balance perceptual quality and fidelity at fixed bitrate. It enables lightweight overfitted codecs to compete with heavy generative decoders.

entry.title: Degree-Equalized View-Graph Selection under Tight Pair Budgets

author.name: Minhyeok Im, Jongseong Brad Choi

entry.summary: The paper shows that one-shot view-graph selectors in Structure-from-Motion can concentrate matching edges on few images, causing reconstruction failure even on nearly connected verified graphs, and proposes a training-free greedy degree-equalizing selection rule. At B=2N on nine 1DSfM collections it substantially improves degree coverage. A focused but useful improvement to SfM pipelines.

entry.title: Egocentric Action Recognition with Objects and Vision-Language Affordances

author.name: Ra\'ul Boix-Aldeguer, Manuel Benavent-Lledo, David Ortiz-Perez, Jose Garcia-Rodriguez

entry.summary: The paper proposes an egocentric action recognition method that combines a frozen SlowFast video backbone with an attention-based object expert via late fusion, representing each object through affordances generated zero-shot by a vision-language model. This targets the fact that egocentric actions are largely defined by manipulated objects, which prior RGB/depth methods underuse. Applications include elder-care monitoring and task assistance.

entry.title: Rain Beyond Streaks: Cascaded Realistic Rain and Wet Surface Synthesis via Scene Priors

author.name: Melissa Tijink, Kirill Tolstobrov, Shunxin Wang, Estefania Talavera, Duc V. Le, Luuk Spreeuwers, Shaodi You, Nicola Strisciuglio

entry.summary: CascadeRS is a rain synthesis framework that uses depth and segmentation priors to render scene-consistent rain together with consequential surface effects such as reflections and puddles, which prior work largely ignores. The physics-inspired, zero-shot, controllable generative pipeline yields photorealistic rainy urban scenes for training robust vision systems. Validation covers perceptual realism qualitatively and quantitatively.

entry.title: ATHAAR: A Medieval Scientific Arabic Manuscript Dataset for Handwritten Text Recognition

author.name: Ismail El Jamiy, Khadija Msalek, Guillaume Loizelet, Farah Benamara, Nabil Hathout

entry.summary: Introduces the first annotation guidelines for transcribing medieval Arabic scientific manuscripts, grounded in textual criticism, and ATHAAR, a manually annotated HTR dataset varying witnesses, calligraphic styles, and content including numerals. It targets a hard low-resource recognition problem that current vision-language models handle poorly.

entry.title: Adaptive Low-Light Enhancement for Road Anomaly Detection: A Multi-Architecture Benchmark and Edge Deployment Study

author.name: Obed Honour Eje, Oluwatosin Kolade, Glory Bagai, Taliha Abiodun Folorunso

entry.summary: Benchmarks four object detectors (YOLOv8n, YOLOv12n, RT-DETR, Faster R-CNN) under physically grounded lighting and weather degradation, showing that uniform low-light enhancement can be actively harmful at dusk-level lighting. It proposes a lightweight training-free luminance-adaptive router that selects enhancement strategies per frame and validates full pipeline deployment on edge hardware.

entry.title: FFMT: Frequency-Factorized Multi-Rate Tokenization for Music-to-Dance Generation

author.name: Qirong Guo, Ruijie Li, Zeyan Li, Sicheng Shu, Guanzhi Ding, Weihang Ding

entry.summary: FFMT decomposes dance motion into a low-frequency choreographic scaffold and a high-frequency residual, tokenizing each at different rates with differently sized codebooks. This representation enables a plan-then-articulate autoregressive factorization where coarse choreography is established first, then refined with rapid local movements.

entry.title: Dynamic Watermarking and Action-Conditioned Latent Dynamics for Secure Vision-Based Controllers

author.name: Aditya Parameshwaran, Navid Aftabi, Abhishek Hanchate, Satish T. S. Bukkapatnam, Dan Li, Yue Wang

entry.summary: This work develops an adaptive dynamic-watermarking framework to detect replay attacks on vision-based control systems: a private Gaussian watermark is added to control inputs, and a latent dynamics network conditioned on the input predicts expected image evolution, with attack evidence drawn from prediction-observation discrepancy. A reinforcement learning policy adjusts watermark strength adaptively.

entry.title: Dual-Arm Tabletop Rearrangement with Movable Stacking and Gap-Aware Push Transfers

author.name: Mohammadreza Firoozalizadeh, Zakiye Rostamirad, Arman Barghi, Ahmad Kalhor, Mohammadreza Nayeri, Mehdi Tale Masouleh

entry.summary: This paper presents a dual-arm tabletop rearrangement framework combining movable buffering stacks with a Gap-Aware Push Transfer mechanism for asynchronous cross-boundary object exchange, replacing fixed handoff configurations. This improves flexibility and coverage in dense, wide workspaces. It is a solid contribution to multi-arm manipulation planning.

entry.title: Generalized Hyperrectangular Prediction Sets in Multivariate Conformal Prediction

author.name: Nabil Alami, Souhaib Ben Taieb

entry.summary: This paper extends hyperrectangular prediction sets in multivariate conformal prediction to Cartesian products of arbitrary one-dimensional sets, called generalized hyperrectangles, improving interpretability over complex geometries like ellipsoids or density level sets. It introduces a rectangularization framework converting any continuous multivariate nonconformity score into one yielding such sets with finite-sample coverage guarantees, and establishes geometric properties.

entry.title: Towards Efficient Whole Page Ranking with One-Pass Inference

author.name: Qi Xu, Zhigang Hua, Zijie Lei, Yan Xie, Jizhe Zhang, Lynn Lu, Delun Du, Sha Hua, Ren Mao, Ke Pan, Haomin Yu, Sandeep Pandey, Luke Simon

entry.summary: This industrial paper from a large web company proposes Multi-Item Scoring, a prefix-aware non-autoregressive framework for whole-page ranking that captures order-dependent interactions between selected items while retaining one-pass inference efficiency. It bridges the quality gap between autoregressive methods and the efficiency of NAR approaches under layout and business constraints for ads and organic content.

entry.title: Regularization vs. Convolution in Kernel-Based Hypothesis Testing

author.name: Omar Hagrass, Bharath K. Sriperumbudur

entry.summary: The authors unify two previously separate lines of work on MMD test optimality - the convolution approach with shrinking bandwidths on R^d and the spectral regularization approach on general spaces - by analyzing the regularization approach over Sobolev balls under L2-separation. They reveal an explicit connection between the two approaches.

entry.title: Persistent Retrieval for Conversational Agents: A Study of Retrieval Efficiency

author.name: Karthik Ravula, Sathwik Kowtha, Rishabh Verma, Kala Mehak Jain, Gunjit Mittal

entry.summary: The paper compares three retrieval architectures for conversational agents: skill-based retrieval in the main agent, a non-persistent retrieval subagent, and a persistent retrieval subagent that maintains retrieval history across turns and returns evidence directly. The persistent design also lets the main agent request corrections from the same subagent. It evaluates the designs on independent, shared-conversation, and dependent enterprise questions to measure efficiency effects.

entry.title: Batch-Conditioned Semantic Anchors for Robust Transductive Adaptation of Vision--Language Models

author.name: Mohammed Rahman Sherif Khan Mohammad, Ardhendu Behera, Sandip Pradhan, Swagat Kumar, Amr Ahmed

entry.summary: Proposes JPTA, a prior-aware framework for transductive test-time adaptation of vision-language models that treats CLIP text prototypes as semantic references to be estimated per batch rather than fixed priors or freely replaceable. This addresses the trade-off between exploiting batch structure and preserving text semantics under sparse batches, prior shift, and partial label-space coverage.

entry.title: Energy-Aware Open-Vocabulary Detection Scheduling for Low-Power Robotic Autonomy

author.name: Abdul Basit, Muhammad Shafique

entry.summary: The paper presents a scheduler that switches among low-, mid-, and high-power YOLO-World-S modes on a Jetson Orin Nano using odometry, map change, and detector confidence, reducing wasted inference on low-value frames during robot navigation. Real trials on an AgileX LIMO show slightly better mission success than fixed-rate baselines with reduced energy use.

entry.title: ZeroRAG: Adaptive Semantic Peer Routing for Decentralized Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Petru Neague, Quinten Stokkink, Martijn de Vos, Rafael Pires, Mathis Randl, Anne-Marie Kermarrec, Johan Pouwelse

entry.summary: ZeroRAG enables retrieval-augmented generation without centralized document stores, routing queries through peer networks for parties who cannot surrender document custody due to privacy, copyright, or regulatory constraints. It avoids both coordinating authorities and global data structures like DHTs via adaptive semantic peer routing. This addresses a real deployment constraint for RAG in privacy-sensitive and federated settings.

entry.title: Estimating Spectrum-Free Information Bounds for Generative Surrogates Beyond Conditional Collapse

author.name: Chaitanya Dumbre, Sourabh Dube

entry.summary: The paper shows that common 1D marginal divergence metrics can reward conditional collapse in generative surrogates for high-energy physics, demonstrating on a CMS benchmark that an unconditional sampler beats a trained mixture density network on all marginals. The authors propose using the Continuous Ranked Probability Skill Score against the exact marginal as a more informative evaluation.

entry.title: SHORE: Stability-Hybrid On-Policy Reinforcement Learning for Online Bin Packing

author.name: Chang Shi, Ann Majewicz Fey

entry.summary: SHORE combines a learned stability probability, trained by a 3D U-Net from executed and simulated packing outcomes, with an on-policy estimate of return conditional on stability for online 3D bin packing with a processing buffer. This hybrid replaces hard stability masks and lets risk influence joint choices of box, orientation, and placement. It matters for physically grounded sequential decision-making where failures terminate episodes.

entry.title: Selective, Risk-Controlled Emotion Forecasting in Conversation: From a Persistence Barrier to Departure Detection with Conformal Guarantees

author.name: Bin Wen, Dai-Qiao Zhang, Tien-Ping Tan

entry.summary: Shows that next-emotion-value forecasting in conversation is dominated by a persistence baseline, and reformulates the task as detecting departures from persistence with conformal risk guarantees. The paper reports an honest negative result: departure timing is learnable on only three of four corpora and near chance on the highest-base-rate corpus.

entry.title: CMDiff: Left Atrial Scar Segmentation from 3D LGE MRI Using Conditional Mask Diffusion Model: A Feasibility Study

author.name: Jing Zhang, Bastien Bergere, Jonas Leite, Emilie Bollache, Mika\"el Laredo, Alban Redheuil, Nadjia Kachenoura

entry.summary: CMDiff applies conditional diffusion to segment left atrial scar in 3D LGE cardiac MRI, using a dynamic-encoder-conditioned 3D sinusoidal UNet, and is evaluated against a deterministic baseline in five-fold cross-validation on 60 LASCARQS subjects. Scar segmentation is clinically meaningful for predicting atrial fibrillation ablation outcomes but is hampered by low contrast and extreme class imbalance. The paper positions itself explicitly as a feasibility study.

entry.title: Edge-Assisted Crowdsensing for Explainable Cyclist Safety Perception

author.name: Hongsen Cao, Chia-Yen Chiang, Mona Jaber, Meihui Wang, Yasmin Fathy

entry.summary: Presents an edge-assisted crowdsensing system where handlebar camera frames are turned into structured traffic attributes by a VLM with a single prompt, combined with OpenStreetMap infrastructure and on-bike kinematics via an explainable boosting machine to predict crowdsourced 1-9 cyclist safety scores. Timing analysis shows VLM extraction must run at the network edge.

entry.title: Wedge-Jamming Mechanism for String Configuration

author.name: Taro Tako, Takanori Jin, Hiroshi Kaminaga, Taisuke Kobayashi

entry.summary: The authors propose a wedge-jamming mechanism for wire-based variable stiffness structures, adding wedge-shaped contacts to resist disturbances in directions beyond the joint-axis holding torque that conventional jamming mechanisms address. Variable stiffness with both flexibility and rigidity is a key enabler for soft and safe robotic systems. This extends the design space of jamming-based variable stiffness mechanisms.

entry.title: Risk-Sensitive Non-Parametric and Kernel Bandits

author.name: Devdan Dey, Sujoy Bhore, Avishek Ghosh

entry.summary: This paper studies non-parametric bandits where arms are evaluated via Cumulative Prospect Theory rather than expected reward, proposing NPCB, an optimistic algorithm decoupling mean estimation from CPT-based decisions. It proves CPT regret of order matching classical non-parametric bandits, showing risk sensitivity under CPT incurs no additional order-wise cost in continuous action spaces.

entry.title: Fundamental Limits of Coherent Imaging in The Presence of Atmospheric Turbulence

author.name: Songbin Liu, Hanyu Yang, Junren Chen, Arian Maleki

entry.summary: This paper establishes minimax upper and lower bounds for jointly estimating signal amplitude and atmospheric phase distortion in multi-look coherent imaging corrupted by speckle and Gaussian noise, for structured parameter classes. The results quantify how structural complexity, dimensions, and number of looks affect fundamental estimation limits.

entry.title: SD-LoRA: Training-Time Structural Distillation into LoRA for Few-Shot Vision-Language Adaptation

author.name: Mohammed Rahman Sherif Khan Mohammad, Ardhendu Behera, Sandip Pradhan, Swagat Kumar, Yonghuai Liu

entry.summary: Proposes SD-LoRA, which uses token-level graph reasoning only during training to distill structural knowledge into a lightweight LoRA-adapted CLIP model, avoiding inference-time overhead. It targets the tension in few-shot vision-language adaptation between fine-grained visual discrimination and deployment efficiency that limits prompt tuning, LoRA, and cache-based adapters.

entry.title: Task-Calibrated Random Features via Influence-Based Error Cancellation

author.name: Shinto Eguchi

entry.summary: The paper proposes Task-Calibrated Random Features, which weight frequency sampling errors using task-specific influence so that only errors affecting the downstream task are canceled, with closed-form weights tied to classical minimum-distance calibration. The analysis yields first-order variance characterizations and non-Gaussian second-order limits for kernel ridge regression and kernel Stein discrepancy.

entry.title: Patch Attention Wisely: Understanding Patch Length in Attention-Based Forecasting

author.name: Junyu Chen, Likai Chen, Weining Wang

entry.summary: The authors develop a theoretical framework explaining why patch length matters in attention-based time series forecasters, deriving an exact factorization of the forecasting coefficient matrix for linear state-space models that separates forecast from filtering dynamics. This yields a principled basis for patch length selection, replacing purely empirical tuning.

entry.title: Trust Responsive Runtime Authorization for Agentic AI with Empirical Characterization of Policy Behavior and Parameter Sensitivity

author.name: Ahsan Habib Shihab, Imre Felde, Ramis Akhmedov, Stefan Gubo, Berik Sabdenaliyev, Madina Mansurova, Amir Mosavi

entry.summary: The paper empirically characterizes TRAP, a runtime authorization policy that maps a weighted readiness score (trust, stability, contextual risk) to agent authority levels via asymmetric escalation and de-escalation rules. On matched Monte Carlo traces, TRAP restricts faster under abrupt degradation and re-escalates sooner than static, trust-only, risk-only, and symmetric baselines, with parameter sensitivity analysis included.

entry.title: Redacting Personal Data: A Speed and Accuracy Comparison of Regex, Presidio and Hybrid Designs

author.name: Sai Yashwant, Manoj Kumar Gondimalla, Arjun Sharma, Shubham

entry.summary: The authors compare four practical PII-redaction designs for LLM pipelines: pure regex, Microsoft Presidio with spaCy, a hybrid where Presidio handles names and regex handles structured identifiers, and a fast hybrid variant. The paper quantifies the latency and recall trade-offs that teams usually lack data on when redacting prompts before they are sent to model providers. It provides actionable engineering guidance for privacy-preserving LLM deployment.

entry.title: SMART: State-based Multi Agent Reasoning Traces for Verification-oriented Problem-Solving

author.name: Sai Vallurupalli, Francis Ferraro

entry.summary: SMART is a multi-agent LLM framework that extracts implicit entity states from problem contexts and curates them as complementary, solution-salient premises using role-based prompting across multiple LLMs. These real-world-verified premises then guide solution reasoning, improving validation performance up to 20 percent on complex scientific claims across three datasets. Grounding premises in real-world knowledge contributes up to 5 percent of the gain.

entry.title: A minimal dynamical model of human-AI cognitive coevolution

author.name: Petar Jolakoski, Dimitar Trajanov, Qiyu Sun, Zhen Wu, Ljupco Kocarev

entry.summary: Builds a phenomenological dynamical model, based on fluid vs. crystallized intelligence from cognitive-aging research, to study whether pervasive cognitive offloading onto generative AI could cause lasting declines in unassisted human reasoning. The model couples human intelligence variables to a machine-intelligence variable via Hill functions, providing a formal framework for a widely debated societal question.

entry.title: Depth or Description? When a One-Step Latent Score Replaces Lookahead in Proactive Information Acquisition

author.name: Biswa Sengupta

entry.summary: Analyzes when a cheap one-step score can replace expensive lookahead in proactive agents deciding what to ask before acting, finding that the need for depth often depends on how hidden causes are described. A score computed on a suitable latent representation can substitute for most of the search depth, while the same problem can defeat a label-level score, with cross-model transfer caveats.

entry.title: Selective Retrieval Routing for Multi-Violation Knowledge Graph Repair

author.name: Tung-Wei Lin, Gabe Fierro, Han Li, Tianzhen Hong, Pierluigi Nuzzo, Alberto Sangiovanni-Vinentelli

entry.summary: The paper proposes a framework for iterative knowledge graph repair in which an LLM repair agent edits the graph while a router selectively controls access to a retrieval agent that gathers external evidence, cutting retrieval costs. The authors extend a violation-injection framework to generate cases with multiple compatible violations and known reference repairs for evaluation. This addresses when external retrieval is worth its cost during graph repair.

entry.title: Echoes of Error: Residual-Directional Local Rollout Consistency for Timeseries Forecasting

author.name: Zheng Wang, Kaixuan Zhang, Xiaonan Lu, Wanfang Chen

entry.summary: Formalizes how rollout errors in time-series forecasting compound when fed back into the evolving state, introducing local rollout consistency that compares predictions under teacher forcing versus free running. Because the residual-to-state alignment operator is hard to design across architectures, the authors derive a first-order surrogate penalizing Jacobian-vector products in the residual direction. This yields a training regularizer aimed at reducing compounding rollout error.

entry.title: Neural Image Compression with Internal-External Prior Fusion and Alignment

author.name: Tiancheng Si, Wenlong Xu, Dahua Gao

entry.summary: The paper proposes IE-PFA, a context model for learned image compression that fuses internal priors from the current image with a shared learnable dictionary serving as an external prior, using an RWKV-based fusion module with linear complexity and a training-only self-distilled alignment mechanism that adds no inference overhead.

entry.title: Network Effect Decomposition for Causal Effect Estimation under Network Interference

author.name: Zhirong Huang, Wenzhen Zhang, Guangquan Lu, Boyan Chen, Debo Cheng, Shichao Zhang

entry.summary: NEDNet is a neural architecture for causal effect estimation under network interference that decomposes outcome response into a query-invariant pre-treatment baseline plus separate treatment- and exposure-response pathways, with path-specific neighborhood contextualization. This addresses the common flaw of joint predictors that leave response components implicit in network data. It advances causal inference methodology for interconnected observational data.

entry.title: tok: a textual concrete syntax of BPMN and DMN for humans and AI agents

author.name: Marek Deja

entry.summary: tok is a plain-text notation for BPMN 2.0.2 process models and DMN 1.5 decisions, with a single checker validating against both standards, compilation to XML with automatic diagrams, and MCP integration for language-model applications. Empirically, tok models use 2.2x fewer tokens than the smallest BPMN XML, the checker catches 98.2% of injected faults versus 85.8% for XML Schema with bpmnlint, and LLMs new to tok write valid models. This is a practical bridge between formal business-process standards and LLM agents.

entry.title: DART: Domain-Agnostic Residual Transfer for Generalist Anomaly Detection

author.name: Muhammad Aqeel, Maham Nazir, Marco Cristani, Francesco Setti

entry.summary: DART is a plug-in framework for few-shot generalist anomaly detection that disentangles residuals from normal-abnormal reference comparisons into anomaly-relevant and domain-specific components, suppressing spurious activations on unseen domains. It combines a Residual Disentanglement Module with domain-invariant filtering to improve cross-domain transfer.

entry.title: Backbone-Informed Adaptation after EEG Pretraining: A Capacity-Controlled Study

author.name: Mingyang Jiang, Yamin Li, Fan Ma, Daniel Moyer, Hua Xu, Catie Chang

entry.summary: This study asks whether adapters that mirror the channel-time structure of EEG foundation models outperform simpler token-wise MLP adapters, under controlled and approximately matched parameter counts with frozen encoders. It is a careful capacity-controlled comparison across two settings. The result informs adapter design for EEG and possibly other structured-modality foundation models.

entry.title: Two-stage residual learning for calibrated uncertainty in solar irradiance forecasts

author.name: RR Flanagan, E Kasha, PW Talbot, AS Epiny, MR Deinert

entry.summary: The paper proposes a two-stage LSTM approach for solar irradiance forecasting in which a second network models forecast errors separately from the expected value, yielding better-calibrated uncertainty than direct distributional parameter prediction. Reliable uncertainty estimates matter for renewable energy integration at extended horizons. The method is motivated by synthetic solar signal generation experiments.

entry.title: Understanding Data Influence in Transportation Networks: A Physics-Constrained Influence-Function Framework

author.name: Hamidreza Attari, Yueyue Fan, Johannes Royset

entry.summary: This paper extends influence-function methods to physically constrained learning settings, addressing how individual training observations affect predictions in transportation networks where physical constraints couple network components. The authors develop a hard physics-informed framework showing that influence propagates only through physically feasible directions, which matters for interpretable and reliable data-driven transportation systems.

entry.title: Comparing Classification and Feature Learning by Analyzing Their Loss Functions in Normalized Spaces with Different Scale Factors

author.name: Qiufu Li, Huibin Xiao, Linlin Shen, Weijia Fan, Xi Jia, Yongdong Huang

entry.summary: This paper challenges the assumption that higher classification accuracy implies better learned features, arguing classification reflects sample-wise local properties while feature learning requires dataset-level global properties like intra-class compactness and inter-class separability. From first principles of feature learning, the authors redesign the binary cross-entropy loss and analyze it in normalized feature spaces with different scale factors. The work clarifies the theoretical relationship between classification objectives and representation quality.

entry.title: GTAFL: Addressing Test-Agnostic Long-Tailed Federated Learning in Medical Image

author.name: Guangyu Chen, Jingyun Zeng, Hui Jiang

entry.summary: The paper introduces Test-Agnostic Long-Tailed Federated Learning (GTAFL), addressing the realistic healthcare scenario where federated medical data is long-tailed in local and global views while test distributions are unpredictable. Existing long-tailed FL methods typically assume uniform test distributions, which fails in practice. The proposed approach targets privacy-preserving decentralized training robust to agnostic test shifts.

entry.title: ToroFit: Fitting Wedge Sums of Tori to High-Dimensional Data

author.name: Tanishq Bhatia, Jose A. Perea, Tarek M. Zikry

entry.summary: ToroFit detects and parameterizes high-dimensional point clouds lying near a wedge sum of tori using persistent cohomology and cup products to identify toroidal components, then fitting low-energy trigonometric polynomials via generalized ridge regression. The method supports modeling, interpolation, denoising, and anomaly detection for nonlinear scientific data.

entry.title: EDGAR: Efficient Diffusion-Driven Gaussian Avatar Refinement via Synthetic Failure

author.name: Kwan Yun, Minhyeok Bang, Colette Suhjung Koo, Junyong Noh

entry.summary: EDGAR is a conditional diffusion framework that refines Gaussian splatting head avatars by correcting artifacts like blurring, stretching, and temporal instability while preserving identity. The authors build a hybrid triplet dataset pairing degraded renderings with ground truth and references to simulate realistic avatar failure cases for training.

entry.title: Regret Bounds for Profit Maximization in Bilateral Trade: Learning the Best Posted-Price Mechanism

author.name: Johannes Br\"ustle, Simone Di Gregorio, Federico Fusco, Stefano Leonardi

entry.summary: The paper studies bilateral trade from the perspective of a profit-maximizing broker in a regret minimization framework, where the learner posts prices to a buyer and seller and observes only whether trade occurred. The authors derive regret bounds against the best fixed pair of posted prices, progressing from weaker to stronger feedback and valuation assumptions.

entry.title: Human-like cross-language generalisation in deep neural speaker embeddings and its acoustic foundations

author.name: Tianze Xu, Xiyang Li, Xiaoming Jiang, Volker Dellwo

entry.summary: Using Cantonese-English bilingual speech, this study tests whether speaker embeddings from 18 state-of-the-art models generalize across languages and how that relates to human perception and acoustic structure via mixed models and representational similarity analysis. Embeddings showed cross-language generalization broadly paralleling human behavior, reflecting identity discrimination and sensitivity to language switching. This connects machine speaker representations to human auditory perception and their acoustic underpinnings.

entry.title: ProcessPrefBench: Evaluating Cross-Task Transfer of Individual Process Preferences from Naturalistic Human-AI Interaction

author.name: Yiwen Yang, Guanming Liu

entry.summary: Introduces ProcessPrefBench, built from three months of natural dialogues between two knowledge workers and an assistant, testing whether a user's process preference revealed in one conversation transfers to later, unrelated tasks. It evaluates three models under target-only, full-history, and distilled-preference conditions on 66 curated source-target cases.

entry.title: Template Gap Reconstruction for Shell Output Simulation with Small Language Models

author.name: Jarrod Ragsdale, Rajendra Boppana

entry.summary: The paper introduces template gap reconstruction (TGR) for simulating shell command outputs without execution: a template bank built from 18.7 million outputs supplies reusable literals with sentinels, and small language models autoregressively generate only the varying gaps. A selector chooses among templates, with an empty template fallback to full decoding. It is a practical efficiency idea for safe sandboxing-like command simulation with compact models.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Diffusion Models for Handwritten Signature Verification via Ruin Reconstruction

author.name: Peirong Zhang, Zhenhua Yang, Jiaxin Zhang, Moises Diaz, Miguel A. Ferrer, Umapada Pal, Wei Zhou, Lianwen Jin

entry.summary: SigDiffuser applies self-supervised diffusion learning to handwritten signature verification through a novel pretext task, Reconstruction from Ruins, in which signatures are deliberately crumpled to destroy structure and style, forcing the encoder to recover discriminative handwriting features. This moves HSV beyond its predominantly supervised paradigm, relevant for forensic and legal authentication where labels are scarce.

entry.title: Describe Your Facial Expressions by Linking Image Encoders and Large Language Models

author.name: Yujian Yuan, Jiabei Zeng, Shiguang Shan

entry.summary: Defines a new task of describing facial expressions in natural language beyond discrete emotion categories or action units, and proposes a three-stage BLIP-2-style training framework. To overcome missing image-text training pairs, it synthesizes captions by combining GPT-3.5 outputs with existing emotion and AU annotations.

entry.title: An Empirical Study of Reinforcement Learning for Keypoint Positioning of Deformable Linear Objects

author.name: Vinay Rodrigues, Sara Zeynalpour, Gokhan Solak, Sebastian Hjorth, Arash Ajoudani

entry.summary: This empirical study compares three PPO training stacks for planar manipulation of grasped deformable linear objects, finding GPU-parallel MuJoCo Playground enables faster convergence than CPU alternatives under equal wall-clock budgets. It also examines observation design, asymmetric actor-critic setups, robustness, and zero-shot sim-to-real transfer.

entry.title: Flexible Piezoelectric Tactile Sensing System for Intelligent Object Recognition

author.name: Razan Khalifeh, Mohamad Yaacoub, Christian Gianoglio, Moustafa Saleh, Maurizio Valle, Yahya Abbass

entry.summary: This study presents a flexible distributed piezoelectric tactile sensing system for early-stage object recognition during grasping, comparing SVM, 1D-CNN, C-RNN, and 2D-CNN classification approaches across six everyday objects. It examines the effects of sensor configuration under real-time constraints. The work contributes practical sensing hardware and a useful comparison of learning approaches for tactile recognition.

entry.title: Distributed Geometric Optimization and Control of Rigid Differential-Drive Formations from Relative-Position Measurements

author.name: Thanacha Choopojcharoen, Erman Selim, Ramisha Anjum, Baris Fidan

entry.summary: The paper derives a two-layer estimation-and-control scheme for differential-drive robot formations with only relative-position measurements and a single absolute position anchor, regulating position, orientation, and shape. It proves finite-step consensus for graph-proximal estimators and bounded reconstruction error from a finite number of primal-dual iterations, combining proximal centroid and orientation supervision in the controller.

entry.title: Support Vector Machines Directly Minimise KL Divergence

author.name: Ivan Silajev

entry.summary: This paper proves that the dual objectives of support vector classification and regression are exact constrained KL divergence minimization problems between Gaussian measures, giving SVMs a probabilistic interpretation they have lacked. The same divergence formulation recovers kernel ridge regression when domain constraints are removed and L2 regularization applied, unifying these methods probabilistically.

entry.title: Is it better to directly or indirectly ban ASI?

author.name: Alek Westover

entry.summary: The author compares direct bans on superintelligent AI development (as proposed by Senator Sanders) with indirect regulatory approaches that condition development on demonstrating absence of specific dangerous behaviors such as sandbox escapes or rogue deployments. The note analyzes costs and benefits of each approach given the current immature state of alignment science.

entry.title: Game of AGI: An AI Policy Simulator

author.name: Craig Quiter

entry.summary: The author presents Game of AGI, a Monte Carlo policy simulator designed to model catastrophic AI risk at an intermediate level of abstraction spanning economics, geopolitics, and deep learning dynamics. It includes a public campaign mode and a Futures Lab view, intended as a starting point for codified evaluation of global AI strategy.

entry.title: People Should Resolve Tensions In AI Safety Research

author.name: David Africa

entry.summary: The author argues that AI safety as a field should prioritize short writeups that compile and reconcile contradictory evidence from the rapidly growing paper literature, organized around research questions and uncertainties rather than individual papers. The post claims this would expose methodological errors and generate productive research directions.

entry.title: Benchmarking Large Language Models on Heterogeneous Cognitive and Biomedical Knowledge Graphs: The Role of Graph Grounding in Multi-Hop Reasoning and Hallucination Mitigation

author.name: Ali Sarabadani, Kheirolah Rahsepar Fard, Tahereh Jeirani

entry.summary: The study benchmarks five LLMs, including GPT-5.1 and Gemini 2.0 Pro, across five biomedical and cognitive knowledge graphs under graph-grounded versus graph-agnostic conditions using a multitier query dataset with strong inter-annotator agreement. Results show general-purpose models, especially GPT-5.1 and Gemini 2.0 Pro, generally outperform domain-specific models like BioGPT on multi-hop reasoning. Graph grounding helps mitigate hallucination in KG-based reasoning.

entry.title: Adapting LLM Judges to Observed Human Annotation Policy through Soft Prompt Tuning

author.name: Tam\'as Janusko, Sven Kleinkop, Ricardo Bochnia, Gunnar Hempel, Steffen Tomschke, J\"urgen Anke, Maik Thiele

entry.summary: Investigates whether soft prompt tuning can align lightweight open-source LLM judges with human annotation policy, training soft prompts on FairBotBench and evaluating on bias, toxicity, and personalization dimensions. Hybrid soft-prompt tuning combining textual prompts with learned vectors improves agreement with human raters, offering a cheaper alternative to proprietary judge models.

entry.title: Encoding and Propagation of Grammatical Number in Large Language Models

author.name: Jacob Solinsky (University of Minnesota), Serguei Pakhomov (University of Minnesota)

entry.summary: Using sparse autoencoders trained on Pythia-70M, the authors examine how grammatical number is encoded and propagated through the layers of a small LLM, probing the model's internal grammar. The work leverages SAE features to study in silico representations of human language at a scale where strong grammatical competence emerges despite tiny model size. It contributes to mechanistic interpretability and the cognitive science of language representation.

entry.title: UniGADD: Universal Generator-Agnostic Deepfake Detector

author.name: Bernard Tomczyk, Agil Aghasanli, Plamen Angelov

entry.summary: UniGADD is a two-stage deepfake detector that first learns discriminative embeddings via contrastive loss on real and known fakes, then refines the embedding space with inter-cluster separation and intra-cluster compactness on real samples to generalize to unseen generators. It aims to combine high in-domain accuracy with robustness to previously unseen deepfake sources.

entry.title: DISCERN: Distributional Synthetic Replay for Retain-Free Incremental Machine Unlearning

author.name: Nicol\'as Segura-Kunsagi, Juan Luis Su\'arez-D\'iaz, Iv\'an Sevillano-Garc\'ia, Francisco Herrera

entry.summary: DISCERN handles incremental class unlearning — deletion requests arriving sequentially — by replacing access to the retain set with synthetic embeddings sampled from per-class parametric distributions (Riemannian, non-isotropic), unlike prototype replay's isotropic Gaussian assumption. It ensures previously forgotten classes stay forgotten while preserving remaining classes. This addresses a practical gap between one-shot unlearning research and real deployment deletion workflows.

entry.title: Towards Scalable Diagnostic-Driven Whole-Slide Image Retrieval for Pathology Archives

author.name: Jingsong Liu, Youssef Wally Han Li, Weiwei Zhou, Jing Dai, Elisabeth Wetzer, Peter J. Sch\"uffler

entry.summary: CLEAR-WSI is a scalable, diagnostic-driven content-based retrieval system for whole-slide pathology images, using constant-length embeddings to find similar cases without relying on inconsistent metadata or handcrafted indexing pipelines. It targets efficient navigation of rapidly growing digital pathology archives. Reliable slide retrieval can support pathologist workflows and computational pathology research.

entry.title: Gradient Boosting for Efficient Rank Discovery in Tensor Network Kernel Machines

author.name: Albert Saiapin, Kim Batselier

entry.summary: The authors propose GB-CPKM, a gradient boosting framework for canonical polyadic tensor network kernel machines that builds capacity by sequentially adding fixed-rank learners instead of searching over tensor ranks. Ensemble size is chosen via validation performance, avoiding the cost of training multiple candidate rank models.

entry.title: Fractional physics-informed neural networks to model social media virality

author.name: Alex Koong, George Em Karniadakis

entry.summary: The authors apply fractional physics-informed neural networks (fPINNs) to learn temporal memory and nonlinear growth dynamics of social media engagement, using symbolic regression to extract interpretable equations. They identify and fix a scale artifact in which the standard pointwise physics residual biases the fractional order under noise. This is a creative application of scientific ML to social dynamics.

entry.title: Online Learning with Ordered Experts (via Two-point Feedback)

author.name: Shiliang Zuo

entry.summary: This theory paper studies adversarial online learning with experts in a totally ordered action space under two-point feedback, deriving logarithmic-improvement regret bounds for separated monotone losses and bounded-variation loss settings. The results characterize when paying for a second observation pays off in sequential decision-making. It contributes to the online learning and bandit-feedback literature.

entry.title: Simple Meta-Learning for HPO and CASH Using Performance Representations

author.name: Emiel Witting, Cheng Yan, Tom Julian Viering

entry.summary: The paper proposes representing each hyperparameter configuration by its historical performance across prior tasks rather than explicit hyperparameter encodings, pairing this directly with standard surrogate models for Bayesian optimization in HPO and CASH. This sidesteps difficulties of learning surrogates in high-dimensional search spaces. The scope is the iterative candidate-selection step of AutoML.

entry.title: Flux as a Codec: Zero-Shot Lossy Compression with Flux

author.name: Fuma Kimishima, Jinjia Zhou

entry.summary: FluxC uses the Flux text-to-image model as a zero-shot compression prior, extending the DiffC idea of diffusion-based codecs. The paper systematically analyzes coding path choice, bit allocation across time steps, and reconstruction methods (ancestral sampling versus one-step and many-step ODE), showing ODE-based reconstruction achieves lower distortion. This maps the rate-distortion-perception tradeoff for generative-model-based compression.

entry.title: Extracting Single-Mode Rayleigh--Taylor Instability dynamics from data via SINDy

author.name: Chuanxing Wang, Hui Luo, Guohuai Zhu, Hongbo Cai, Shaoping Zhu, Mingxing Luo

entry.summary: The authors develop a physics-constrained, data-driven framework using sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics (SINDy) to extract low-dimensional equations for bubble and spike evolution in Rayleigh-Taylor instability, capturing overshoot and reacceleration behaviors that classical potential-flow and buoyancy-drag models miss. A nondimensional initial amplitude is introduced as an explicit parameter.

entry.title: AI-Native Task-Oriented Semantic Communications over a Relay: Benefits and Vulnerabilities

author.name: Yalin E. Sagduyu, Tugba Erpek, Aylin Yener

entry.summary: The authors jointly design source encoder, relay transformation, and destination decoders for relay-assisted semantic communication, showing gains over direct transmission especially at low SNR for image classification tasks. They also identify a security vulnerability introduced by the relay and formalize a Byzantine attack on the scheme.

entry.title: How Well Can Large Language Models Impersonate Individual Authors? A Comparative Evaluation

author.name: Harshit Gupta, Shunichi Ishihara

entry.summary: This comparative evaluation tests authorship impersonation by six widely used LLMs, including Gemini 3 Pro, Claude Opus, GPT 5.2, GPT 5.2 Pro, DeepSeek 3.2, and Grok 4.1 Fast, on short product reviews using simple versus stylometric-guided prompts, measured with a cosine-distance metric and embedding visualization. Results indicate impersonation remained challenging for most models, with some models faring better. These are established, previously released models, so the study offers an analysis of current capabilities rather than a new launch.

entry.title: TandemBench: Benchmarking Decision Models for Multi-Agent Collaboration

author.name: Baohang Li, Xiaocheng Feng, Bing Qin

entry.summary: TandemBench is a benchmark of 1,200 questions in multi-agent cooking scenarios where models must select optimal team plans given complete global information, with reference answers established through execution and exact search, plus paired variants judging whether better arrangements exist beyond supplied options. The authors evaluate 40 native decision models against 10 general-purpose language models. It matters for evaluating dedicated decision models in cooperative multi-agent settings.

entry.title: Interpretable Text Embeddings Based on Hierarchical Questions

author.name: Kohei Oda, Po-Min Chuang, Kiyoaki Shirai, Natthawut Kertkeidkachorn

entry.summary: Improves QA-based interpretable text embeddings by organizing yes/no questions hierarchically, so deeper levels become more specific and humans can replace detailed questions with aligned ancestors during interpretation. This reduces the number of questions reviewers must examine while retaining interpretive detail.

entry.title: Ranking Agreement Does Not Reveal Paragraph-Edit Agreement in Two Released Paper Acceptance Predictors

author.name: Shaoliang Yang, Jun Wang

entry.summary: This paper tests whether agreement between acceptance-prediction models on existing papers supports using a fast classifier to pre-screen revisions for a slower evaluator. On 198 ICLR papers and automatically screened paragraph rewrites, the classifier agrees with two released predictors on original-paper rankings but shows no detectable agreement on which rewrites raise scores.

entry.title: Growing One's AI Tools: A Paradigm of Practice-Grown Tools

author.name: Zeming Zhao

entry.summary: This article documents a conference interpreter without programming training building her own computer-assisted interpreting tool over eight weeks, traced through 62 commits, six versions, and telemetry from 133 sessions with over 20,000 recognized utterances. It proposes practice-grown tools as a paradigm where end users co-evolve their software with their practice using AI coding assistance. It is a rich case study of AI-enabled non-programmer software creation.

entry.title: Reviving the Discarded High-Resolution Feature for Transformer-Based Tiny Object Detection

author.name: Zehao Wang, Si Wu, Guiping Cao, Xin Li, Yaowei Wang

entry.summary: ReDHF revives the highest-resolution feature that DETR-like detectors typically discard, for tiny object detection, using three components: Cross-Scale Deformable Fusion to semantically enhance the high-resolution feature, injection of fine details into shallow features, and mechanisms to suppress dense background noise. Tiny object detection matters for aerial imagery, surveillance, and remote sensing. The work targets the loss of fine detail during feature downsampling.

entry.title: CRISP: Constraint-Resolved Interactions between Subsystems for Predictive Whole-Body Cooperation

author.name: Dario Valenzuela, Jeeseop Kim

entry.summary: CRISP is a layered control framework that decomposes humanoid dynamics into a single rigid body torso plus floating-base arm and leg models, with dynamic interactions represented as holonomic constraints whose Lagrange multipliers parametrize transmitted wrenches. It targets predictive whole-body control for dynamic dual-arm manipulation on humanoids.

entry.title: Closed-Loop Physics-Based Manipulation Evaluation at a Commodity Price: What 4.4 L4 GPU hours at $3.50 Buys You

author.name: Rohun Kshirsagar, Diana Rypkema

entry.summary: The authors present a reproducible harness for large-scale closed-loop evaluation of contact-rich manipulation on serverless commodity GPUs, costing roughly $3.50 and 38 minutes per 200-rollout replication. They also report a partially controlled negative result showing chunked action checkpoints yield zero genuine successes across 780 rollouts versus 2.6-11.8% for single-step checkpoints with sparse data.

entry.title: A Sequential Framework for Urban Drone Delivery: Network Design, Vehicle Sizing, and Energy and Cost Assessment

author.name: Hong-Su Nam, Seokhwan Lee, Jungwoo Cho, Hak-Tae Lee

entry.summary: The paper presents a sequential engineering framework for urban drone delivery linking hub location, route planning, vehicle sizing, and energy and cost assessment, using MILP to determine route frequencies and guiding motor-propeller and battery selection. This provides an end-to-end pipeline for planning drone delivery networks. It is useful for practitioners but methodologically conventional.

entry.title: Radio-to-Pose Information for Gauge-Drift Correction in Cooperative Localization

author.name: Aditya Iyer, Andy Ye, Akshay Narayan, Nora Ayanian

entry.summary: The paper addresses gauge drift, where a robot team's jointly estimated position and orientation drift together despite consistent relative measurements, by exploiting a radio attenuation map registered in the world frame. It proposes Radio-to-Pose Information, an interface converting received power residuals into Gaussian information contributions for the pose estimator.

entry.title: From Type to Token: Petri Nets, Individual Token Philosophy, and Individualized Causal Effects

author.name: Fernando Delbianco, Fernando Tohm\'e, Gustavo Bodanza

entry.summary: This conceptual paper argues that structural causal models and Bayesian networks are inherently type-level and fail under unbounded treatment-effect heterogeneity, and proposes Petri Nets under the Individual Token Philosophy as a token-level causal formalism. It develops a formal translation from Bayesian networks to Petri nets providing a two-layer account of individualized causality.

entry.title: The Changing Shape of Doom: My AI Safety Explainer

author.name: Josh Snider

entry.summary: An AI safety explainer that traces how the achievability and danger of building machine intelligence have evolved from early rule-based expert systems to contemporary deep learning. The thesis is that achievability has risen over time while the nature of present danger differs from classic fears, based on extrapolating from current technology.

entry.title: DelegateEval: Evaluating Platforms for Personal External Service Agents

author.name: Jichao Li, Jinrong Lu, Manjiang Yu, Zhixuan Liu

entry.summary: The paper defines personal external service agents, which act on behalf of an individual to serve external clients using that person's knowledge and service boundaries, and proposes DelegateEval, an eight-dimension platform-level evaluation framework covering creation ease through service delivery. The framing highlights a new economic role for agents generating value at scale.

entry.title: Value-oriented policy distillation for interpretable wind farm power control

author.name: Max Bruninx, Timothy Verstraeten, Jan Decuyper, Ann Now\'e, Jan Helsen

entry.summary: The authors tackle implicit balancing for wind farms, where power setpoints are adjusted in anticipation of unknown imbalance prices. Because reinforcement learning policies lack the interpretability needed for real deployments, they propose distilling an RL solution into an interpretable policy while accounting for how the control strategy itself affects the settlement price. This connects energy systems operation with explainable RL.

entry.title: KG-Neighbor: Knowledge-Guided Neighborhood Construction for Embedding Visualization

author.name: Chang Won Kim, Jaewook Lee, Haeun Min, JunNyeong Jeong, Minwoo Sim, Barom Kang, Kyohoon Jin

entry.summary: The paper proposes KGN, a method that improves dimensionality-reduction visualizations by reconstructing neighborhood graphs using shared knowledge-graph triples as pairwise semantic evidence instead of raw embedding distances alone. It requires no class labels and introduces an accompanying profiling tool (IDProfile). This addresses the common mismatch between embedding proximity and true content relationships in visualizations.

entry.title: FreePath: Neural Mean Free Path for Image Dehazing

author.name: Rongrong Gao, Jingxuan Feng, Wenyu Xu

entry.summary: Proposes FreePath, a physics-inspired neural framework for single image dehazing that reframes restoration as feature-space path state restoration rather than estimating atmospheric scattering parameters. A Mean Free Path Residual Block within a residual encoder-decoder learns path and collision fields to guide restoration. It aims to combine physical interpretability with learning-based stability on complex scenes.

entry.title: When, Where, How: Active In-Context Learning for Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Christian M. M. Frey

entry.summary: This paper studies active in-context learning for tabular foundation models, where adaptation happens only through labeled rows in context, asking how diversity, uncertainty, and target-aware information gain acquisition rules perform as a frozen TFM acquires context. It introduces TANN and EPIC acquisition strategies evaluated against classical rules across twenty benchmarks. It addresses the practical reality that labels for tabular tasks require scarce domain expertise.

entry.title: Using Transformers for Teaching and Learning via Symbolic Distillation of Neural A-life Agents

author.name: Shuwei Wang, Vadim Bulitko, Matthew R. G. Brown, Michael Youngblood, Ramon Lawrence, Roscoe Smith, Shinichi Nakagawa, William Yeoh

entry.summary: The paper distills opaque neural policies controlling artificial-life agents into compact symbolic policies, enabling human interpretability and cross-agent knowledge transfer between different neural architectures. Transformers are used to accelerate the symbolic policy search that typically dominates distillation cost. This supports population-level learning among heterogeneous agents.

entry.title: Acoustic Anomaly Detection for Early Identification of Drill Jamming

author.name: Maria Beatriz Silva, Lucas Edson Silva de Ara\'ujo, Sergio F. Chevtchenko, Ermeson Andrade, Danilo Araujo, Saeed Afshar

entry.summary: The paper presents an acoustic anomaly detection system using ultrasonic sensors to detect pre-failure drill jamming patterns in CNC machining, benchmarking semi-supervised autoencoders against supervised XGBoost with leave-one-drill-out validation. The authors also release a public dataset of acoustic features from 17 drills. It demonstrates that autoencoder-based normality modeling is effective for industrial safety applications.

entry.title: The Blindfolded Controller: Decision Model-Guided Training for Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Muhammad Ibrahim Khan, Aniket Dixit, Faizan Ahmed, James Brusey

entry.summary: DMGT uses a decision model given a description of the environment and task to initialize an RL policy, combining the decision model's zero-training competence in sparse-reward tasks with RL's ability to improve toward optimality. This targets the well-known sample inefficiency of RL agents facing exploration challenges and sparse rewards. The approach bridges LLM-style decision models and classical reinforcement learning.

entry.title: Randomized and Oracle-Based Feasible Directions Methods for Nonsmooth Nonconvex Constrained Optimization

author.name: Dan Greenstein, Nadav Hallak

entry.summary: This paper develops a feasible-directions framework for minimizing differences of smooth and convex functions over closed convex sets without objective derivatives, introducing eta-feasible directions to handle boundary points where the feasible direction cone is not closed. The authors provide randomized and oracle-based methods with convergence guarantees.

entry.title: SRRM: A Retrieval-Reconstruction Benchmark for Evaluating Long-Context Memory in Small Language Models

author.name: Christopher Alberto Hamonangan

entry.summary: SRRM is a lightweight, fully reproducible benchmark that jointly evaluates targeted retrieval and global information reconstruction in small language models, introducing a Memory Preservation Ratio metric linking the two. It addresses the gap where existing long-context benchmarks only test retrieval, not whether retrieval reflects comprehensive memory preservation. It matters as small models are increasingly deployed on consumer hardware.

entry.title: DEQ-Det: Dual Evidence Queries for Few-Shot Analog IC Device Detection

author.name: Zidong Zhao, Rong Huang, Chengxing Fan, Jie Hu, Malik Haris, Ghazal A. Fahmy, Morteza Mousazadeh, Guoqiang Zhang

entry.summary: DEQ-Det performs few-shot detection of analog integrated-circuit devices in layout images by building complementary foreground and background references from the same support images without extra annotation. Foreground references capture target morphology while background references characterize competing layout patterns, jointly guiding query selection and region verification. This supports automated circuit analysis and inspection.

entry.title: Curvature by Design: A Support Structure for Continuum Robots

author.name: Justus Sagem\"uller, Harald Minde Hansen, Kristin Y. Pettersen

entry.summary: Rather than assuming curvature profiles in kinematic models and estimating deviations, this paper presents a multi-segment scissor-based mechanical support structure that physically constrains continuum robots to prescribed constant or spatially varying curvature profiles. Taylor approximations distribute global bending across small-angle flexure movements in an overconstrained linkage.

entry.title: Detecting signs of hypertension using wearable sensors

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A Google Research blog post in the Health and Bioscience area describing detection of hypertension signs using wearable sensor data. The supplied content contains only the category label, so detailed methodology and results are not visible.

entry.title: Enhancing Local and Global Structure in Compressed AI Agent Memory

author.name: Henry Han

entry.summary: This paper studies compression of agent memory embeddings, evaluating both local fidelity (nearest neighbors surviving) and a new global fidelity metric over large fractions of the memory, since agents also consolidate, delete, and compare memories. At 96 bytes per passage, rescored binary codes achieve local fidelity of 0.97 but move 10.1 percent of passages across themes, while 8-bit PCA codes behave differently. The author proves bounds relating the fidelity band structure.

entry.title: Energy Measurement and Optimization of TinyML in Resource-Constrained Embedded Systems: A Systematic Mapping Study

author.name: Clariele Almeida, Renan Beserra, Rafael Moura, Danilo Ara\'ujo, Bruno Nogueira, S\'ergio Chevtchenko, Ermeson Andrade

entry.summary: This systematic mapping study organizes the heterogeneous literature on energy-aware TinyML, classifying models, energy-measurement methodologies, reported metrics, influencing factors, and optimization strategies for ML on microcontrollers and edge devices. It provides a structured overview to guide future energy-efficiency research in embedded ML. Useful reference work for the IoT/edge community.

entry.title: Improving Context-Shift Robustness of Convolutional Networks via Context-Regularized Cross-Entropy

author.name: Jinen Setpal, Chaoyue Liu

entry.summary: The paper proposes a training framework using spatial feature attribution to regularize CNNs toward object-relevant features rather than non-causal contextual cues, improving robustness under context shift. It also identifies a theoretical limitation of existing feature attribution methods as part of the derivation.

entry.title: Hamed Karimi wins ECML PKDD Test-of-Time Award

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Amazon senior applied scientist Hamed Karimi and colleagues won the 2026 ECML PKDD Test-of-Time Award for their 2016 paper proving linear convergence of gradient and proximal-gradient methods under the Polyak-Lojasiewicz condition. The paper organized a previously scattered area of ML optimization and became a standard analytic tool for new training methods.

entry.title: Technohybridism: Recursive Semantic Normalization in AI-Mediated Societies

author.name: Charalampos M. Liapis, Epameinondas Panagopoulos

entry.summary: This theory paper develops a sociotechnical account of how machine-generated language re-enters the communicative practices from which training data is drawn, introducing the concept of recursive semantic normalization and arguing that the proper unit of analysis is the hybrid human-AI semantic system (technohybridism). It draws on social theory, social epistemology, and philosophy of language. The topic — AI feedback loops reshaping language and institutions — is of growing importance to understanding model collapse and cultural dynamics.

entry.title: Performance metrics in machine learning: a scenario-based guide from the confusion matrix to calibration, regression and uncertainty

author.name: Mehmet Baygin, Sengul Dogan, Turker Tuncer

entry.summary: A methodological tutorial on how performance metrics can yield contradictory conclusions depending on class prevalence, thresholds, aggregation rules, and software conventions, illustrated through fifteen controlled scenarios spanning classification, calibration, regression, and uncertainty. It organizes 22 confusion-matrix metrics in a prevalence-coded map with 205 verification checks on released files. Useful pedagogically for practitioners misinterpreting metric results, but not original research.

entry.title: Joint Modeling of Conditional Mean and Variability in Multilevel Functional Data: Application to Postprandial Glucose Trajectories in the AEGIS Study

author.name: Yang Xiao, Francisco Gude, Marcos Matabuena

entry.summary: The authors propose a heteroskedastic functional mixed-effects regression framework that jointly models conditional mean and variance of repeated functional trajectories with participant-specific random effects in both components, plus a participant-level bootstrap for uncertainty. They apply it to postprandial glucose trajectories in a digital health study.

entry.title: VREgo: Consumer VR Headsets for Learning Robot Manipulation from Egocentric Demonstrations

author.name: Liuchuan Yu

entry.summary: VREgo trains manipulation policies from demonstrations recorded on consumer VR headsets, instantiated with EgoKit on a PICO 4 Ultra, using on-device head and hand tracking plus stereo object localization. Evaluation in simulation on two tabletop tasks shows PICO policies reach moderate success rates with 40 demonstrations, compared against Project Aria recordings.

entry.title: Gods of straight lines on graphs strike Starburst. I am shocked and puzzled.

author.name: Chapin Lenthall-Cleary

entry.summary: Hobby researchers report that SOTA LLM intelligence measured by Starburst, a puzzle game requiring inferring the physics of a fictional universe, has increased roughly linearly since the start of the reasoning era. The measurement derives from a bespoke human intelligence scale calibrated through a small number of playthroughs and intuition.

entry.title: The Two-Ledger Model: Transaction-Grain Cost Accounting for Multi-Agent AI Systems Across Clouds, Models, and Systems of Record

author.name: Vivek Acharya

entry.summary: This position-style paper formalizes the grain mismatch between settlement-grain AI billing data and enterprise transaction boundaries, and proposes a Two-Ledger Model pairing FOCUS-conformant billing data with a transaction-grain ledger. This lets enterprises answer what an individual order, claim, or case cost in AI.

entry.title: Don't Prompt Your Agents. Equip Them: Skillware as a Modular Standard for Sovereign, Auditable, and Deterministic Capability Execution for Logical Systems

author.name: Vladimiros Peilivanidis (ARPA Hellenic Logical Systems)

entry.summary: Skillware proposes replacing loose prompt-based skill definitions with modular, versioned software capability bundles that agents invoke deterministically, separating what an agent wants to do from how it is executed. The goal is to reduce context-window bloat, API cost, and brittle production behavior in autonomous agents. It is essentially a position/framework paper arguing for auditable, deterministic tool execution standards.

entry.title: Typed Knowledge over Constructive Institutions

author.name: Hans-Martin Will

entry.summary: Develops the theory of Eigenius, a persistent store of typed knowledge over constructive institutions, built on a dependent type theory with cumulative universes, inductive families, and intensional identity types. Unlike proof-irrelevant type theories for math or verification, it retains provenance: who established a claim, by which derivation or tool, and under which assumptions. Proof irrelevance is an explicit axiom with a witness rather than a kernel-level erasure.

entry.title: Evaluating Token Probabilities as Confidence Estimators in Human Behavior Simulations: A Case Study in Luxembourgish Next Like Prediction

author.name: Nils Schwager, Simon M\"unker, Alistair Plum, Achim Rettinger

entry.summary: The authors argue that evaluating LLMs as simulators of human behavior via accuracy alone is inadequate on noisy digital-trace data, and test whether open-weight token probabilities can serve as confidence estimates on a Luxembourgish next-like-prediction task. Using Ministral 3 (3B, 8B), an existing small model family, they find in-context-only models are overconfident and that calibration-based evaluation changes the picture. This is a useful caution for the growing field of LLM-based human behavior simulation.

entry.title: NutriVisRAG: Multimodal Exemplar Grounding for Nutrient Estimation with Vision-Language Models

author.name: Lubnaa Abdur Rahman, Ioannis Papathanail, Maria Panagiotou, Nefeli Dimitropoulou, Margret Har{\dh}ard\'ottir, Elisabeth J. den Brok, Bastiaan E. de Galan, Stavroula Georgia Mougiakakou

entry.summary: NutriVisRAG is a retrieval-augmented framework for nutrient estimation from free-living meal images that retrieves visually similar annotated meals and provides them as multimodal in-context exemplars to VLMs at inference time without task-specific fine-tuning. It is evaluated across four datasets, four VLMs, three retrieval encoders, and two prompting strategies. Grounding nutrition estimation on visually similar annotated examples addresses a practical healthcare AI need.

entry.title: Hybrid Machine Learning for Imbalanced Landing-Phase Safety Event Prediction from Flight Data

author.name: Taha Asghar, Bilal Mufti, Syed Qasim Zaheer, Luqman Ahmed

entry.summary: The paper presents an interpretable hybrid framework for predicting rare landing-phase safety events from imbalanced multivariate flight data, fusing LSTM autoencoder reconstruction-error descriptors with statistical flight-history features in a class-weighted XGBoost classifier. It distinguishes Normal, Specific, and other event classes across airport operating contexts.

entry.title: Data-Driven Modeling of Molten Chloride Corrosion Using Static Test Data

author.name: Md Mahmudul Hasan Pathik

entry.summary: This single-author work compiles 291 published molten chloride corrosion experiments into a structured dataset and builds an interpretable ML framework for corrosion-rate prediction, including a novel Chloride Salt Preparation Index to normalize heterogeneous salt conditions. A blended tree-based ensemble achieves the best consistent performance. It is a useful materials-science application aggregating scattered literature data.

entry.title: Ordering Multivariate Time Series by Volatility Memory: A Temporal Convolutional Approach to Volatility Heredity

author.name: Kaoutar El Azaar, Mohamed Hamlich, Moncef Garouani, Franck Ravat, Asmae Chakir, Mohamed Tabaa

entry.summary: QS-TCN combines statistical estimates of volatility memory (via quasi-maximum likelihood and the Matrix Pencil method) with temporal convolutional networks to order multivariate time series by directional dependence hidden in volatility dynamics. Structured filters derived from persistence estimates complement learned filters to compare directional evidence between variables. This targets relationships invisible to conditional-mean-based methods.

entry.title: Reproducing Kernel (Quasi-)Banach Spaces with the $\ell^p$ Coefficient Norms

author.name: Tianfang Wang, Guohui Song, Haizhang Zhang

entry.summary: This paper advances reproducing kernel Banach space theory by investigating the general l^p regularization framework, including the non-convex regime 0 < p < 1 where stronger sparsity approaches the l^0 pseudo-norm. The authors construct reproducing kernel quasi-Banach spaces with l^p quasi-norms and establish existence and sparsity results for interpolation and regularized learning.
