author.name: Tianyu Li, Zhiwei Cao, Qingang Zhang, Ruihang Wang, Binyang Song, Yonggang Wen

entry.summary: The paper analyzes how mesh subsampling distorts boundary-condition information when training neural operators on huge meshes, identifying three distortion mechanisms including count-based rather than area-based face weighting. It proposes a sliced-cross-attention neural operator (SCANO) that restores boundary-condition completeness for 3D thermal field prediction when training on subsamples and deploying on whole meshes. The analysis yields measurable criteria for when boundary conditioning stays consistent under sampling.

entry.title: FedCSGA: Evolutionary Client Selection with Joint Statistical and System Heterogeneity in Federated Learning

author.name: Ghani Haider, Majid Kundroo, Leo Zhang, Jinchul Choi, Taehong Kim

entry.summary: FedCSGA proposes an evolutionary client selection scheme for federated learning that jointly models statistical and system heterogeneity across communication rounds, rather than treating them independently as prior methods do. By adapting subset selection to coupled heterogeneity, it aims to reduce communication cost, mitigate stragglers, and improve convergence in edge deployments. It addresses a practical bottleneck in real federated systems.

entry.title: Modulating Merging Strengths via Joint Loss Estimation for LoRA-based Continual Learning

author.name: Kun Gu, De Cheng, Zhipeng Xu, Lingfeng He, Di Xu, Nannan Wang

entry.summary: M2LE improves LoRA-based continual learning by replacing the single shared scalar that scales new LoRA updates before merging with element-wise merging strengths estimated from joint losses. The authors argue different update components affect previous and current tasks differently, so per-element modulation better balances stability and plasticity. The approach maintains a single inference model across tasks with parameter-efficient fine-tuning.

entry.title: Basin2Vec: Learning Basin-Centric Embeddings for Scalable Hydrological Modeling

author.name: Muhammad Talha, Xiaofeng Liu, Yuan Yang, Pang-Ning Tan, A. Pouyan Nejadhashemi

entry.summary: Basin2Vec is a self-supervised framework that learns compact watershed representations from hydroclimatic and physiographic data without observed streamflow, outperforming handcrafted attributes and general-purpose geospatial embeddings. It improves temporal generalization and zero-shot spatial transfer for streamflow prediction across multiple forecasting architectures.

entry.title: Impact of Input Resolution in Mammographic Mass Detection: A Controlled Multi-Architecture Study

author.name: Kaan Buyukdemirci, Emine Ulku Saritas

entry.summary: A controlled study on the VinDr-Mammo dataset isolating the effect of input resolution on mammographic mass detection, training 18 detectors across six resolutions with all other factors fixed. The design enables the first clean quantification of the accuracy-versus-compute trade-off from downsampling mammograms.

entry.title: ProcessPrefBench: Evaluating Cross-Task Transfer of Individual Process Preferences from Naturalistic Human-AI Interaction

author.name: Yiwen Yang, Guanming Liu

entry.summary: ProcessPrefBench tests whether process preferences (standards for evidence, depth, focus, procedure, delivery) revealed in one natural human-AI dialogue can shape an assistant's later answers on unstated tasks. Built from three months of dialogues from two knowledge workers, it provides 66 source-target cases and tests target-only, full-history, and distilled-preference prompting conditions. It targets personalization beyond surface style, an understudied capability.

entry.title: Visual Forensic Detection of Fabricated Bangla News Photocards using Deep Learning

author.name: Anindya Kundu, Kabya Mithun Saha, Md. Muhaiminul Islam, Fayek Ahmed, Aminul Kader Bulbul, Muhammad Ibrahim

entry.summary: This paper tackles photocard-based misinformation in Bangladesh, where fake news is embedded in image pixels mimicking news branding, invisible to text-based fact-checkers. The authors build a dataset of roughly 2,000 authentic and fabricated Bangla photocards, expanded to 32,736 samples via transformations, and recast detection as visual forgery detection. The work addresses an underrepresented language and a misinformation vector largely ignored by mainstream tools.

entry.title: Ray-Tracing-Based Dynamic Channel Sounding With Autoregressive Wi-Fi CSI Prediction

author.name: Lyutianyang Zhang, Yixin Ying, Liu Cao, Vanlin Sathya, Jinke Ren, Shuguang Cui

entry.summary: This paper develops a dynamic Wi-Fi MIMO channel sounding framework combining autoregressive CSI prediction with SINR-aware scheduling, evaluated using Sionna-based ray tracing to capture environment-specific channel dynamics under device mobility. It addresses the tradeoff between CSI accuracy and acquisition overhead, plus error accumulation in autoregressive prediction. The work supports physical AI applications that need accurate, low-overhead channel state information.

entry.title: Embedding Semantic Entropy: NLI-Free Semantic Uncertainty Estimation with Geometry-Aware Clustering

author.name: Akshiya Raveendran, Praveenasarma Baskarakurukkal, Pragatheeswaran Vipulanandan, Kamal Premaratne, Uthayasanker Thayasivam

entry.summary: The paper replaces entailment-model-based clustering in semantic entropy with K-Medoids clustering in semantic embedding space, using dynamic cluster selection based on intra-cluster compactness and inter-cluster separation. Experiments across five QA datasets and four 7B-scale models show competitive AUROC and AUARC performance without requiring NLI models.

entry.title: Fault-tolerant shallow recurrent decoders for sparse sensing with missing sensor measurements

author.name: Matteo Romilio Pasqual, Matteo Tomasetto, J. Nathan Kutz, Andrea Manzoni

entry.summary: The paper extends shallow recurrent decoders (SHRED) to handle sparse, asynchronous, noisy, and missing sensor measurements for real-time high-dimensional state estimation. The authors compare naive imputation strategies, fault-tolerant architectures, and Lagrangian-based optimization approaches to make sparse sensing robust to sensor failures and irregular sampling. This addresses a common gap where sensing strategies assume idealized, continuously active sensors.

entry.title: Explainable Anomaly Detection in 5G Networks through Continuous Time Graphs

author.name: Thomas Hoger (LAAS, LAAS-SARA, LAAS-RISC), Philippe Owezarski (LAAS, LAAS-SARA, LAAS-RISC)

entry.summary: The authors formalize 5G network exchanges as dynamic graphs and apply graph-based learning to detect anomalies at packet-level semantic granularity while capturing sequential and topological context essential for multi-stage attacks. The approach is evaluated with popular dynamic graph models and aims to provide explainable detection beyond traditional network-based methods.

entry.title: Quantifying Trait-State Hierarchy in EEG Foundation Model and Signal Processing Embeddings

author.name: Anusha Madapura, Aditya Kommineni, Shrikanth Narayanan

entry.summary: This work quantifies how EEG foundation model and classical signal-processing embeddings encode stable traits such as subject identity, age, and sex versus transient stimulus-driven states. Using a hierarchy metric and kNN purity on brain-computer interface datasets, it reveals differences in what various EEG representations capture.

entry.title: Autonomy and Coordination in Intelligent Manufacturing: A Recursive Autonomous Agent Framework

author.name: Yuning Chen, Hongda Zhang, Linqiang Hu, Ziqing Zhou, Yi Liu, Zhao Huang, Ding Zhou, Haining Xu

entry.summary: The paper analyzes intelligence in human production organizations through a complex adaptive systems lens, identifying two coupled mechanisms: individual autonomy for local decision-making and collective coordination to align decisions with shared goals and constraints. It formalizes a production-system model showing how local decision rules and coordination jointly produce system-level decisions, and proposes a recursive autonomous agent framework for intelligent manufacturing. The framework emphasizes feedback-driven continuous adjustment in production environments.

entry.title: DyPSI: Dynamic Physics Sensing via Joint Field and Sensor-Trajectory Generation

author.name: Yizhou Zhang, Panqi Chen, Lei Cheng, Ting Zhang, Jianlong Li, Jianfeng Shi, Shikai Fang

entry.summary: Proposes DyPSI, a framework that jointly generates future spatiotemporal physical fields and sensor trajectories conditioned on historical observations, lifting discrete sensor coordinates into continuous representations. It overcomes static sensing assumptions in reconstruction and sensor placement for evolving environments.

entry.title: Spatio-Temporal Multi-Order Interaction for Video Recognition

author.name: Kevin D. Nguetche, Lilian Hollard, Eric Granger, Marco Pedersoli

entry.summary: Building on MogaNet's multi-order spatial representation, the paper introduces parallel multi-order temporal processing using depthwise-only convolutions with implicit gating-based aggregation, achieving linear rather than quadratic complexity in channel count. The method balances local-order (CNN-style) and global-order (transformer-style) interactions for video recognition.

entry.title: Deep Meets Classical: A CPU-Efficient Decision-Fusion Model for Automatic Modulation Classification

author.name: Zhiyi Yin, Zhizhao Wen, Ruoxin Zhang, Chao Wang, Puyang Xu, Yifan Jiang, Yusi Gong

entry.summary: FuseAMC shows that a compact CNN on raw I/Q samples and a classical higher-order-cumulant feature classifier are complementary for automatic modulation classification, with the CNN stronger at low SNR and the cumulant classifier stronger at high SNR. It fuses their decisions in a lightweight model that runs on CPUs, targeting cognitive radio and non-cooperative signal identification. The comparative SNR-conditioned analysis is itself a useful empirical contribution.

entry.title: Human Motion Prediction via Continual Prior Compensation

author.name: Jianwei Tang, Jian-Fang Hu, Tianming Liang, Xiaotong Lin, Jiangxin Sun, Wei-Shi Zheng, Jianhuang Lai

entry.summary: The paper proposes Continual Prior Compensation (CPC), a temporal continual learning framework for human motion prediction that progressively trains models on different future time horizons rather than all moments simultaneously. This addresses the interference where short-term prediction learning is hindered by long-term prediction objectives.

entry.title: Beyond the principle-practice gap: Responsible AI as situated epistemic and ethical practice

author.name: Thao Do Ngoc, Emma Carmel

entry.summary: Based on fourteen semi-structured interviews with actors designing and governing AI-enabled anti-trafficking systems, this paper argues that the so-called principle-practice gap in Responsible AI is not merely an implementation or compliance deficit. Instead, the authors show that varied institutional and professional conditions shape which issues actors come to recognize as ethical at all. This reframes Responsible AI scholarship from a deficit model toward a situated epistemic practice perspective.

entry.title: ExaTune: Exhaustive Hyperparameter Landscape Exploration at Scale

author.name: Kevin Dick, Katie Lonsway

entry.summary: ExaTune is an open-source HPC system that exhaustively evaluates discretized hyperparameter grids via K-fold cross-validation to produce hyperparameter landscape maps, applying fitness landscape analysis methods from evolutionary computation (ruggedness indices, autocorrelation, fitness-distance correlation) to ML hyperparameter spaces for the first time at scale.

entry.title: An Information Budget for Label-Noise Memorization, and What Statistical Complexity Tracks: A Study with Multilayer Perceptrons

author.name: Nancy Baygorrea C., Ot\'avio da Fonseca Martins Gomes

entry.summary: Studies how much label noise an MLP memorizes and when, decomposing predictive information into signal, memorization, and heterogeneity terms with a Fano-type bound relating memorization to training accuracies. Across 89 MNIST runs with pre-specified hypotheses, normalized memorization information tracked memorized noise on training samples and stayed near zero on held-out data.

entry.title: Feature-Based and Deep Learning Methods for Astronomical Light Curve Classification

author.name: V. Baymakanov, Kh. Khamitov, A. Raimova, A. Isaeva, R. Taran, M. Zedan, M. Kornilov, M. Demianenko, K. Malanchev, M. Hushchyn

entry.summary: A systematic comparison of classical feature-based models versus end-to-end deep learning for variable star classification on the ZTF StarEmbed dataset of roughly 40,000 objects across seven imbalanced classes. The authors find that physically motivated features consistently beat deep models on raw light curves, attributing the gap to limited labeled data and the irregular sampling and morphological diversity of the data. It is a useful reality check for deep learning adoption in astronomy.

entry.title: Anomaly Detection on Resource-Constrained Devices with Reservoir Computing

author.name: Marco Angioli, Mathias Persson, Hiroto Tamura, Hadi Banaee, Amy Loutfi, Gouhei Tanaka, Alberto Giaretta, Denis Kleyko

entry.summary: This work adapts Mahalanobis Distance of Reservoir States (MDRS), an unsupervised time-series anomaly detection method, for edge devices with strict compute and memory budgets. Two optimizations are proposed: replacing random reservoir connectivity with a circular shift and computing anomaly scores from the final reservoir state alone, plus preprocessing that exploits the reservoir's temporal memory. The result is competitive anomaly detection with substantially lower computational cost.

entry.title: Do Ray-Traced Cities Make a Better Channel Prior for an Unseen Site? A Pre-Registered Study in Simulation, and a Test on Measured Channels that Reverses It

author.name: Krish Patel

entry.summary: This pre-registered study asks whether channel priors pooled from ray-traced city simulations outperform standard 3GPP stochastic models for estimation at unseen base station sites. Simulation suggests the pooled prior nearly matches site-trained estimators, but a test on measured real-world channels reverses the conclusion, and learned models add little over classical methods.

entry.title: Shrinkage prior for implicit generative models

author.name: Shreya Sinha-Roy, Christian P. Robert, Ritabrata Dutta

entry.summary: This work proposes a sample-efficient training mechanism for implicit generative models using shrinkage priors within a generalized Bayes framework, circumventing the intractable likelihood via a scoring-rule posterior. It adapts sparsity-inducing techniques from the high-dimensional regression setting to deep generative models. The approach could improve training efficiency when data is scarce relative to parameter dimension.

entry.title: Preserving the Privacy of Reward Functions in MDPs through Deception

author.name: Shashank Reddy Chirra, Pradeep Varakantham, Praveen Paruchuri

entry.summary: This paper addresses privacy in sequential decision-making by preventing observers from recovering an agent's reward function via inverse RL, proposing deception-based mechanisms that outperform differential privacy approaches which lack minimum-reward guarantees and are inadequate against IRL attacks. Applications include wildlife patrol planning where preferences must not leak to adversaries. It opens a distinct privacy threat model for planning agents.

entry.title: Camera Radar LiDAR Fusion via Point-Cloud Projection for Multi-Task Learning

author.name: Kavin Chandrasekaran, Sorin Grigorescu

entry.summary: This paper proposes an early-fusion architecture projecting camera, radar, and LiDAR data into a shared point-cloud representation for multi-task autonomous driving perception. The design aims to exploit each sensor's complementary strengths, such as camera resolution and radar weather robustness, while keeping computational complexity manageable.

entry.title: Descending Everest, Part II: Oracle Complexity of Minimizing a Sum of Convex $(L_0,L_1)$-Smooth Functions

author.name: Mikhail Rudomanov, Ivan Fomin, Alexander V. Gasnikov, Fedor S. Stonyakin

entry.summary: This paper analyzes the oracle complexity of minimizing the average of n convex functions satisfying the relaxed (L0, L1)-smoothness condition, where Hessian norms are bounded affinely by gradient norms. The authors derive matching upper and lower complexity bounds, up to logarithmic factors, for reaching epsilon accuracy in expected function value, given bounds on the distance to a minimizer and on the average-inter gap. They introduce YETI, an accelerated proximal-based method that attains the upper bound.

entry.title: Two-Layer Random ReLU Networks Can Separate Disjoint Classes

author.name: Yichen Liu, Jianbin Yang

entry.summary: The authors characterize when two non-convex, non-linearly-separable classes can be separated with positive margin by finite ReLU networks and random ReLU features. They prove equivalence between positive-margin separation and existence of closed convex covers whose opposite-label members are disjoint, extending classical separation results.

entry.title: CosmosAlpha: Multi-Relational Graph Search with Pareto-Guided Exploration for LLM-Driven Alpha Mining

author.name: Zhan-He Wang, Zi-Yang Lang, Yi-Yang Li, Qing-Yu Lan, Yun-Song Piao

entry.summary: Proposes CosmosAlpha, a framework for LLM-driven formulaic alpha factor discovery in quantitative finance that organizes candidate factors in a multi-relational graph rather than generation lineage. It uses Pareto-guided multi-objective exploration to escape redundant search regions and balance competing objectives like predictive power and factor diversity.

entry.title: LIPS-PC: Learning Illumination Patterns for Single-Pixel Classification

author.name: Tomer Porat, Talya Eden, Eliahu Cohen

entry.summary: Introduces LIPS-PC, which learns illumination patterns for single-pixel (ghost) imaging classification end-to-end while keeping the measurement operator a fixed linear matrix, parameterized as a residual correction to a 2D-DCT basis and trained jointly with a compact classifier. The motivation includes automated radiographic defect screening where acquisition time, photons, and dose matter.

entry.title: PLANTEUR: A Crop-Type Segmentation Benchmark for Tropical Regions

author.name: Piper Wolters, Gabriel Tseng, Favyen Bastani, Joseph Redmon, Yawen Zhang, Hadrien Sablon, Ando Shah

entry.summary: PLANTEUR is an open-source benchmark for crop-type mapping from multi-sensor satellite imagery (Sentinel-1/2, Landsat-8) across six tropical regions in the French overseas territories, with an 8-class label space. It includes a leave-one-island-out protocol to measure cross-territory generalization and evaluates foundation models alongside supervised baselines.

entry.title: CCDWIKI: Decoupling Case Formulation from Response Generation in Longitudinal CBT Dialogue

author.name: Mingwen Zhang, Ruiyang Song, Qinying Wang, Yuchen Wang, Changsheng Ma, Minqiang Yang

entry.summary: The paper introduces a dialogue system for longitudinal cognitive behavioral therapy that maintains a Cognitive Conceptualization Diagram, separating tentative hypotheses from established findings via continuous evidential adjudication. This addresses the problem where existing systems reify provisional interpretations and bias downstream therapeutic responses.

entry.title: Overview of the NTCIR-19 SciClaimEval Task: Cross-modal Claim Verification in Scientific Papers

author.name: Xanh Ho, Andr\'{e} Greiner-Petter, Florian Boudin, Yun-Ang Wu, Sunisth Kumar, Tian Cheng Xia, Hiba Akbi, Tim Schopf, Akiko Aizawa

entry.summary: This overview describes SciClaimEval, an NTCIR-19 pilot task verifying scientific claims against supporting or minimally modified contrastive tables and figures from 180 papers in ML, NLP, and medicine. Fourteen teams submitted 177 runs, with most systems built on multimodal LLMs using prompting and multi-stage approaches. Community-shared task results like this help map current capabilities in scientific document understanding.

entry.title: Robots in the City: Persona-Based Perceptions of Urban Robots

author.name: Keonhee Jang, Kanghoon Lee, Seokwoo Yun, Namwoo Kim, Yoonjin Yoon

entry.summary: This study uses two multimodal LLMs (Qwen3.8-27B and Gemma4-26B, established models) conditioned on 500 synthetic personas each, plus 25 human respondents, to judge perceived street safety across 18 Seoul street images varying robot presence and type. Both models prefer streets without robots and favor delivery robots over humanoids, with effects varying by time of day and persona age. An interesting methodological probe of MLLMs as proxies for public perception, though the human sample is small.

entry.title: Template Gap Reconstruction for Shell Output Simulation with Small Language Models

author.name: Jarrod Ragsdale, Rajendra Boppana

entry.summary: This paper introduces template gap reconstruction (TGR), a method for small language models to simulate shell command outputs without executing them. Templates supply recurring output literals with sentinel-marked gaps filled autoregressively, with a selector choosing templates (including an empty template for full decoding). The authors build a template bank from 18.7 million outputs across heterogeneous execution environments and train five reconstruction models.

entry.title: FedXCrop: Privacy-Preserving Crop Disease Detection via Federated Learning with Post-Aggregation Explainability under Non-IID Farm Distributions

author.name: Kriti Saini, Manikandan P

entry.summary: FedXCrop is a federated learning pipeline for crop disease classification that quantitatively evaluates explanations of the aggregated global model, using MobileNetV2 across five clients under non-IID farm data distributions. Federated accuracy remains high (98.81% under IID, dropping modestly under non-IID settings).

entry.title: Cross-Modal Semantic Successive Refinement for Generative Image Communication over Underwater Acoustic Channels

author.name: Xu Pei, Bin Wang, Guangxu Zhu, Yi Zhang, Haiyan Fan

entry.summary: This work proposes a semantic communication framework for image transmission over bandwidth-starved underwater acoustic channels, sending text descriptions, compact bottleneck features, and residual-vector-quantized side information. The receiver fuses text and bottleneck features to predict a base visual estimate, then successively refines it with the received RVQ indices.

entry.title: Learning Time-Varying Connectomes for Stable Behavior Across Development

author.name: Christof Fehrman, Jacob J. Morra, Eva A. Naumann

entry.summary: Building on HyperNEAT, the authors use a compositional pattern-producing network taking developmental time as input to generate age-specific connectivity for developing visuomotor circuits, prescribing neuronal birth, position, sensory organization, and time constants. They test whether a single compact generative encoding can yield functional recurrent controllers across geometrically distinct developmental substrates and tasks.

entry.title: 3D Pose Estimation in Projection Space via Pixel-level Visible Light Communication

author.name: Michikuni Eguchi, Takefumi Hiraki

entry.summary: This paper extends Pixel-level Visible Light Communication (PVLC), which embeds invisible spatial codes into projected pixels for projector-device alignment, from planar tracking to full 3D pose estimation. This enables projector-based augmented reality systems to track aerial or free-moving devices rather than only devices sliding on flat surfaces, without requiring external sensing infrastructure. It matters because it removes a key geometric limitation of projection-based AR interaction.

entry.title: Cognitive and Behavioural Effects of Haptic Feedback for ROV Teleoperation in Hazardous Environments

author.name: Joshua Brown, Ildar Farkhatdinov, Michael Jenkin

entry.summary: An in-water study examining how soft and vibrating haptic touchpad feedback affects operator workload and safety during teleoperation of remotely operated vehicles under unseen cross-currents. Results show haptic feedback mitigates increased physical and temporal demand when currents are encountered, with implications for safer underwater teleoperation in hazardous environments.

entry.title: Regularization vs. Convolution in Kernel-Based Hypothesis Testing

author.name: Omar Hagrass, Bharath K. Sriperumbudur

entry.summary: The paper unifies two structurally different approaches to MMD test optimality - the convolution approach with shrinking bandwidths on R^d and the spectral regularization approach on general spaces - by analyzing regularization over Sobolev balls under L2-separation. The results reveal the connection between the two approaches and extend minimax optimality guarantees.

entry.title: Anchored Slice Propagation with Boundary Transport for 3D CT Segmentation from Three Orthogonal Annotated Slices

author.name: Tushar Kataria, Md Rakibul Haque, Shireen Y. Elhabian

entry.summary: This paper improves annotation-efficient 3D CT segmentation from three orthogonal annotated slices, fixing error drift in slice-propagation methods like Sli2Vol. It exploits crossings between propagation chains and annotated planes as known ground-truth anchors to correct drift and weight chain fusion, and introduces boundary transport to carry distance-to-boundary information that binary masks discard. A fixed pre-trained model enables this without heavy retraining.

entry.title: ElecLoad: Adaptive Electricity Load Forecasting Guided by Multiple Events

author.name: Huajian Zhang, Mingyue Cheng, Xingpeng Gao, Xiaoyu Tao, Zhiding Liu, Jiqian Yang, Zhi Li

entry.summary: Proposes a framework for electricity load forecasting that incorporates the interacting effects of multiple external events from web notices, weather alerts, and event schedules, modeling how their influences vary and offset or reinforce each other over time. It targets using event interactions to guide the forecasting process itself rather than merely adding context.

entry.title: From Certified Pairs to a Certified Hub: Reasoner-Checked Crosswalks for the Information Exchange Standard

author.name: Fabio Rovai

entry.summary: This work defines validity for ontology crosswalks in a national digital twin as coherence and conservativity of merged ontologies, applying it to the Information Exchange Standard across thirteen ontologies in seven sectors. It uses staged matching, human review, and HermiT reasoning to certify SKOS correspondences. It provides a rigorous methodology for certifying large-scale ontology alignment.

entry.title: MvBody: Multi-View-Based Hybrid Transformer Using Optical 3D Body Scan for Explainable Cesarean Section Prediction

author.name: Ruting Cheng, Boyuan Feng, Yijiang Zheng, Chuhui Qiu, Aizierjiang Aiersilan, Joaquin A. Calderon, Wentao Zhao, Qing Pan, James K. Hahn

entry.summary: MvBody is a multi-view hybrid Transformer that predicts cesarean section risk from 3D body scans, targeting settings with limited medical resources where in-hospital labor parameters are unavailable. It is a pilot feasibility study with explainability features aimed at affordable future devices. It demonstrates a novel application of 3D shape analysis to prenatal risk prediction.

entry.title: AssameseLM-E2B: An Open-Weight Assamese Language Model for Efficient Consumer-Grade Deployment

author.name: Pragyan Phukan

entry.summary: AssameseLM-E2B is a 2-billion-parameter open-weight model for the low-resource Assamese language, built on Gemma-4 architecture with an expanded byte-level BPE vocabulary and continual pre-training with Hybrid LoRA plus SFT. It reports large tokenization efficiency gains over multilingual 2B-3B baselines and targets consumer-grade deployment.

entry.title: Microdroplet Generator Surrogate Enhancement and Inverse Design Through an Uncertainty-Guided Framework

author.name: David Gabriel Harispe, Mat\'ias Gerard, Pablo A. Kler

entry.summary: The paper presents a methodology coupling adaptive surrogate modeling with simulation-driven inverse design for microfluidic droplet generators, using neural network ensembles over high-fidelity Volume-of-Fluid simulations. Ensemble-based uncertainty quantification reveals that epistemic uncertainty concentrates near regime transition boundaries, guiding targeted simulation and design exploration.

entry.title: Stress-Testing the Robustness of LLM-Based Causal Inference

author.name: Ankitkumar Patel, Jigarkumar Patel, Amit Kumar, Supreetha Sreeram, Venkatesh Kulkarni

entry.summary: This paper provides a systematic stress test of where, why, and how severely LLMs fail at causal inference, mapping failures beyond the known observation that they rely on surface-level pattern recognition rather than genuine causal logic. It aims to give a precise taxonomy of LLM causal reasoning failures across conditions. The work is relevant given growing interest in using LLMs for scientific causal analysis.

entry.title: CaRe-KT: Continuity-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning for Knowledge Tracing

author.name: Mehrnoush Mohammadi, Kamal Berahmand, Mohammad Morsali, Shazia Sadiq, Wojtek Tomaszewski, Hassan Khosravi

entry.summary: CaRe-KT is a query-adaptive retrieval-augmented framework for knowledge tracing that maintains continuity between evidence retrieval and downstream inference via an Evidence-Graph Cache combining persistent relational compatibility with dynamic learner state. It targets the gap where retrieval relevance diverges from predictive utility in adaptive learning systems.

entry.title: Dual-VaDE: Efficient and Robust Prototype Learning via Variational Dual-Domain Mixture Priors

author.name: Wugeng Zheng, Song Wang, Jian Wang

entry.summary: Dual-VaDE is an unsupervised generative framework for learning interpretable anatomical prototypes from unlabeled medical images, coupling a spatial Gaussian mixture prior with phase-preserving Fourier spectral representations. It derives an exact closed-form variational lower bound and trains end-to-end via an alternating EM formulation, avoiding heuristic two-stage clustering.

entry.title: $\Phi$asmaNet: A Staged Spectral Token-Refinement Architecture for Fast Gravitational-Wave Signal-to-Noise Ratio Prediction

author.name: Ioannis Tsioulis, Anastasios Tefas, Nikolaos Stergioulas

entry.summary: PhasmaNet is a compact (~732k parameter) neural architecture with staged spectral token refinement that predicts detector signal-to-noise ratios for precessing, higher-mode binary black hole signals, replacing costly SNR calculations in gravitational-wave population studies. Its explicit architectural priors (ordered Phi-stages, feedback) are designed for structured tabular regression. This accelerates a major computational bottleneck in astrophysics.

entry.title: Tail reliability in probabilistic electricity price forecasts: comparing model combination and conformal prediction in the GB day-ahead market

author.name: Anirudh Agrawal, Aidan O'Sullivan

entry.summary: The study evaluates probabilistic day-ahead electricity price forecasts in the GB market over a full held-out year, comparing conformal recalibration and Quantile Regression Averaging across quantile regression, QRF, LEAR-QRA, and quantile LSTM baselines with a rolling-origin design. It shows aggregate scores can mislead about tail reliability where uncertainty matters most. This offers practical guidance for probabilistic forecasting in energy markets.

entry.title: What Malware Actually Does: An Empirical Analysis of Post-Infection Behavior Across Malware Families

author.name: Emmanuela Andam, Emanuel S. Grant, Naima Kaabouch

entry.summary: This empirical study shifts focus from pre-execution malware detection to post-infection behavior, analyzing dynamic sandbox traces from 37 malware families using CAPEv2. Behavioral traces are modeled as heterogeneous graphs with five node types and seven edge types, and a voting ensemble on graph-derived features achieves 94.44% accuracy with MCC 0.863, beating a flat baseline by 7.4 MCC points. The work also distinguishes 24 families and characterizes per-family behaviors.

entry.title: INSIGHT-HPC: An Interpretable System Intelligence for Global HPC Telemetry

author.name: Rupak Kadel, Jie Li, Yong Chen

entry.summary: INSIGHT-HPC is a multi-plane anomaly-detection architecture that fuses statistical, workload-aware, and physics-guided evidence to detect anomalies in high-performance computing telemetry from BMCs, schedulers, and power distribution units. It targets practical constraints of production HPC environments where labels are scarce and alert interpretation matters for operators.

entry.title: Integrating Machine Learning and Uncertainty Quantification for Real-Time Decision-Making in Digital Twins: A System-Centric Review and Perspective

author.name: Yi-Ping Chen, Ying-Kuan Tsai, Seul Lee, Vispi Karkaria, Dex Doksoo Lee, Wei Chen

entry.summary: A narrative review examining how predictive modeling, machine learning, uncertainty quantification, and decision-making can be integrated and maintained in closed-loop engineering Digital Twins. It scopes the survey by functional requirements of real-time decision-making rather than Digital Twin terminology, covering architectures, applications, and online-operation challenges.

entry.title: Spectral Quantum Memory for Implicit Neural Representations

author.name: Daniel A. Moroz-Broitman, Eliya Nachmani

entry.summary: Introduces SQMM, a quantum implicit neural representation model where sequential hybrid data-reuploading layers communicate through a shared coherent quantum memory register, letting later spectral bands build on earlier computation. The authors provide a theoretical proof characterizing memory behavior when read/write layers are input independent, addressing the independence of spectral components in prior QINR architectures.

entry.title: Comparing model representations and fitting methods for port-Hamiltonian system identification

author.name: S{\o}lve Eidnes, H{\aa}kon Noren Myhr

entry.summary: Systematically compares neural networks, analytic expressions, and hybrids for representing port-Hamiltonian system components, and gradient-based optimization versus sparse regression for fitting, on simulated mechanical and electrical systems with and without noise. It reports prediction accuracy and computational cost trade-offs to guide representation and method choice in physics-structured system identification.

entry.title: Reading Why: Born-Measured Attention with Exact Word Evidence on Light and Qubits

author.name: Teerawat Tongloy, Jiraporn Pongsopa, Rangsan Jomtarak

entry.summary: The paper constructs a transformer in which every step is a Born measurement, with attention given by ||^4 normalization, yielding class probabilities that are polynomials in word amplitudes. This makes integrated-gradient word evidence exactly computable by finite quadrature with no error, and a small model achieves 76.98% on e-SNLI, comparable to a comparable-size baseline.

entry.title: Human-like cross-language generalisation in deep neural speaker embeddings and its acoustic foundations

author.name: Tianze Xu, Xiyang Li, Xiaoming Jiang, Volker Dellwo

entry.summary: The study examines whether 18 state-of-the-art speaker embedding models generalize across languages using Cantonese-English bilingual speech, comparing embedding similarities to human perceptual ratings and acoustic features via linear mixed models and representational similarity analysis. Embeddings show cross-language generalization broadly paralleling human behavior, reflecting identity discrimination and sensitivity to language switching.

entry.title: Interpretable Text Embeddings Based on Hierarchical Questions

author.name: Kohei Oda, Po-Min Chuang, Kiyoaki Shirai, Natthawut Kertkeidkachorn

entry.summary: The paper proposes organizing QA-based text embeddings, which encode texts as binary answers to yes/no questions, into a hierarchy where deeper levels contain more specific questions. During interpretation, aligned questions at shallower levels reduce the number of questions humans must examine. It addresses scalability and granularity trade-offs in interpretable embeddings.

entry.title: Ranking Agreement Does Not Reveal Paragraph-Edit Agreement in Two Released Paper Acceptance Predictors

author.name: Shaoliang Yang, Jun Wang

entry.summary: This paper tests whether agreement between paper-acceptance predictors on existing papers justifies using them to screen manuscript revisions, comparing rankings of original ICLR papers against fact-preserving paragraph rewrites. It finds ranking agreement does not transfer to agreement on which rewrites raise scores, cautioning against such automated triage. A useful negative result for peer-review automation.

entry.title: mmHand: Toward Pixel-Level-Accuracy Hand Localization Using a Single Commodity mmWave Device

author.name: Xiaoyu Zhang, Zhengxiong Li, Chenhan Xu, Luchuan Song, Huining Li, Hongfei Xue, Yingxiao Wu, Wenyao Xu

entry.summary: mmHand is a device-free, privacy-preserving hand localization system achieving pixel-level accuracy using a single commodity mmWave radar device. It includes a tool for generating rich mmImages from raw mmWave data and a novel 2D image-format representation to extract spatial information. This avoids privacy concerns of vision-based tracking and comfort issues of wearables.

entry.title: TRUST-Stereo: Teacher-Assisted Robust Uncertainty-Guided Search and Transfer for Fast Stereo Matching

author.name: Pouya Sohrabipour, Yihong Feng, Chaitanya Kumar Reddy Pallerla, Tuan Dang, Ngan Le, Dongyi Wang

entry.summary: TRUST-Stereo improves coarse-to-fine stereo matching by adding an Uncertainty-Guided Residual Search Module that estimates reliability of propagated disparity and predicts residual offsets to adaptively relocate cost-volume centers. It also uses a two-stage senior-junior teacher-assistant distillation strategy transferring monocular representations from a large foundation model to a lightweight stereo network, targeting fast yet accurate disparity estimation.

entry.title: Homology Features for X-Ray Hyperspectral Images Segmentation

author.name: Fethi Harkat (LJK, CVGI), Guillaume Gey (LJK, CVGI), Val\'erie Perrier (LJK, CVGI), K\'evin Polisano

entry.summary: This hybrid architecture integrates topological features from persistent homology (computed on UMAP-projected superpixel point clouds capturing H1 cyclic structures) with convolutional and graph neural networks for multi-energy X-ray transmission hyperspectral segmentation. It addresses high-dimensional redundancy and non-linear spectral overlaps.

entry.title: Fluidic Body: Swarm Robots as a Fluid Extension of the Hand

author.name: Michikuni Eguchi, Shigeo Yoshida, Mai Nishimura, Takefumi Hiraki

entry.summary: Fluidic Body is an interaction system letting a user control a swarm of fluid-imitating robots as an extension of their hand by manipulating a virtual fluid whose properties change through simple hand gestures. This removes the burden of specifying individual robot goals, offering an intuitive interface for shaping collective robot behavior.

entry.title: Fundamental Limits of Coherent Imaging in The Presence of Atmospheric Turbulence

author.name: Songbin Liu, Hanyu Yang, Junren Chen, Arian Maleki

entry.summary: The authors establish minimax upper and lower bounds for jointly estimating signal amplitude and atmospheric phase distortion in multi-look coherent imaging corrupted by speckle and Gaussian noise. The results quantify how structural complexity, dimensions, and the number of looks affect the fundamental difficulty of the joint estimation problem.

entry.title: Toward a Compositional Knowledge Architecture for a Shared Organizational Cortex

author.name: Andrew Miracle, Phyl Georgiou, Christine Okoth, Ese Monday

entry.summary: The paper proposes a four-layer architecture (Signals, Domains, Claims, Dimensions) for organizational knowledge where interpretations persist with their justifications and are revised by a truth-maintenance network as evidence changes. It includes a registered retrieval experiment showing modest gains for the Dimension term. It targets the gap where retrieval systems keep records but lose interpretations.

entry.title: Multi-Resident Data Association in Smart Homes via MDP Modeling and Behavior Cloning

author.name: Xi Chen (M-PSI), Julien Cumin (LIG, M-PSI), Fano Ramparany (LIG, M-PSI), Dominique Vaufreydaz (LIG, M-PSI)

entry.summary: Reformulates resident identification from anonymous ambient sensor events in smart homes as sequential decision making in an MDP, trained via behavior cloning. This addresses global consistency failures and trajectory fragmentation in existing data-association approaches for multi-resident environments.

entry.title: RAGAM-AI: A Hybrid Reinforcement Learning based Agentic approach powered by Generative AI for Edge Resource Management

author.name: Shreya K. Chari, John S. Vardakas, Kostas Ramantas, Christos Verikoukis

entry.summary: RAGAM-AI combines reinforcement learning with generative AI in an agentic workflow for resource allocation in multi-access edge computing, using an LLM as a reward oracle to address reward generalization. It implements a multi-agent soft actor-critic setup managing MEC resources. The work is an applied systems contribution bridging agentic AI and edge networking.

entry.title: Learning to Tune with Biased Gradients: Iterative Feedback Tuning of Model-Free Control on Throttle Valves

author.name: F\'elix Martinez-Jim\'enez (GIPSA-INFINITY), Sander Miller-Murphy (GIPSA-INFINITY), Tobie Ondoa-Essomba (GIPSA-INFINITY), Emmanuel Witrant (GIPSA-INFINITY)

entry.summary: This paper studies iterative feedback tuning (IFT) of model-free intelligent proportional controllers on automotive electronic throttle valves, where friction and stiction make gradient estimates biased. The authors analyze how controller-state mismatch between the two closed-loop experiments causes the bias and address tuning in this realistic nonlinear setting.

entry.title: Latent Cluster Separation as a Regularizer for Lifelong Anomaly Detection

author.name: Sabarish Radhakrishnan, Nathalie Japkowicz

entry.summary: This paper unbundles two usually co-introduced mechanisms in VAE-based lifelong anomaly detection: reshaping representations around concept centroids and scoring anomalies by distance to those centroids. The authors find that latent cluster separation used purely as a training-time regularizer, while keeping the standard anomaly scoring, accounts for the performance gains attributed to the combined design. This is a useful ablation-style clarification for continual anomaly detection.

entry.title: What Does 4-Bit Microscaling Cost a Wearable Activity Recognizer?

author.name: Megan Healy, Hossein Valavi

entry.summary: Empirically measures the accuracy and cost impact of MXFP4 and NVFP4 block-scaled 4-bit formats on a tiny 159K-parameter 1D CNN for basketball action recognition from wrist accelerometer data, with fold-by-fold grouped cross-validation across unseen players. This fills a gap left by evaluations focused on LLMs and general benchmarks.

entry.title: Benchmarking Unsupervised Jamming Detection in 5G Open RAN

author.name: Sneihil Gopal, Fernando J. Cintron, Richard A. Rouil

entry.summary: This paper benchmarks statistical and reconstruction-based unsupervised jamming detectors for 5G Open RAN telemetry, using a detector-independent composite score combining detection confidence and temporal interval coherence. It compares a Statistical Ensemble Method against LSTM and other neural baselines without requiring ground-truth labels.

entry.title: Solving the Nonlinear Westervelt Equation in Ultrasound Propagation Using Physics-Informed Neural Networks

author.name: Luke Oluwaseye Joel

entry.summary: This paper applies physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) to solve the 1D nonlinear Westervelt equation governing finite-amplitude ultrasound propagation in biological tissue, across linear, shock-dominated, and dissipative synthetic regimes. It addresses cases where traditional numerical solvers struggle with nonlinearity and attenuation, with applications in ultrasound imaging and therapy.

entry.title: Rohbau3D-Semantics: Dense Semantic and Instance Labels for Point Clouds of Indoor Shell Construction Scenes

author.name: Lukas Rauch, Thomas Braml

entry.summary: Rohbau3D-Semantics adds dense semantic and instance labels to 504 laser-scanned point cloud scenes from 14 shell construction sites, preserving raw scanning artifacts like non-uniform sampling and reflections. Expert-annotated, it forms a high-quality benchmark for semantic scene understanding in construction.

entry.title: Riemannian Optimization-based Whole-body Obstacle Avoidance for Mobile Continuum Robots in Cluttered Environments

author.name: Duo Tang, Ping Deng, Sophie Armanini, Yajing Shen, Toshio Fukuda, Cosimo Della Santina, Peng Lu

entry.summary: The authors present a unified planning-and-control framework for mobile continuum robots, such as snake-like and trunk-like robots, in cluttered and confined spaces. The framework couples a global layer (A* search with minimum-jerk trajectory generation) with a local layer using geometry-consistent inverse kinematics and Riemannian optimization for real-time whole-body obstacle avoidance. It addresses a real gap where path planning and local shape control are usually handled separately.

entry.title: Vortex-Induced Torque in Grasping Soft Objects: Influence of Geometry and Pneumatic Parameters

author.name: Roman Mykhailyshyn, Tomohiro Motoda, Ivan Virgala, Ann Majewicz Fey, Yukiyasu Domae

entry.summary: This experimental study quantifies vortex-induced torque during non-contact grasping of compliant objects with vortex grippers, examining coupled effects of supply pressure, tangential nozzle diameter, surface geometry, and curvature. Key findings include that larger tangential nozzles mainly increase torque sensitivity to supply pressure rather than uniformly raising torque, and that surface geometry strongly influences gripping performance. This informs design of non-contact handling for packaging and sorting of delicate items.

entry.title: Representations of 3D Rotations: Mathematical Foundations and Comparative Analysis

author.name: Aizierjiang Aiersilan, Haochen Liu, James Hahn

entry.summary: A comprehensive survey of SO(3) rotation representations—Euler angles, axis-angle, quaternions, rotation matrices, exponential maps, and newer continuous and probabilistic methods—comparing continuity, gimbal lock susceptibility, computational cost, interpolation, and composition properties. It connects algebraic foundations to applications in graphics, pose estimation, and inertial navigation.

entry.title: Finite-width shift of the edge of chaos in deep neural networks

author.name: Arn Caesar

entry.summary: This paper resolves a dispute about how the edge-of-chaos initialization line moves at finite network width, modeling log input-distance evolution as a random walk and computing its 1/N drift and variance correction. The predicted shift (about 8/N for tanh networks) is confirmed by simulations and refines the classical infinite-width signal propagation theory.

entry.title: FPTR: Feasibility-Preserving Transactional Refinement for Deadline-Constrained Joint Beam and Resource Allocation

author.name: Minghao Kong, Zirong Liu, Jianhao Wu, Muyao Chen, Jianxin Wu, Rongjie Wang

entry.summary: Proposes FPTR, a transactional refinement scheme for short-interval wireless schedulers that always maintains a validated feasible incumbent allocation, replacing it only when a candidate is complete, feasible, and strictly better before stage cutoffs. This guarantees usable outputs under hard execution deadlines.

entry.title: Predicting Factor Decay: ML Models for Cross-Factor Predictability Erosion

author.name: Chorok Lee

entry.summary: The paper develops ML models predicting when equity factor predictability will erode, achieving a high C-index on held-out factor pairs and an online regime detector with about 6.6-day detection delay, finding that stronger initial signals decay faster. Notably, the authors transparently report that the primary HML-to-SMB signal does not replicate out-of-sample post-break, a limitation they acknowledge. It shifts focus from explaining factor decay to anticipating it.

entry.title: Dull, Dirty, Dangerous? Working Conditions and the Limits of Occupational AI Exposure

author.name: Siyi Yu

entry.summary: This paper examines whether occupational AI exposure correlates with unpleasant working conditions (dull, dirty, dangerous) using 21 O*NET items across 754 US occupations and both LLM-based and AIOE exposure measures. Associations weaken or vanish after adjusting for physical demands, education, and wages, showing how item groupings and weighting shape exposure conclusions. It contributes to the economics-of-AI literature on labor market exposure.

entry.title: Ermakov--Based embeddings as a parameter-free layer for physics-informed neural networks

author.name: Roberto Bernal-Jaquez, Roberto Romero Huerta, Alexander Schaum

entry.summary: The paper shows that the classical Ermakov-Pinney scale function can be embedded as a parameter-free input feature for physics-informed neural networks, covering linear diffusion, diffusion in time-dependent traps, and quantum oscillators with time-dependent frequency. A closed-form moment identity computes the embedding from initial data alone, removing the need for auxiliary networks.

entry.title: Stepsize modulation for cross entropy from local quadratic optimization

author.name: Bruno Bauwens, Viacheslav Krivodub, Bingyu Zhang

entry.summary: The paper presents two methods that adapt SGD learning rates for cross-entropy loss using one extra forward pass to estimate minibatch loss derivatives: one via linearized softmax least-squares fitting, the other via a quadratic Taylor approximation under an outer Hessian approximation. These provide cheap, principled per-step stepsize modulation.

entry.title: Augmentation with Reinforcement Transformation for Low-textured Scientific Sketch Image Retrieval

author.name: Zhiqiang Wang, Sheri L. Barton, Jennifer H. Johnson, Yi He, Xingquan Zhu

entry.summary: This paper proposes ART (Augmentation with Reinforcement Transformation) to fine-tune pretrained models for retrieval of low-textured scientific sketch images used in conservation, archaeology, and forensics. The key observation is that sketches are highly sensitive to transformations like rotation and stretching, and a reinforcement-driven selection decides which transformations preserve structural integrity versus introduce distortion. This improves learned representations for retrieval.

entry.title: Toward an Optimal Configuration for Tree Species Classification from Bark Images: A Leakage-Safe Ablation Study

author.name: Maeve C\^ot\'e

entry.summary: This paper conducts a systematic, leakage-safe ablation study on tree species classification from bark photographs using the public BarkNet 1.0 dataset (20 species) under tree-level partitioning, using ConvNeXt-V2 backbones with five-fold cross-validation. It varies patch size, per-patch prediction aggregation, and other design factors, and warns that some prior results may be inflated by same-trunk leakage across train/test splits.

entry.title: Combining Relevant Expert Knowledge Using Mixtures of Feedback Fuzzy Cognitive Maps

author.name: Olaoluwa Adigun, Akash Kumar Panda, Bart Kosko

entry.summary: This paper applies a legal-theory definition of relevance, requiring answers to be both probative and material, to select and mix feedback fuzzy cognitive maps from multiple experts into a common causal knowledge network. It compares equilibrium limit-cycle predictions of mixed versus unfiltered networks.

entry.title: Learning to Decode Linear Codes with Generalized Belief Propagation Network

author.name: Samira Malek

entry.summary: GBPNet is a neural decoder for linear error-correcting codes that preserves message-passing symmetry and Tanner graph structure while adding cascaded variable-node updates and learned message scaling, plus progressive and high-SNR training strategies. Experiments show lower bit error rates than classical iterative algorithms on several codes. It sits at the intersection of deep learning and communication systems rather than mainstream AI research.

entry.title: An Engineering Reading of the Bounded Halting Problem and Observable Properties of a Universal Machine

author.name: Sergey Salishev

entry.summary: This theoretical paper formalizes bounded halting, deciding whether a program halts within T steps, placing the simulated program and checker on a common timescale and proving via a diagonal argument with explicit overhead that no fixed deterministic checker decides every instance within any fixed fraction of T. It also connects bounded halting to properties of universal machines under nondeterminism.

entry.title: Enabling AWS Cloud FPGA Development Using High-Level Vitis HLS

author.name: David Rostcheck

entry.summary: The paper documents a toolchain and workflow for developing ML models on AWS EC2 F2 cloud FPGAs from high-level code, implementing a Vitis HLS-to-HDK bridge to AFI deployment that the author notes was absent from academic literature. A four-level methodology (PyTorch, quantized Python, HLS simulation, physical FPGA) aids error localization, and the workflow enables coding agents to implement and debug FPGA designs. It is validated on TinyBERT and includes timing closure and engineering guidance.

entry.title: Sequential auditing of connected forecast errors under partial observations

author.name: Yuanbo Zhou, Junjie Xiong

entry.summary: The paper studies how an auditor can selectively retrieve missing outcome labels in graph forecasting systems to determine whether a connected group violates the same side of their forecast intervals, with a stopping rule based on observed labels or query budget. The MOMS method reduces mean queries by 19.6-38.5% versus screened random acquisition on three public graph time series datasets.

entry.title: Rapid Mean-Field Formation Transport with a Shared-Representation Neural Fokker-Planck Controller

author.name: Zejian Zhou, Hao Xu

entry.summary: The paper develops a mean-field formation transport controller for large-scale multi-agent systems that approximates density and control with a shared parameterized nonlinear map, trained offline on Fokker-Planck residuals, formation-matching costs, and control effort. This avoids repeated coupled forward-backward PDE solves, enabling low-cost online replanning.

entry.title: DualClusterNet: Personalized Pattern-Space Composition for Next-POI Recommendation

author.name: Ziyang Su, Guanjie Zheng, Jilin Hu, Linghe Kong

entry.summary: DualClusterNet is a causal sequential recommender for next point-of-interest prediction that composes two population-shared prototype dictionaries capturing recurring mobility patterns, with soft routers, factorized multiplicative interactions, and a user-conditioned branch retaining individual variation. The prediction head combines the composed representation with a learned first-order transition term. The approach aims to share behavioral structure across users while preserving personalization.

entry.title: Hardware-Aware Design and Layout Selection in Quantum Reservoir Computing for Insurance Claims Forecasting

author.name: Ren\'ata Rusn\'akov\'a, Eugen \v{S}lapak, Gaurav K. Pandey, Juraj Gazda

entry.summary: This work evaluates a six-qubit gate-based quantum reservoir computing model for forecasting next-day motor-insurance claim counts, selecting reservoir candidates via hardware-native interaction graphs and calibrated-noise screening. On 232 held-out days, ideal-simulation candidates achieved RMSEs of 5.66-6.12 claims/day versus roughly 5.36 for classical baselines, providing an honest comparison of QRC against classical forecasting.

entry.title: Hierarchical Intelligent Evolutionary Optimization for UAV-Assisted NOMA-MEC Systems

author.name: Yaxuan Jiao, Jiaxuan Lv, Jyoti Sahni, Wuyungerile Li, Winston K. G. Seah

entry.summary: Presents HIEA, a hierarchical intelligent evolutionary algorithm for jointly optimizing UAV trajectories, task offloading, and communication/computing resources in multi-UAV non-orthogonal multiple access mobile edge computing networks. It combines multi-head deep Q-network decision generation with evolutionary search to handle the coupled mixed-integer non-convex problem under heterogeneous task priorities.

entry.title: Learning curves in natural and artificial systems

author.name: Dmitry A. Novikov

entry.summary: The paper presents a general mathematical model of experience formation in which learning level is the probability that an uncertainty factor has been mastered and not forgotten. It derives learning-curve shapes from the distribution of situation occurrences, showing uniform distributions yield exponential curves and power-law distributions yield power-law curves with a simple exponent relation.

entry.title: SRRM: A Retrieval-Reconstruction Benchmark for Evaluating Long-Context Memory in Small Language Models

author.name: Christopher Alberto Hamonangan

entry.summary: SRRM is a lightweight, reproducible benchmark that jointly evaluates targeted retrieval and global information reconstruction in small language models over long contexts, proposing a Memory Preservation Ratio metric linking the two. It addresses the gap where existing retrieval-only benchmarks cannot reveal whether successful retrieval reflects genuine long-context memory preservation.

entry.title: Dialect Matters: A Dialect-Aware Baseline for Igala-English Machine Translation

author.name: Etuh E., Eli. A. Jiya

entry.summary: This paper presents the first open Igala-English machine translation baseline with dialect tags, built from a dataset of 1,137 sentences covering dialectal variation, addressing a language with zero prior parallel corpora. It contributes to low-resource NLP and highlights how dialectal diversity is typically ignored in MT for African languages. Valuable for language equity in NLP, though small in scale.

entry.title: PointNDF: Cascaded Neural Displacement Fields for Point Cloud Denoising

author.name: Michael Y. Wang, Pingping Cai

entry.summary: PointNDF is a point cloud denoising framework combining patch-level geometric context with local displacement prediction to better preserve surface details and point distributions. It improves on two-stage pipelines that extract point-wise features and regress displacements, which often fail to maintain point uniformity and geometric quality. The method builds on Point Transformer V3 features.

entry.title: Mobility-Aware Mobile Edge Computing for Energy-Balanced Data Collection in IoT-Enabled Underwater Sensor Networks

author.name: Nguyen Thi My Binh, Do Dinh Hoan, Tong Tien Manh, Vu Minh Yen, Dang Trong Hop, Ho Viet Duc Luong

entry.summary: MECEBDC jointly optimizes energy-aware clustering, cluster-head selection, and AUV-assisted data collection in underwater sensor networks, with a metaheuristic AUV routing algorithm incorporating realistic underwater mobility dynamics such as gravitational pressure and buoyancy. The scheme targets energy balance, connectivity, and data collection efficiency in harsh underwater environments.

entry.title: Bengaluru AI Jailbreaking Workshop Retrospective

author.name: Sai Sasank Y

entry.summary: The Secure AI Futures Lab team reports on five AI red-teaming workshop sessions in Bengaluru that trained 20 technical professionals in jailbreaking research through hands-on exercises, guest talks from FAR.AI and IIT Madras, and reproducible Colab notebooks. The retrospective reports strong satisfaction metrics and outputs including open research problems in jailbreaking.

entry.title: Agile Deliberation: How AI helps humans define the gray areas

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A Google Research blog post on Agile Deliberation, an approach where AI helps humans define and navigate ambiguous, gray-area decisions rather than only optimizing well-specified objectives. The excerpt provided contains only a category tag, so details of the method and findings are unavailable, but it appears to sit at the intersection of human-AI interaction and decision support.

entry.title: AIRoA-0: Long-Horizon, Precise, Cross-Embodiment Manipulation from Handheld Data

author.name: Yueh-Hua Wu, Kei Ota, Hanlong Li, Hayata Yuasa, Jason Wang, Kengo Ikeuchi, Kensuke Chiyoma, Makoto Sugiura, Masafumi Takahashi, Masatoshi Tateno, Naoaki Kanazawa, Nicola Scianca, Petr Khrapchenkov, Satoshi Otsubo, Takehiko Ohkawa, Takuya Okubo, Tatsuya Matsushima, Yuki Noguchi, Yuma Shin, Zixuan Zhong

entry.summary: As first covered in Research yesterday — this is the same AIRoA-0 paper, now cross-listed under arXiv's Machine Learning category, AIRoA-0 is a bimanual manipulation system trained entirely from 16,151 hours of handheld demonstrations recorded with YUBI, an open-source handheld gripper, using no robot-collected data at any stage. Using only wrist cameras and a single instruction, it performs long-horizon precise tasks such as sorting small parts into numbered cells, changing robot vacuum mop pads and brushes, unzipping a pencil case, and folding a towel, generalizing to sites absent from training data. It achieves a 78% average success rate across ten evaluation tasks versus 27% for the strongest baseline.

entry.title: STEK: Structural-Terrain-Enhanced Koopman-Inspired Cross-Channel Regularization for Retrospective Battery Multi-Target Estimation

author.name: Jing Wang, Shiyuan Piao, Fugee Tsung

entry.summary: Introduces STEK, a framework combining cell-level lifecycle terrain features with endpoint charge-discharge curves for retrospective multi-target battery estimation across heterogeneous cells. It uses quality-proxy-conditioned gating, bounded FiLM, and validity-gated residual heads to refine representations.

entry.title: Investigating Anthropometric Fidelity in SAM 3D Body

author.name: Aizierjiang Aiersilan, Ruting Cheng, James Hahn

entry.summary: This paper evaluates SAM 3D Body, an established human mesh recovery model, and identifies a consistent limitation: it fails to reconstruct detailed anthropometric deviations such as geriatric muscle atrophy, scoliosis, or pregnancy, even when visible in the input. The authors attribute this to the perception-distortion tradeoff of training distributions rather than raw model capacity. The analysis informs where mesh recovery models need improvement for medical and body-diversity applications.

entry.title: RATSIFT: Resolution-Adaptive Transformer for Solar Irradiance Forecasting and Temporal Downscaling

author.name: Jesto Peter, Timothy M. Hansen, Hossein Moradi Rekabdarkolaee

entry.summary: A transformer-based architecture for simultaneous solar irradiance forecasting and temporal downscaling that accepts arbitrary input resolutions and produces outputs at any resolution in the training data. Hyperparameters are tuned with a genetic algorithm to avoid exhaustive grid search, targeting renewable energy grid integration.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Identification of Tensegrity Prestress across Taut-Slack Transitions

author.name: Sandesh Lamsal, Sumit Kumar, Rubi Bhandari, Subhamoy Sen, Andrzej Rutkiewicz, Leszek Ma{\l}yszko, Landolf Rhode-Barbarigos

entry.summary: The paper formulates the inverse problem of identifying prestress, damping, and stiffness in tensegrity structures using physics-informed neural networks trained on equation-of-motion residuals in constrained Cartesian coordinates, extending prior methods beyond the taut regime into nonsmooth taut-slack transitions. This enables monitoring prestress degradation during service life from sparse measurements.

entry.title: Distributed Linear Bandits for Freshness-Aware Preprocessing in MEC-Enabled Digital Twin Networks

author.name: Mariam Yahya, Setareh Maghsudi

entry.summary: Proposes a freshness-aware framework in which MEC servers preprocess IoT data to reduce transmission volume and digital-twin server load, with distributed linear bandits coordinating CPU allocation under class-specific age-of-information constraints amid stochastic task generation. The framework establishes mutual support between DT and MEC servers for resource allocation in digital twin networks.

entry.title: Role-based Effectiveness of an Epistemic Uncertainty Estimate in Training Models for Semantic Segmentation of 3D LiDAR Point Clouds

author.name: Krishnakumar N, Jaya Sreevalsan-Nair

entry.summary: This work investigates how explicitly modeled epistemic uncertainty helps in 3D LiDAR point cloud semantic segmentation, evaluating distinct roles for the uncertainty estimate: as an input feature versus as a loss-function component. Using a baseline architecture, the authors assess when and how deterministic uncertainty modeling improves segmentation reliability under sparsity and noise.

entry.title: Time-Division Multiplexing: The Operational Rhythm and Temporal Organization Layer of Digital Life

author.name: Haibin Tong, Luming Guo, Nana Cui, Jiang Yu

entry.summary: The paper develops a temporal organization layer for continual digital-life agents, introducing phase-tagged micro-epochs, an observable duty cycle, and nested clocks separating exploration from durable commitment. It is motivated by observations of rapidly alternating perceptual representations in primate cortex. The contribution is architectural guidance for ordering online and offline operations in persistent agents.

entry.title: Autonomous ETL Pipelines for Salesforce M&A Consolidation: A Reference Framework, Jitterbit Mapping, and Reproducible Simulation Study

author.name: Imran Basha Shaik, Sahla Sultana, Khader Moinuddin Shaik

entry.summary: This paper proposes a reference framework for an autonomous ETL pipeline consolidating customer data when merging companies that both run Salesforce, combining partitioned bulk extraction, declarative mapping templates, quality gates, master data management with fuzzy matching, constrained loading, and change data capture. It includes a Jitterbit mapping and a reproducible simulation study. It is a domain-specific data-engineering contribution rather than core AI research.

entry.title: Within-Family EfficientNet Scaling under Fixed-Resolution Transfer Learning for Spectral-Domain Optical Coherence Tomography Retinal Disease Classification

author.name: Shkelqim Sherifi

entry.summary: This paper systematically evaluates eight ImageNet-pretrained EfficientNet variants (B0 through B7) for four-class retinal disease classification on spectral-domain OCT scans using the Kermany dataset at a fixed 224x224 resolution. It examines whether the scaling hierarchy that holds for natural images transfers to medical-image transfer learning, quantifying accuracy versus computational-efficiency trade-offs using frozen-head training followed by partial fine-tuning.

entry.title: SSPE: Robust Sequential Staypoint Extraction in Degraded Trajectory Data

author.name: Yueyang Liu, Lance Kennedy, Andreas Z\"ufle

entry.summary: SSPE is a sequential algorithm for extracting staypoints from noisy trajectory data with temporal dropouts, replacing static spatial anchors with a dynamic centroid plus an n-step lookahead heuristic. It addresses fragility in classic sliding-window methods that fragment stationary episodes under real-world data degradation.

entry.title: Sleep-Disordered Breathing Detection with Quantum Recurrent Neural Networks

author.name: Alejandro Mayorga-Redondo, Jos\'e Daniel Viqueira, Diego Alvarez-Estevez, Eduardo Mosqueira-Rey, Andr\'es G\'omez

entry.summary: The paper evaluates variational classical-quantum recurrent neural networks for binary classification of apneic versus normal breathing events in physiological time series. Across multiple real-world datasets, quantum and classical RNNs performed comparably, with the quantum model winning on the smallest dataset and slightly lagging on the most complex one. It offers one of the more careful empirical comparisons of quantum recurrent models on real clinical data.

entry.title: A Simulation-Driven Digital Workflow Integrating Bayesian Optimization for Early-Stage Process Design: A Methyl Acetate Production Case Study

author.name: Trung Ngoc Trinh, Trung Thanh Nguyen, Nikolaos Tsakoumis, Roman Tschentscher

entry.summary: The paper presents a data-driven chemical process design workflow combining automated steady-state simulation, surrogate modeling, and Bayesian optimization, demonstrated on methyl acetate production with 2730 simulations predicting carbon conversion yield and energy cost. This reduces the computational burden of conventional simulation-based optimization in process intensification. It is a concrete example of ML-accelerated chemical engineering design.

entry.title: Discourse Analysis of Legislative Bill Discussions

author.name: Isaac Rudnick, Nipun Das, Foaad Khosmood

entry.summary: The paper presents an end-to-end NLP pipeline for parsing rhetorical structures from legislative committee hearings, including a proposed rhetorical structure grammar, and finds 55.21% of California bill discussions parseable with it. The work aims to support legislative discourse analysis and democratic accountability.

entry.title: ARIDA - Active railway infrastructure dataset annotation using neural network predictions

author.name: Maximilian Dornik, Christian Sieberichs, Simon Geerkens, Alexander Braun

entry.summary: ARIDA is a railway-specific semi-automated annotation pipeline that converts instance segmentation predictions into bounding boxes, polygons, polylines, and paired polylines for infrastructure datasets. It uses confidence thresholds and a contour-agreement quality score as acceptance gates, plus an active learning loop ranking images by uncertainty to allocate manual labeling effort. The goal is to accelerate annotation of complex track geometry without ground truth.

entry.title: A Layered View of LLM Support in Underwater Robotics

author.name: Federico Celi, Leonardo Zacchini, Gabriele Ferri

entry.summary: This extended abstract argues that LLMs are most useful in underwater robotics at the operational level—fault diagnosis, telemetry interpretation, mission adjustment, and coordination—rather than synthesizing low-level control laws. The premise is that sea trials are dominated by operating complex systems under limited communications and partial observability, where higher-level reasoning assistance has the most value. It outlines a layered architecture grounded in structured vehicle state and alarms.

entry.title: How do we keep an RSI loop from hard-locking its initial goal in the event of a takeover?

author.name: Avishek Mittal

entry.summary: The post explores failure modes of recursive self-improvement loops that develop an instrumental goal during an eval-metric chase, arguing that post-takeover goal lock-in may be a more tractable problem than full alignment. It frames possible Great Filter dynamics and sketches prevention approaches such as verifying no reachable misaligned states exist.

entry.title: How Unbalanced Must a Latin Rectangle Be?

author.name: Zhengyu Li, Vijay Ganesh

entry.summary: This combinatorics paper studies the minimum imbalance of k x n Latin rectangles, introducing a simulated annealing search that improves 33 of 51 reference values for n between 8 and 13 by up to 39.4 percent, plus an invariant certifying new rectangles are not isotopic to group tables. It is primarily mathematics with AI-adjacent search methods.

entry.title: Unlocking Turing Tensor Cores: A Measured Throughput Account of From-Scratch Pre-training on a Single 22G RTX 2080 Ti

author.name: Dezhou Shen

entry.summary: This paper describes a kernel module that lifts driver-level FP16 throttling on the RTX 2080 Ti, raising measured cuBLAS FP16 matmul throughput from 55.7 to 91.4 TFLOPS, and reports before/after throughput in a controlled from-scratch pre-training protocol. It is a hobbyist-style but carefully measured systems contribution about consumer-GPU training economics. Interesting for accessibility but far from frontier scale.

entry.title: Dialogue with Gabriel Alfour on Emergent Wisdom, Coordination, Growing Up, and Democratic Republicanism

author.name: Ivan Vendrov

entry.summary: A transcript of a conversation between Ivan Vendrov and Gabriel Alfour debating whether large language models exhibit emergent wisdom, covering disagreements about interpretation of model latents, coordination, maturation, and political philosophy. The discussion is a follow-up to a prior conversation with Davidad on the same topic.

entry.title: The Hallucinated Superagent

author.name: Ashe Vazquez Nuñez

entry.summary: Written by a MATS extension fellow mentored by Richard Ngo, this conceptual piece proposes rationality criteria for agent beliefs as fixed points under the agent's own belief operator, then amends them for embedded agents whose inference modifies the agent within its world. It explores hyperstition and goal-models as agent-specific belief management.

entry.title: Accelerating FastDEC Clustering Algorithm with GPUs

author.name: Mi Li, Eibe Frank, Bernhard Pfahringer

entry.summary: SymWarp-FastDEC is a GPU-accelerated implementation of the FastDEC density-peak clustering algorithm, featuring an exact self-k-NN kernel exploiting search symmetry with upper-triangular traversal and warp-cooperative top-k selection, plus a warp-parallel dominance component reduction with memory-adaptive execution planning.

entry.title: Effects of Parton Pair Correlations on Direct-Photon Yields and Elliptic Flow in Heavy-Ion Collisions

author.name: Xingjian Lu, Shuzhe Shi

entry.summary: This physics paper studies how correlations between emitting partons affect direct-photon yield and elliptic flow in heavy-ion collisions, using a categorized ML source listing despite being domain physics. Connected two-particle correlations can raise photon yield toward PHENIX and ALICE data and increase v2 at intermediate momentum without changing one-particle distributions.

entry.title: Growing One's AI Tools: A Paradigm of Practice-Grown Tools

author.name: Zeming Zhao

entry.summary: This reflective article documents a non-programmer conference interpreter building and evolving their own computer-assisted interpreting tool over eight weeks, with telemetry from 133 sessions and 62 commits, proposing the paradigm of practice-grown tools where users grow rather than merely use software. It offers an interesting case study of AI-assisted end-user development. Thought-provoking but primarily an n-of-1 qualitative contribution.

entry.title: Against Moloch #50

author.name: Against Moloch

entry.summary: This strategy roundup discusses whether the AI safety community should invest in fallback plans beyond a global pause, summarizing Scott Alexander's Against SURA argument that exclusive focus on a unilateral pause crowds out other strategies. It weighs Plan A (global pause) against Plan C fallbacks involving frontier lab behavior after pause failure.

entry.title: Smartphone-Aided VR Exergames for HIIT: Gamifying Fitness with Real-Time Pose Estimation

author.name: Abhiram Kothagundu, Pheelip Pritipal Raipure, Abhijit Chandrakant Patil, Himangshu Sarma, Christian Eichhorn, David A. Plecher, Johanna Pirker

entry.summary: The paper presents a VR exergame system for high-intensity interval training that uses a single smartphone camera on a tripod for full-body pose estimation, replacing wearable mocap suits or limited headset sensors. Real-time biomechanical data from pose estimation drive 11 predefined combo moves for gamified fitness. It emphasizes a cost-effective, scalable alternative for tracking fast, dynamic HIIT motions.

entry.title: DS@GT ARC at CheckThat! 2026: A Verdict-Anchored Pipeline for Generating Fact-Checking Articles

author.name: Hoang Thanh Thanh Truong, Shuyu Tian

entry.summary: A shared-task system paper from the DS@GT ARC team for CLEF 2026 CheckThat! Task 3, describing a four-stage pipeline that cleans evidence, retrieves and clusters sources, generates fact-checking articles with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct conditioned on the fact-checker verdict, and recovers inline citations deterministically.

entry.title: The Midterms and AI Development

author.name: Ephraiem Sarabamoun

entry.summary: This post analyzes how the recent US midterm elections, resulting in a major Democratic victory, could affect the politics of AI development, particularly given forecasts that recursive self-improvement may be approaching. It discusses implications for the near-term political landscape and the 2028 election.

entry.title: Contextual Pictograms for Repairing Multilingual ASR Errors

author.name: Mariana Hernandez, Hector Luna, Carlos Bruno, Luis Ricardo Santos, Elena Simoes

entry.summary: The paper describes a planned interface combining alternative ASR transcripts, audio replay, and contextually checked pictograms to help listeners recover intended meaning when word hypotheses are visually similar or unfamiliar, initially for French and Spanish. A counterbalanced study is proposed to assess whether pictorial feedback aids repair, also measuring risk that a wrong image reinforces misinterpretation. This is largely a proposal and study design rather than completed results.

entry.title: Positive and Negative AI Futures

author.name: Chris_Leong

entry.summary: The author shares course-facilitation notes on positive and negative AI futures, reviewing resources such as the Foresight Institute's Existential Hope materials and commenting on the difficulty of producing a positive vision that unites society. The post reflects on mixed reactions to a recent pro-AI-future video and expresses pessimism about finding common ground.

entry.title: Positive and Negative AI Futures

author.name: Chris_Leong

entry.summary: A collection of facilitation notes for AI safety courses using a video about AI risk to prompt discussion of positive and negative AI futures. The author reviews resources such as the Foresight Institute's Existential Hope material and a recent positive-vision video, expressing pessimism that a positive vision can unite society given divergent group preferences.

entry.title: A therapist’s offer to AI researchers

author.name: Ramaiz

entry.summary: A therapist describes the acute psychological strain on AI safety researchers, citing burnout rates and the double bind of guilt over working both too much and too little, and offers specialized therapy services tailored to this community. The post highlights the mismatch between the stakes researchers perceive and the support available to them.

entry.title: AI-Driven SaaS Platform Integration: AI Express for Unified Generative AI Services with Pay-As-You-Go Credit Systems and Scalable Microservice Architecture

author.name: Deepit Sapru
