Using conditional centering, empirical deviations form a martingale, enabling variance-adaptive tests and finite-sample Hoeffding-style guarantees.

entry.title: Variational Learning with Lie Group Exponential Families

author.name: Eren Mehmet K{\i}ral, Thomas M\"ollenhoff, Koichi Tojo, Mohammad Emtiyaz Khan, Kenichi Bannai

entry.summary: The paper extends a Lie group framework for variational Bayesian learning in deep networks to general Lie groups, giving explicit connections to natural-gradient variational methods such as Bayesian learning rule. Lie group parameterizations naturally handle constraints and yield low-variance gradient estimators.

entry.title: Sheaf-MPNN: A Library for Sheaf Neural Networks as Message Passing

author.name: Alessio Borgi, Mario Severino, Luke Braithwaite, Steve Azzolin, R\'emi Bourgerie, Olga Zaghen, Emanuele Mule, Riccardo Ali, Leo Minh Kustermann, Edoardo Coppola, Antonio Purificato, Stefano Fiorini, Christopher Irwin, Filippo Spiga, Fabrizio Silvestri, Michael Bronstein, Pietro Li\`o

entry.summary: Sheaf-MPNN is a PyTorch Geometric library reformulating sheaf neural network diffusion as local incidence-wise transport instead of assembling a global sheaf Laplacian matrix, reducing memory and compute overhead. Sheaf networks give nodes and edges their own vector spaces to address oversmoothing and heterophilic graphs.

entry.title: On the Complexity of Finite-Sum Nonconvex-Strongly-Concave Minimax Optimization with Exact Proximal Oracles

author.name: Yuxing Peng, Zhiqing Tang, Weijia Jia

entry.summary: This paper establishes lower bounds for finite-sum nonconvex-strongly-concave minimax problems, showing that neither unrestricted adaptivity nor exact component proximal access improves polynomial complexity. The proximal oracles considered expose global saddle points of regularized component problems, directions invisible to plain gradients. The result tightens our understanding of what is achievable in adversarial training and distributionally robust optimization.

entry.title: Cool Graphs: Active Property Search Towards Quantum Nano-Refrigerators

author.name: Sofia Blyufer, Amir Kleiner, Uri Peskin

entry.summary: The authors combine a Graph Variational Autoencoder with an uncertainty-driven active learning loop to search the exponentially large configuration space of quantum nano-refrigerators, identifying energy-absorbing configurations in electronic junctions. The GVAE maps physical parameters into a smooth latent space separating cooling from dissipative regimes, drastically reducing the number of expensive quantum-chemical computations needed. A nice example of ML accelerating materials and quantum device discovery.

entry.title: Federated Transfer Learning for Medical Image Classification under Mixed Skew

author.name: Alexandre G. Leclercq, S\'ebastien Bougleux, Aur\'elien Corroyer-Dulmont, Romain H\'erault

entry.summary: The paper proposes a personalized federated learning method for medical imaging that handles mixed skew (feature, label, concept, and quantity shifts across institutions) and starts from a pretrained foundation model rather than training from scratch, which is essential given limited per-site data. This addresses privacy-constrained multicenter medical AI realistically. Deployable personalized FL for healthcare is a significant practical need.

entry.title: NovoCRF: Globally Normalized De Novo Peptide Sequencing on a Prefix-Mass Lattice

author.name: Rui Qiao, Lei Xin, Baozhen Shan

entry.summary: NovoCRF is a conditional random field whose states are prefix masses, restricting candidate paths to peptides within a tight mass tolerance, with edge scores from physics-derived ion-match features and globally normalized training over all mass-feasible peptides. It claims to be the first de novo peptide sequencing method trained with exact normalization over all mass-feasible candidates.

entry.title: A local orchestration harness for molecular design with foundation models

author.name: Sakib Mostafa, Md Atik Ahamed, James Zou, Lei Xing, Md Tauhidul Islam

entry.summary: MolCrew is a locally deployable system that coordinates specialized molecular models for generation, description, endpoint prediction, and editing through a language-model orchestrator and RDKit validation, keeping molecular data under local control. It addresses data privacy, cross-task model integration, and chemical constraint verification in molecular design workflows.

entry.title: Co-Occurrence Priors Override Visual Spatial Evidence: Understanding False Alarms in Vision-Language Models for Construction Struck-By Hazard Detection

author.name: Xiaoshan Zhou

entry.summary: Using 355 counterfactual worker-excavator scene pairs, this study probes Qwen2.5-VL-7B and InternVL3.5-8B to show that false hazard alarms in construction safety VLMs stem from learned co-occurrence priors overriding spatial evidence, despite correct entity recognition and spatial relation encoding. The work combines behavioral analysis, representation probing, causal interventions, and decision correction.

entry.title: Conditional independence and graphical models for rankings

author.name: Aritz P\'erez

entry.summary: The paper introduces relative rank models, a probabilistic framework based on structured coarsenings of the ranking space that relax mutual-exclusivity constraints while preserving relative order information. This yields a well-defined notion of conditional independence for rankings and enables graphical model structure over ranking distributions.

entry.title: PROSE: Preservation-Constrained Selective Editing for Guilty Bias in Legal Judgment Prediction

author.name: Yimeng Wang, Zeyuan Tian, Xinyu Wang, Danyang Gao, Chenglei Shen, Zhongxiang Sun, Lei La, Weijie Yu

entry.summary: The paper studies guilty bias in legal judgment prediction models, which retain guilty verdicts even when a decisive legal condition is removed, and introduces CAIL-MC, a dataset of 11,478 matched case pairs across 261 Chinese criminal charges. PROSE performs preservation-constrained selective editing so unsupported verdicts change while supported ones remain stable.

entry.title: Computational Phenomenology of Borderline Personality Disorder: A Comparative Evaluation of LLM-Simulated Expert Personas and Human Clinical Experts

author.name: Marcin Moskalewicz, Anna Sterna, Karolina Dro\.zd\.z, Kacper Dudzic, Marek Pokropski, Paula Flores

entry.summary: This cross-listed study evaluates whether GPT, Gemini, and Claude models can support qualitative phenomenological analysis of clinical life-story interviews with BPD inpatients, using blinded expert judges, semantic congruence measures, and neural methods across two studies. It finds generally strong expert-rated validity for AI-generated thematic analysis relative to human clinical experts.

entry.title: SettleSplat: Monocular Gaussian Mapping under In-View Scene Changes

author.name: Anh Thuan Tran, Xiyun Song, Yubin Zhou, Heather Yu, Jana Kosecka, Liang Peng

entry.summary: SettleSplat tackles in-view scene changes in online 3D Gaussian mapping, where objects are manipulated in front of the camera and transition from transient distractors to persistent parts of the scene. This setting is distinct from prior work on out-of-view or cross-capture dynamics and requires disentangling transient from persistent change.

entry.title: Mitigating Spatial Blindness in Multiple Instance Learning for Whole-Slide Image Analysis

author.name: Xiangyu Li, Jincheng Li, Xing Xie, Bin Guan, Shaohua Kevin Zhou, Rui Yan, Ran Su

entry.summary: Identifies spatial blindness in whole-slide MIL, where models predict from tissue composition while ignoring spatial organization, and proposes ResTopoMIL: freeze a composition predictor, then train a graph residual pathway with a coordinate-reassignment separation loss. Includes permutation and information analyses plus a controlled spatial task to validate the mechanism.

entry.title: ReXMo: End-to-End Video Character Replacement with Expression and Motion Preservation

author.name: Hualiang Wei, Wenhui Li

entry.summary: An end-to-end framework for video character replacement supporting single-, multi-, and selective-character scenarios, using paired triplet supervision with synthetic driving data and an in-context diffusion transformer conditioned on driving videos, reference identities, and text. Aims to preserve expressions, motion, and scene dynamics better than masked pose-guided methods.

entry.title: Lightweight graph transformers for clutter and target classification in automotive radar

author.name: Adrian Gheorghiu, Tunc Alkanat, Ashish Pandharipande

entry.summary: The paper proposes TGTNet, tiny graph transformer models that classify radar detections as clutter versus stationary or moving targets on the public RadarScenes dataset. The models match state-of-the-art precision and recall while being one to two orders of magnitude smaller with significantly faster inference.

entry.title: CoReMatch: Recurrent Continuous Coordinate Refinement for Real-Time Robotic Feature Matching

author.name: Robert J. Wang, Charles Ling, Boyu Wang

entry.summary: Presents CoReMatch, a recurrent feature-matching framework that refines correspondences directly in continuous coordinate space instead of predicting confidence on fixed grids, using a Deep Aggregated Transformer for global context at the coarse stage. The approach targets robotic perception tasks like SLAM, localization, and navigation with real-time requirements.

entry.title: Mass Scaling Laws for Energy-Optimal Horizontal Multirotor Flight

author.name: Ayush Patnaik, Nicolas Michel, Leonard Baursfeld, Davide Scaramuzza, Xinfan Lin

entry.summary: The paper derives closed-form scaling relationships between energy-optimal steady horizontal flight behavior of a multicopter and its vehicle mass, validated experimentally on two multirotor platforms. These relations enable energy-aware flight planning under frequent payload-induced mass variation, addressing range and endurance bottlenecks in real drone applications.

entry.title: PACT: Pose-Robust Actuation Co-Design for Tendon-Driven Robotic Hands

author.name: Prashant Kumar, Rachael Granberry, Taylor Niehues, Andrew A. Stanley, Gabe Pirie

entry.summary: PACT is a co-design framework that jointly optimizes tendon routing, moment arms, and capstan dimensions for tendon-driven robotic hands under pose-dependent force requirements and bandwidth constraints, using a feasible-force formulation with equilibrium enforcement at all joints. It avoids the sequential design trap where force capability and joint speed trade off against each other.

entry.title: AI Safety at the Frontier: Paper Highlights of October 2026

author.name: gasteigerjo

entry.summary: A monthly digest summarizing frontier AI safety research highlights, including claims that superposition may be practically irrelevant for interpretability, OpenAI's expanded misalignment monitoring flagging 80% of past incidents, rogue self-deployment risk from cheap 26B-capable devices, LLM-simulated control evaluations, gradient routing to remove reward hacks, and Claude agents finding finetuning datasets that evade monitors.

entry.title: Exact Optimality Certification of QPLIB 2096 through Complete Set Partitioning

author.name: Jingyang Du, Zixiong Yi, Yang Shen

entry.summary: The authors provide an exact computational proof that the QPLIB_2096 nonconvex quadratic instance has global minimum 7,025,720, via a coefficient-level reconstruction into a set-partitioning formulation over 25 items, with the solution approach explored using ZiYor, a self-evolving AI system. This is a rare exact optimality certificate for a hard benchmark instance.

entry.title: RAHC: Rule-Augmented Hyper-Relational Knowledge Graph Completion for Materials Synthesis

author.name: Jiawei Sun, Sijia Xu, Zihan Chen, Zhengyi Yang

entry.summary: RAHC addresses recovering missing synthesis conditions in materials science via rule-augmented hyper-relational knowledge graph completion. It builds a traceable rule catalog from training records and retrieved literature, retrieves rules per query-candidate pair, and combines graph structure with explicit domain regularities to complete single-slot and joint multi-slot synthesis conditions.

entry.title: When the Consumer Is an Agent: Execution-Grounded Service-Level Agreements

author.name: Michal Orzechowski, Renata G. Slota, Jacek Kitowski

entry.summary: The paper introduces execution-grounded completion contracts, where an independent control plane verifies deadline-bound service-state predicates to determine whether an LLM agent's task is truly complete in asynchronous distributed services. Evaluation on a live multi-provider data service shows accepted completions can miss deadlines and the contracts improve accountability and recovery.

entry.title: Shuffled OPSD: When Semantic Consistency Hurts On-Policy Self-Distillation?

author.name: Qingyuan Zheng, Zhihao Dou

entry.summary: The paper asks whether preserving the semantic structure of the shared problem statement helps on-policy self-distillation, and shows that shuffling the question words while keeping the teacher-only worked example intact can surprisingly improve distillation of reasoning ability. This challenges an intuitive design assumption in OPSD.

entry.title: Physical Experience Builds Continual Spatial World Models

author.name: Yuhang Sun

entry.summary: Studies how continual physical experience can improve spatial world models over time using a physics-grounded dynamic maze that separates recurring spatial changes from action consequences, with a cross-episode Spatial Change Memory learning relations among environmental transformations. The work addresses how agents can update prior expectations without letting them override current physical evidence.

entry.title: Counterexample-driven autonomous research with application to excess radiated energy in a Z-pinch

author.name: Bowen Zhu, Jian Wu

entry.summary: Simjecture is an open-source framework where LLM agents pursue human-defined physical conjectures through counterexample-driven falsification and prospective hypothesis repair, using computational physics as an executable testbed. It is demonstrated on excess radiated energy in Z-pinch plasma physics.

entry.title: What Is This Memory Useful For? Measuring Task-Conditioned Utility in Long-Term Agent Memory

author.name: Chih-Hsuan Yang, Anjir Ahmed Chowdhury, Feng Yan, Rajeev Thakur

entry.summary: The paper proposes measuring task-conditioned utility of agent memories instead of single importance scores, using a task-blind writer, a frozen reader with and without the memory, and a cost ledger for resource accounting. On LongMemEval-V2-derived tasks, answer-bearing memories yield a +0.33 mean paired reward gain over matched controls.

entry.title: Forgetting to Improve: Principled Data Removal in Active Learning

author.name: Manuel Wendl, Erik Englesson, Andreas Krause, Carl Henrik Ek

entry.summary: The authors propose Forgetting to Improve, an influence-function method for Gaussian process models that identifies and removes data that harms modeling under model mismatch, embedding the downstream task into the modeling framework. It offers a principled treatment of aleatoric-epistemic decomposition as a property of the model rather than the data-generating process.

entry.title: Palimpsestic Accountability in the US Federal AI Inventories

author.name: Dipto Das, Syed Ishtiaque Ahmed, Aditya Vashistha, Shion Guha

entry.summary: This study links entries across three releases of the US Federal AI Use Case Inventory (2023-2025), analyzing how accountability accounts are rewritten as the inventory grew from 710 to 3,611 entries, guided by the ADMAPS framework. It reveals governance dynamics over time that single-release audits miss, with implications for public-sector AI oversight.

entry.title: Benchmarking Unsupervised Jamming Detection in 5G Open RAN

author.name: Sneihil Gopal, Fernando J. Cintron, Richard A. Rouil

entry.summary: Benchmarks statistical and reconstruction-based unsupervised jamming detectors in 5G Open RAN using a symmetric evaluation interface combining detection confidence and temporal interval coherence, enabling comparison without ground-truth labels. It compares a Statistical Ensemble Method detector against vanilla, LSTM, and other neural detectors. Useful for deployments lacking labeled RF attack data.

entry.title: Large Language Model-Assisted Adaptive Heuristic Search for Agile Earth Observation Satellite Scheduling

author.name: He Wang, Yeye Liu, Ruijie Li, Xuemei Jiang, Junyu Wu, Lining Liu Zhuoqi Man, Tao Li, Yanjie Song

entry.summary: Proposes an LLM-assisted adaptive heuristic search for agile Earth observation satellite scheduling, where an LLM generates an initial task-selection heuristic and refines it during ant colony search based on performance feedback. Evaluated via paired statistical tests, the letter targets a real operations-research problem with attitude maneuvering and energy constraints. A compact applied contribution combining LLMs with metaheuristic optimization.

entry.title: Reconstruction-Based Diagnosis through G\"odel-Regularized Virtual Observability

author.name: Oliver Niggemann, Jonas Ehrhardt, Alexander Diedrich

entry.summary: This arXiv paper addresses fault diagnosis in technical systems where not all components can be instrumented with sensors, causing faults to be detected only after their effects have propagated. The authors introduce virtual sensors built from a novel neural observer trained only on normal operating data: it uses available sensor measurements where possible and reconstructs missing variables to predict nominal behavior, flagging deviations as local symptoms for fault isolation. External knowledge describes the fault-sensitive variables for each component-fault combination, and the approach is regularized in a formally inspired (Goedel-regularized) manner.

entry.title: Fast, Cheap, and Fair? Evaluating Decision Models

author.name: Muhammad Uzair Ul Haq, Davide Rigoni, Alessandro Sperduti, Flavia Fabris

entry.summary: This paper presents the first systematic bias and fairness audit of a compact typed-decision model intended for recruitment screening, motivated by the EU AI Act classifying such systems as high-risk. The study evaluates whether cheap System-1 decision models introduce fairness problems relative to general-purpose LLMs in high-stakes HR decisions.

entry.title: AgentAM: An AI Agent for Spatter- and Defect-Aware Process Optimization in Laser Powder Bed Fusion

author.name: Olabode T. Ajenifujah, Amir Barati Farimani

entry.summary: AgentAM is an LLM agent that gives process engineers natural-language access to CFD-trained surrogate models for melt pool geometry and spatter in laser powder bed fusion via the Model Context Protocol. Polynomial surrogates predict melt pool dimensions with R2 of at least 0.95 and classify defect regimes consistently with simulations, lowering the programming barrier to shop-floor use.

entry.title: Zero-Gated Cross-Attention

author.name: Basavaraj R M, Manav Verma

entry.summary: Inductively Gated Cross-Attention (IGCA) is a zero-initialized cross-attention bridge that preserves frozen language model behavior at initialization while enabling gradual multimodal conditioning, demonstrated across Falcon-40B, open_llama_30b, and Bloom-7b1 backbones. It acts as an exact algebraic no-op at initialization, addressing early optimization instability when injecting non-text modalities.

entry.title: EvoMemState: Evolving Memory State for Personal Agents

author.name: Zhishang Xiang, Yunbo Tang, Zhongqiao Liu, Junkai Chen, Zerui Chen, Qingguo Hu, Yuxuan Zhang, William Grant, Qinggang Zhang, Jinsong Su

entry.summary: EvoMemState proposes a state-centric framework for LLM agent long-term memory that augments stored facts with Relational States tracking how facts remain valid and interact, plus a Reasoning State capturing applicability and priority for the current request. This addresses limitations of fact-centric memory systems that miss conflicts and updates between facts.

entry.title: Stacking-Based Weighting for Large Language Bayes in M-Open Settings

author.name: Anant Bhide, Akarsh Gupta, Edmond Cunningham, Justin Domke

entry.summary: The paper improves Large Language Bayes, where an LLM generates candidate probabilistic programs for a natural-language problem, by replacing likelihood-based Bayesian model averaging with stacking-based aggregation that selects weights by predictive performance. This better handles misspecified candidate models in M-open settings while preserving the language-model-driven model generation.

entry.title: Must AI Spell It Out? Pragmatic Comprehension of Alerts in a Time-Critical Task

author.name: Anwesha Das, Vera Demberg, Anna Maria Feit

entry.summary: This HCI-focused study tests whether users can understand deliberately incomplete alerts from assistive systems using pragmatic inference, comparing a pragmatic planner that models listener knowledge against a fully explicit baseline. In a preregistered study with 114 participants performing a time-critical monitoring task, the authors assess how prior knowledge and time pressure affect detection of critical situations.

entry.title: Separating Common and Unique Directions for Data-Free Model Merging

author.name: Shiting Wang, Yingjie Zou, Ke li

entry.summary: The paper identifies a two-regime structure in task vectors — a low-dispersion common bulk shared across tasks and a high-dispersion task-dominated tail — and proposes CUSD, a data-free pre-merging method that separates common and unique directional components and merges each with tailored rules.

entry.title: IntentGEO: Intent-aware Generative Engine Optimization for Recommendation

author.name: Runlin Lei, Shiqi Zhang, Xiaokui Xiao, Zhewei Wei

entry.summary: IntentGEO formulates intent-aware generative engine optimization, showing that existing content-centric GEO methods produce visibility gains that vary with user need specificity and decision progression. It proposes optimizing shared item rewrites with awareness of how changing intent affects visibility in LLM-generated recommendations.

entry.title: From Watching to Steering: Enabling Human-Coding Agent Collaboration through Execution Traces

author.name: Xiaoke Yan, Jiaying Lei, Danqing Shi, Zichen Wang, Nan Cao

entry.summary: Vibetrace is an interactive system for visualizing and intervening in coding-agent execution traces, built on OpenCode, supporting an Observe-Understand-Intervene-Evolve workflow. Users can fork executions from prior steps for targeted corrections and distill traces plus human feedback for improvement.

entry.title: Polyp Matching Using Deep Learning

author.name: Kristian Dalsb{\o} Hindberg, Puneet Sharma, Benedicte Schelde-Olesen, Ulrik Deding, Jakob Frederik Fr{\o}kj{\ae}r Justsen, Jan-Matthias Braun, Esmaeil S. Nadimi

entry.summary: The paper presents a contrastive-learning Siamese network approach for matching polyps across images in colon capsule endoscopy, trained on clinician-annotated pairs from a Danish trial. Accurate matching prevents polyp over-counting and unnecessary interventions or follow-up procedures.

entry.title: When Ground Truth Is Not Ground Truth: Automatic Labeling for Hallucination Detection

author.name: Rounak Sen, Divya Kumari, Deeksha Varshney

entry.summary: The paper critiques the common practice of constructing hallucination ground-truth labels by thresholding similarity metrics like BLEURT against reference answers, arguing this is unreliable given BLEURT's English-centric, unbounded, similarity-oriented design. It proposes automatic labeling alternatives for more trustworthy hallucination-detection evaluation.

entry.title: CLARA: A Cognitively-Driven Clarification Framework for Grounding Ambiguous Requests

author.name: Dimitrios Bekris, Marios Glytsos, Panagiotis P. Filntisis, Niki Efthymiou, George Retsinas, Petros Maragos

entry.summary: CLARA is a framework that lets vision-language robotic systems proactively ask clarifying questions when high-level instructions such as clean the room omit crucial user preferences and object arrangements. It addresses the tendency of LVLMs to overestimate their understanding of ambiguous commands.

entry.title: Rethinking GA2Ms: performance and out-of-distribution generalisation

author.name: George Dimitriadis, Damian Machlanski, Paul Clarke, Spyridon Samothrakis

entry.summary: The paper benchmarks spline-based Generalized Additive Models on large-scale tabular learning via the TALENT suite and proposes CoGA2M, a multi-resolution higher-order composite GAM that ranks in the top third across baselines while remaining interpretable. It also examines robustness under distribution shift, where structured inductive biases should help.

entry.title: Fairness Metrics based on the AUC in Clinical Predictive AI

author.name: Jo\~ao Matos, Ben Van Calster, Richard D. Riley, Paula Dhiman, Gary S. Collins

entry.summary: This methodological paper examines eight AUC-based fairness metrics used to evaluate clinical prediction models for binary outcomes, including within-group AUC parity, cross-group xAUC parity, gap-to-overall AUC, and equity-scaled variants. The authors leverage the fact that AUC is a non-collapsible metric — subgroup-specific and overall values are not directly comparable as is often implicitly assumed — to question how existing AUC-based fairness metrics should be used and interpreted. This matters because misapplied fairness metrics in clinical AI can lead to flawed assessments of model equity across patient subgroups with real consequences for care.

entry.title: False Reassurance in LLM Severe-Weather Guidance: A Replayable Evaluation Against Real NWS Alerts

author.name: Kadharmoideen Fadurudeen

entry.summary: This single-author study measures false reassurance, where an LLM assistant tells users conditions are calm while a severe-weather warning is active, by replaying 117 frozen cases built from real US National Weather Service alerts through five conditions of a Claude-based preparedness pipeline. The production pipeline with alert access showed 0% false reassurance, while a blind neutral prompt produced 37.7%. It is a concrete, replayable safety evaluation with disclosed labeling methodology.

entry.title: HARP: Training-Free Dual-Profile Agentic Communication for LLM-Based Recommendation

author.name: Zhen Tao, Xun Zhou, Xuhui Chen, Ziyue Qiao, Qingqiang Sun

entry.summary: HARP reformulates LLM-based recommendation as an agentic communication process in four stages (BUILD, TRANSMIT, UNDERSTAND, SYNC), identifying asymmetries where only users get structured profiles and item-side signals only reach a bandwidth-limited reranker prompt. The proposed approach introduces training-free dual profiles that flow into retrieval as well as reranking and update from interactions. It addresses structural gaps in memory-augmented LLM recommenders.

entry.title: From Autonomous Agents to Cognitive Symbionts: Toward AI-Augmented Human Intelligence

author.name: Hao Fei

entry.summary: This position paper argues that the Physical AI era should focus not only on autonomous embodied robots but equally on AI-augmented humans, framing a class of systems called cognitive symbionts that support human memory, attention, and decision-making from within the person's situation. It proposes a research agenda that complements AGI with human-intelligence augmentation as a first-class goal.

entry.title: ExaTune: Exhaustive Hyperparameter Landscape Exploration at Scale

author.name: Kevin Dick, Katie Lonsway

entry.summary: ExaTune is an open-source HPC system that exhaustively evaluates discretized hyperparameter grids via K-fold cross-validation to produce hyperparameter landscape maps, a new artifact class enabling fitness landscape analysis (ruggedness, autocorrelation, fitness-distance correlation) of ML hyperparameter spaces at scale. It repurposes methods from evolutionary computation never before applied to ML HPO at this granularity.

entry.title: Ermakov--Based embeddings as a parameter-free layer for physics-informed neural networks

author.name: Roberto Bernal-Jaquez, Roberto Romero Huerta, Alexander Schaum

entry.summary: The authors propose embedding the classical Ermakov-Pinney scale function as a parameter-free input-layer feature for physics-informed neural networks solving evolution equations with time-dependent coefficients. A single construction with one closed-form moment identity covers linear diffusion, diffusion in time-dependent traps, and the quantum oscillator with time-dependent frequency, freeing network capacity from learning scales the equation already determines.

entry.title: Structured Priors: Towards an algebra of component priors for prior-data fitted networks

author.name: Thomas Bartz-Beielstein

entry.summary: The paper proposes replacing hand-built synthetic data generators for prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) like TabPFN and Mitra with a structured prior composed of named component priors combined via formally proven algebraic operators (mixture, convolution, scaling, local transform, projection). This measure-theoretic framework makes the influence of prior design choices on the trained network explicit and validated, rather than only observable after costly pre-training.

entry.title: ScaleTraj: Scale-Decomposed Human Trajectory Generation

author.name: Yulin Zeng, Yiheng Zhao, Jun Yan, Yuhong Liu

entry.summary: ScaleTraj tackles the tension between individual-level realism and population-level statistical fidelity in synthetic human mobility data, formalizing the Population-Level Displacement Gap where bottom-up generators fail to reproduce heavy-tailed displacement distributions. The method decomposes trajectory generation by scale to satisfy both individual and aggregate constraints. It matters for applications like urban planning and privacy-preserving mobility simulation.

entry.title: An Information Budget for Label-Noise Memorization, and What Statistical Complexity Tracks: A Study with Multilayer Perceptrons

author.name: Nancy Baygorrea C., Ot\'avio da Fonseca Martins Gomes

entry.summary: The authors decompose predictive information into signal, memorization, and heterogeneity terms, deriving a Fano-type bound relating memorized label noise to training accuracies. Experiments across 89 MNIST runs with pre-specified hypotheses show memorization information rises on training samples but stays near zero on held-out data.

entry.title: SCANO: Restoring Boundary-Condition Completeness in Sampled Meshes with a Sliced-Cross-Attention Neural Operator for 3D Thermal Fields

author.name: Tianyu Li, Zhiwei Cao, Qingang Zhang, Ruihang Wang, Binyang Song, Yonggang Wen

entry.summary: The paper analyzes how mesh subsampling distorts boundary conditioning for neural operators trained on memory-constrained subsamples, identifying three distortion mechanisms and four measurable failure criteria. It proposes SCANO, a sliced-cross-attention neural operator for 3D thermal fields that restores boundary-condition completeness.

entry.title: What Does It Mean to Remove an Edge? Intervention-Aware Fidelity for Graph Neural Network Explanations

author.name: Rocco Mattia Di Mauro, Marco Grassia, Giuseppe Mangioni

entry.summary: The paper formalizes the ambiguity in deletion-based GNN explanation evaluation, distinguishing structural deletion from message suppression as different interventions, and derives conditions under which they coincide. The analysis clarifies that deletion fidelity scores depend on which intervention the evaluation targets.

entry.title: Exact Selective Inference for Spectral Clustering via Piecewise-Constant Graph Perturbation

author.name: Naotoshi Nakamura

entry.summary: This paper makes selective inference tractable for spectral clustering on unweighted epsilon- or k-nearest-neighbor graphs by showing that the difficulty lies in the affinity construction, not the eigendecomposition: along the perturbation path, graph changes occur at finitely many real roots. This enables exact, valid p-values for testing discovered clusters despite the double use of data. A meaningful statistical contribution to post-clustering inference.

entry.title: Ensembles of Random Partition-Based Models under Covariate Shift

author.name: Mary Versa Clemens-Sewall, Eliza O'Reilly

entry.summary: The authors extend theory of covariate shift severity from single models to ensembles, introducing new discrepancy measures that control risk of partition-based kernel estimators. They prove that with sufficient ensemble size these models achieve minimax-optimal convergence rates under covariate shift, theoretically justifying observed ensemble robustness.

entry.title: Predicting Factor Decay: ML Models for Cross-Factor Predictability Erosion

author.name: Chorok Lee

entry.summary: This paper builds machine learning models that predict when quantitative factor signals will erode, achieving a C-index of 0.93 on held-out factor pairs and an online regime detector with roughly 6.6-day detection delay. The key finding is that stronger initial signals decay faster, and the work shifts from explaining why factors decay to predicting when.

entry.title: Language Model Augmented Decision Transformer for Multi-Task Offline Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Xinbo Zhao, Yuhang Liu, Xin Zhang, Lei Le, Zhaohan Xi, Yu Yang, Yingxue Zhang

entry.summary: LaMA-DT is a unified sequence-modeling framework for offline multi-task reinforcement learning that uses a single LLM for both task-aligned trajectory augmentation and multi-task policy learning, guided by natural-language task descriptions. A scoring-and-filtering mechanism selects augmented trajectories to address per-task data scarcity and limited cross-task generalization.

entry.title: Point interpolation and distributional universality in flow-based generative models

author.name: Antonio \'Alvarez-L\'opez, Jingpu Cheng, Liyan Zhang, Qianxiao Li

entry.summary: This theory paper establishes quantitative relationships between finite-sample point interpolation and distributional approximation in Wasserstein distance for flow-based generative models parameterized by Lipschitz vector fields. It derives universality criteria, showing affine-invariant families containing a non-affine field are universal, and proves coordinate-wise dynamics are insufficient in dimension two and above for total variation.

entry.title: One-shot Distributed Learning via Weighted Averaging with Server-side Information

author.name: Pavle Tepav\v{c}evi\'{c}, Du\v{s}an Jakoveti\'{c}, Milo\v{s} Savi\'{c}

entry.summary: The paper studies one-shot distributed learning where workers send locally fitted models to a server for aggregation, avoiding iterative communication. It addresses settings where many workers with small local samples create nonzero local estimation bias, using server-side data to design weighted averaging schemes that aim to recover pooled-data MSE rates.

entry.title: Data informed Ansatz Selection for Variational Quantum Circuits

author.name: Manav Seksaria, Advith Desu, Anil Prabhakar

entry.summary: The paper provides three training-free rules for selecting variational quantum circuit ansatz and depth from the dataset and gate set alone. Using SVD of dataset Fourier coefficients to determine entanglement requirements, a law governing quantum Fisher information matrix rank growth per layer to fix depth, and a third rule for readout, the work aims to eliminate costly trial-and-error training of VQC candidates.

entry.title: PLANTEUR: A Crop-Type Segmentation Benchmark for Tropical Regions

author.name: Piper Wolters, Gabriel Tseng, Favyen Bastani, Joseph Redmon, Yawen Zhang, Hadrien Sablon, Ando Shah

entry.summary: Presents PLANTEUR, an open-source benchmark for crop-type mapping from Sentinel-1/2 and Landsat-8 satellite imagery across six tropical regions in the French overseas territories. It includes a leave-one-island-out protocol for measuring cross-territory generalization and evaluates supervised models, linear probes, and fine-tuned foundation models.

entry.title: AdSteer: Native Advertising in Large Language Model Generation

author.name: Shuhang Lin, Chuhao Zhou, Zhenyu Wang, Xiao Lin, Changsheng Wang, Saibo Geng, Dimitris N. Metaxas

entry.summary: Proposes AdSteer, a lightweight decoding-time framework that adaptively adjusts token probabilities to integrate contextually appropriate native advertising into LLM responses without prompt injection, multi-pass rewriting, or fine-tuning. It is framed as a monetization mechanism for LLM services facing high serving costs.

entry.title: TEMPO: Time Series Understanding via Discrete Tokenization

author.name: Riccardo Maggioni (Forgis)

entry.summary: TEMPO extends an LLM vocabulary with discrete codes from a context-aware transformer tokenizer using finite scalar quantization, mapping four-step time-series patches to a 625-code vocabulary processed alongside text. With a Qwen3-4B backbone and DoRA adapters, it achieves strong results such as 89.0% macro-F1 on activity recognition.

entry.title: GM League Arena: An Interactive Long-Horizon Task Benchmark Based on Professional Sports League Management

author.name: Junkai Zhou, Ziming Pan, Zhaoyi Zhang

entry.summary: GM Bench is an interactive benchmark where LLMs manage professional sports teams across seasons under financial constraints, player demands, market mechanisms, and competition, with simulators built for four sports from real rosters. It targets cumulative decision quality and long-term goal achievement rather than local multi-step success.

entry.title: Spatial and Temporal Super-Resolution and Denoising of Intracardiac 4D Flow MRI

author.name: Yusuf A. Ozturk, Jie Zheng, Fanwei Kong

entry.summary: The authors propose 4D-MRAR, a deep learning method that jointly performs super-resolution and denoising of 4D Flow MRI, enabling non-invasive, time-resolved measurement of 3D cardiovascular velocity fields inside the heart. Unlike prior learned reconstruction methods that operate on static vascular regions, the approach handles deforming cardiac anatomy across large motion, aiming to resolve complex intracardiac flow features relevant to disease diagnosis and treatment planning.

entry.title: CHROMA-MILL: Joint Low-Light Enhancement and White Balance under Colored Illumination

author.name: Pol Riubrogent-Comas, David Serrano-Lozano, Maria Pilligua, Michael S. Brown, Ramon Baldrich, Javier Vazquez-Corral

entry.summary: This paper examines the underexplored ordering of low-light enhancement before auto white balance, releasing CHROMA-MILL, a calibrated RAW dataset of 50 scenes across four illuminants and eleven intensity levels with physically grounded linear-domain blends for training and evaluation. It enables joint LLIE and AWB modeling under colored illumination.

entry.title: Improving Diffusion-Based Augmentation for Data-Scarce Image Classification via Mask-Guided Reference Attention and Repulsive Noise Optimization

author.name: Hyun-Jic Oh, GaYeon Koh, Won-Ki Jeong

entry.summary: This work fixes a dual failure mode of diffusion-based augmentation in extreme data-scarce settings: missing discriminative foreground details and biased class priors causing similar outputs regardless of prompts. The sampling-side framework uses mask-guided reference attention and repulsive noise optimization to improve generated training data.

entry.title: GroundSeek-CXR: Retrospective Evaluation-Guided Active Observation Framework for Multi-Label Chest Radiography Diagnosis

author.name: Yihang Fu, Xinyu Liu, Qing Xu, Xiaofeng Yang, Zhen Chen

entry.summary: Proposes an active chest X-ray diagnosis framework that learns observation and stopping decisions by retrospectively scoring each observation against the final diagnosis, rather than only its immediate effect. This addresses a supervision credit-assignment gap in vision-language models that actively examine image regions.

entry.title: EndoS3:Endoscopic Semantic Splatting SLAM

author.name: Mona Sheikh Zeinoddin, Benjamin Wright, Zafer Tandogdu, Greg Shaw, Evangelos Mazomenos, Danail Stoyanov

entry.summary: Presents a Gaussian Splatting-based semantic SLAM framework for endoscopic surgery that jointly handles camera tracking, deformable reconstruction, and semantic mapping using instance masks, including a module to separate static and dynamic tissue instances. Addresses the scarcity of datasets providing ground truth for all three tasks.

entry.title: Entropy-Gated Dynamic Rectification for Object Hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Riasad Alvi, Md. Asaduzzaman Shuvo, Md. Ahashan Habib, Md. Faiyaz Abdullah Sayeedi

entry.summary: Proposes EGDR, which reduces object hallucination in large vision-language models via latent steering gated by predictive entropy: the intervention threshold lowers when entropy from already-available logits is high, exploiting the temporal variation of entropy across decoding steps rather than a fixed gate. Requires only one forward pass.

entry.title: Gradient-Guided Orientation Learning for Weakly Supervised Oriented Object Detection

author.name: Junyong Jang, Juheon Park, Minyoung Jeon, Jaehyup Lee

entry.summary: Proposes a gradient-guided orientation learning strategy for weakly supervised oriented object detection that exploits orientation priors in the input image itself, improving stability under illumination changes, shadows, and clutter where geometric-consistency supervision is ambiguous. Reduces costly rotated-box annotation.

entry.title: How Well Does Webcam Eye Tracking Work "in the Wild"? A Large-Scale Validation of Chiasm and a Comparison with WebGazer

author.name: Artem V. Belopolsky, Florian Perdreau

entry.summary: A large-scale online validation (N=505) of the Chiasm webcam eye tracker across diverse participants, devices, and conditions, reporting ~2.39 cm mean spatial accuracy and comparing against WebGazer. The study provides practical benchmarks and calibration criteria for when webcam eye tracking is usable outside the lab.

entry.title: PadLoc: Training-Free Floor-Plan Localization by Sparse Geometric Matching

author.name: Marian Bookhahn, Frank Neumann

entry.summary: PadLoc is a training-free localization back-end that places a moving sensor within a known floor plan by replacing dense pose-grid filtering with sparse geometric matching based on dominant wall orientations. It combines masked cross-correlation scoring with a Gaussian-mixture Bayes filter and matches or beats learned baselines like UnLoc while keeping any depth front-end swappable.

entry.title: GSCV++: Lightweight 3D Gaussian Splatting Sequence Compression via Standard Video Codecs

author.name: Qi Yang, Yingzhan Xu, Kai Zhang, Li Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes GSCV++, a pipeline for compressing 3D Gaussian Splatting sequences using standard video codecs, combining energy-adaptive spherical harmonic dimensionality reduction, improved 3D-to-2D mapping, and practical codec configurations. It targets low-complexity, hardware-compatible compression for industry deployment.

entry.title: h-NESDF: An Infinitely Differentiable Signed Distance Between Two Sets with Robotic Applications

author.name: Vinicius Mariano Gon\c{c}alves, Pedro Antonio de Souza Campos Rodrigues

entry.summary: Defines NESDF, a Normal Euclidean Signed Distance Function between two general possibly non-convex sets, and its smoothed generalization h-NESDF, which is infinitely differentiable for any positive smoothing parameter and converges to NESDF as h approaches zero. The metric supports derivative-dependent robotics applications such as motion planning and control.

entry.title: Grasping and Stabilizing Tumbling Objects with Rotating-Base Multi-Arm Space Manipulators

author.name: Farhad Aghili

entry.summary: The paper proposes guidance and control for space manipulators that actively maneuver their base to hold a tumbling object stationary before capture, in two phases: a synchronization control that rigidizes the target-servicer system around an instantaneous center of rotation, followed by Hamiltonian-dynamics-based post-grasp control. This enables impact-free capture with single or multi-arm configurations without predefined grasping interfaces.

entry.title: Reality and Perceptual Gaps in Expressive Swarm Robotics

author.name: Ali Imran, Abdalwhab Bakheet Mohammed Abdalwhab, Rafael Gomes Braga, H\'el\`ene Duval, Audrey Rochette, Vivek Shankar Varadhajan, Yann Bouteiller, Jean Mazerolle, Giovanni Beltrame, David St-Onge

entry.summary: This study deploys the same decentralized swarm coordination code across three platforms (tabletop, aerial, and human-scale manipulators) during live artistic performances, documenting how physical embodiment alters visible group behavior beyond the classic sim-to-real reality gap. It introduces the perceptual gap: the divergence between what a swarm physically does and what human onlookers perceive.

entry.title: PanelGP: A Probabilistic Factor Model for Asset-Return Panels

author.name: Andrea Ruglioni (EPFL), Damir Filipovic (EPFL)

entry.summary: PanelGP is a conditional factor model for large stock-return panels in which firm characteristics set factor loadings and economic conditions set expected factors, both learned nonparametrically with Gaussian-process priors. The kernel design nests instrumented PCA and smooth nonlinear maps, and sparse variational inference yields a joint posterior over loadings and factors, enabling a single model to forecast both expected returns and covariance matrices. Because predictions are bilinear in a Gaussian state, the full predictive distribution is tractable.

entry.title: Directional Statistics in Signal Processing: A Geometry Driven Overview of Models, Learning, and Applications

author.name: Anders S. Olsen, Kanti V. Mardia, Dimitri Van De Ville, Morten M{\o}rup

entry.summary: A comprehensive overview developing a geometry-driven framework for directional statistics in signal processing, mapping signal representations with periodicity, phase ambiguity, or PSD constraints to their natural manifolds and compatible probability models. It reviews circular through Grassmannian and covariance-valued distributions with attention to assumptions, computation, and dimensionality.

entry.title: OpenAI Updates Its Model Spec

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi provides a detailed diff-based analysis of OpenAI's updated Model Spec, examining new values, risk taxonomy, and examples. He concludes the update is philosophically and practically similar to the prior version with mostly improvements, while critiquing that new examples are overdetermined and fail to teach behavior in genuinely difficult cases.

entry.title: GlucoAgent: Personalized Glucose Forecasting from Multimodal Personal Context

author.name: Xingzhi Sun, Hyo Jin Kim, Zhiyuan Wang, Hao Chen

entry.summary: GlucoAgent is an LLM-based agentic system for personalized glucose forecasting that dynamically writes and runs code over multimodal personal context - continuous glucose monitor data, smartwatch signals, meal logs, health profiles - returning predictions with reasons and evidence. Its case-by-case inference-time analysis addresses the problem that modality relevance varies drastically across individuals and time.

entry.title: Reconstructing Fraudulent Strategies in Online Payments via Interpretable Inverse Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Huilin He, Weiyu Han, Linbo Shao, Ruobing Zuo, Xiao Tan, Shuai Chen, Dawei Cheng

entry.summary: PaySeqGen is an interpretable inverse reinforcement learning framework that reconstructs fraud behavior policies from observed payment transaction sequences, preserving sequential relationships among transaction choices, payment feedback, and subsequent adjustments. The generated fraud samples broaden detector coverage beyond distribution-matching data augmentation approaches.

entry.title: A Compact Formula-Aware Spreadsheet Abstraction for Large Language Models

author.name: Tie Cheng

entry.summary: This paper proposes a compact formula-aware abstraction that represents large homogeneous spreadsheet ranges via positions, types, R1C1 formula patterns, and boundary values, serialized textually for LLMs. A range-detection algorithm supplies this abstraction before detailed content, addressing the mismatch between spreadsheet structure and sequential text representations.

entry.title: Agentic Path Maps: Exposing an Agent's Traversal Through the Garden of Forking Paths

author.name: Madeleine Grunde-McLaughlin, Hafsah Usman, Daniel Mitroshkov, Emily Reif, Nino Migineishvili, Lakshya Chauhan. Kevin Yu, Jeffrey Heer, Daniel S. Weld

entry.summary: This HCI work presents a design space for communicating an AI agent's unexplored alternative paths after executing an underspecified task, and reports a user study (n=48) showing users rarely consider alternatives unprompted but AI-surfaced alternatives aid comprehension. It focuses on how the number of displayed alternatives affects understanding.

entry.title: Who is the Pronoun Pro? Comparing LLMs and Humans at Number-Disambiguation of 'they'

author.name: Carlos Hartmann

entry.summary: In a controlled annotation study, 73 human annotators and over 40 LLM configurations disambiguated 174 authentic uses of singular/plural they from Reddit; the best model, Kimi K3 (an established model since mid-2026), reached 94.5% accuracy, above human majority vote at 86.2% and second only to the single best human. The study also examines practical cost and speed advantages and qualitative error patterns.

entry.title: Stress-Testing the Robustness of LLM-Based Causal Inference

author.name: Ankitkumar Patel, Jigarkumar Patel, Amit Kumar, Supreetha Sreeram, Venkatesh Kulkarni

entry.summary: This work maps where, why, and how severely LLMs fail at causal inference, stress-testing their causal reasoning beyond anecdotal evidence. It aims to distinguish surface-level pattern recognition from genuine causal logic and provide a precise failure taxonomy for LLM-based causal discovery.

entry.title: Embedding Semantic Entropy: NLI-Free Semantic Uncertainty Estimation with Geometry-Aware Clustering

author.name: Akshiya Raveendran, Praveenasarma Baskarakurukkal, Pragatheeswaran Vipulanandan, Kamal Premaratne, Uthayasanker Thayasivam

entry.summary: This work replaces entailment-model-based clustering in semantic entropy with K-Medoids clustering in semantic embedding space plus dynamic cluster selection based on intra-cluster compactness and inter-cluster separation, removing the need for NLI models. Evaluated on five QA benchmarks across four open models, it achieves competitive AUROC and AUARC for uncertainty estimation.

entry.title: RGDM: Robust Graph Diffusion Model

author.name: Yancheng Wang, Ping Li, Dongfang Sun, Yingzhen Yang

entry.summary: RGDM is a graph diffusion model designed to generate labeled synthetic nodes and edges robustly even when trained on adversarially corrupted graphs, combining a Robust Graph Autoencoder with a latent diffusion model. Edge selection and low-rank regularization on latent features enable generated structures to integrate seamlessly into existing graphs. It extends robustness guarantees to node-level graph generation.

entry.title: The Price of List Replicability: Tight Bounds for Bias Estimation

author.name: Michael Chen, Atieh Bastan, A. Pavan, N. V. Vinodchandran

entry.summary: The paper establishes the first nontrivial sample complexity lower bounds for list replicable algorithms estimating biases of d coins, complementing prior upper bounds. List replicability requires algorithm outputs to fall in a small set of candidate vectors for each input.

entry.title: All Paths All at Once: A Quantum Monte Carlo and Neural Committor Approach to Reaction Pathway Search

author.name: Chien-Chai Chang

entry.summary: This work presents tReax_expedition, an energy-only method combining Monte Carlo exploration, stochastic quench labeling, and restrained continuation to find competing reaction pathways without potential-energy gradients or transition-state guesses. Benchmarks recover intermediates and competing routes, with sampled barrier estimates within 0.76 kJ/mol of refined saddle energies for most gas-phase reactions tested.

entry.title: Nonparametric GARCH: An Iterated Neural Estimator

author.name: Ruizhi Deng, Guohao Shen, Ngai Hang Chan

entry.summary: The paper proposes an iterated neural estimator for nonparametric GARCH-type volatility estimation that alternates between estimating the recursion map and updating unobserved conditional variances, with finite-sample error bounds. It proves minimax rate-optimal in-sample and forecast performance up to logarithmic factors, with rates robust to lag overspecification.

entry.title: LIPS-PC: Learning Illumination Patterns for Single-Pixel Classification

author.name: Tomer Porat, Talya Eden, Eliahu Cohen

entry.summary: LIPS-PC learns end-to-end illumination patterns for single-pixel (ghost) imaging classification where each measurement costs time, photons, or dose. Patterns are parameterized as a residual correction to a 2D-DCT basis with a fixed linear measurement operator, jointly trained with a compact classifier, motivated by radiographic defect screening.

entry.title: Shared Context Candidate Scoring with Jointly Adapted Readout Networks

author.name: Jingyang Du, Yiben Fu, Yang Shen

entry.summary: Presents Q64, a candidate-scoring system built on a frozen 64-layer Qwen3.8-27B backbone that reuses hybrid prefix states and intermediate document representations, jointly training a residual adapter, four-layer decoder, and candidate-conditioned readout. Trained on roughly 8,000 selected views with 88.66 million updated parameters, it is evaluated on accuracy and latency over a fixed 5,112-item evaluation.

entry.title: CounterSketch: Physics-Grounded Counterfactual Reasoning for Sketch-to-Video Generation

author.name: Hien Trinh, Tan-Hiep To, Dinh-Khoi Vo, Tam V. Nguyen, Minh-Triet Tran, Trung-Nghia Le

entry.summary: CounterSketch converts natural-language what-if queries into physically plausible sketch animations by combining VLM-guided scene grounding, causal event-chain reasoning, constraint-based trajectory generation, and verification, then uses verified trajectories to guide sketch-video synthesis. It is evaluated on a new 80-question CounterSketchBench.

entry.title: VidUEU-Agent: A Data-Curation Agent for Multimodal Understanding, Editing, and Unified Tasks

author.name: Tengju Ru, Weitong Lian, Zecong Tang, Lingyi Meng, Haoran Li, Zhejun Cui, Yichen Zhu, Hangshuo Cao, Qi Kang, Yechi Liu, Kaixuan Wang, Yu-Jie Yuan, Chunwei Wang, Yu Zhang, Bo Dai

entry.summary: An automated agent pipeline that converts raw videos into instruction data for multimodal understanding, editing, and unified training tasks through four stages: quality filtering, keyframe and multimodal signal mining, metadata construction, and routed instruction synthesis, with autonomous iteration. Targets the scarcity and annotation cost of high-quality multimodal instruction data.

entry.title: EP-LVMQA: Evidence-Preserving Coarse-to-Fine Localization for Low-Quality Long Video Moment Question Answering

author.name: Guoning Chen, Zhexun Hu, Yifan Wei, Yixuan Weng, Bin Li, Yufei Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes an evidence-preserving coarse-to-fine framework for long video moment QA that returns timestamped answer-supporting evidence despite noisy ASR, sparse OCR, and missing subtitles, built from an uncertainty-aware multimodal evidence timeline, coarse planner, and fine localizer. Targets medical education and industrial training video applications.

entry.title: TAQ-MOTR: Tracking-Aware Detection Query Formation for End-to-End Multiple Object Tracking

author.name: Hanyang Liu, Hong Zhang, Ding Yuan, Yang Han, Yifan Yang

entry.summary: TAQ-MOTR improves tracking-by-propagation multi-object tracking by making detection-query formation aware of trajectory states, rather than inheriting single-frame detection queries built before the decoder. This helps discover currently untracked objects while retaining evidence for challenging tracks whose queries persist.

entry.title: Visibility-Aware Reference Generation for Benchmarking Visual 3D Reconstruction in Vegetation-Rich Environments

author.name: Zhipeng Zhong, Matthew Coombes, Cunjia Liu

entry.summary: Introduces a LiDAR-based reference-generation pipeline for benchmarking zero-shot feed-forward visual-geometry models against structure-from-motion in vegetation-rich outdoor scenes, reusing existing multi-sensor localization datasets to produce per-view depth maps and visible reference point clouds. A novel LargeDepth-Gap Visibility Score filters visibility errors in accumulated LiDAR scans.

entry.title: LLM-Assisted Planning with Distributed Onboard Behaviour Tree Execution for Multi-AUV Missions

author.name: Ehsan Khorrambakht, Cristiano Caissutti, Andrea Munafo, Andrea Caiti

entry.summary: A hierarchical framework couples LLM interpretation of natural-language mission instructions with MILP optimization and distributed behavior-tree execution for multi-AUV underwater missions. The LLM extracts assignment and ordering constraints, the MILP combines them with vehicle capabilities, and onboard behavior-tree agents handle local faults with selective replanning so unaffected vehicles continue when communication is limited.

entry.title: Validation-Gated ML Pipeline Synthesis with Expert-Grounded Self-Evolving Skills

author.name: Zixiao Zhao, Jing Sun, Zhe Hou, Mengze Li, Qian Liu, Cheng-Hao Cai, Zijian Zhang, Xin Wang, Gillian Dobbie, Jin Song Dong

entry.summary: EvoML is an agentic framework for end-to-end ML pipeline synthesis built on expert-grounded skills that evolve across runs, decomposing construction into four phases coordinated by three agents with an Orchestrator enforcing validation gates to prevent silent error propagation. It addresses reliability weaknesses of free-form code generation in agentic AutoML.

entry.title: RoboScope Kit: Unified Interfaces for Fast and Scalable Embodied-AI Evaluation

author.name: Deng-Ke Wu, Yifan Jin, Yida Yang, Lei Qian, Zhaoye Zhou, Hongru Zhang, Kai Ye, Shuyuan Hu, Yiran Mao, Zewei Ye, Bo Zhao

entry.summary: RoboScope Kit wraps models and simulation benchmarks in unified Policy and adapter interfaces without changing benchmark scoring, and schedules simulator workers and policy replicas as separately sized pools with deterministic sharding across GPUs. Profiling showed official evaluators leave GPUs at 14.3% utilization; the kit dramatically accelerates embodied-AI evaluation such as 500 RoboTwin episodes.

entry.title: Spectral Quantum Memory for Implicit Neural Representations

author.name: Daniel A. Moroz-Broitman, Eliya Nachmani

entry.summary: SQMM introduces a memory-coupled quantum INR architecture in which sequential hybrid data-reuploading layers communicate through a shared coherent quantum memory register, allowing later spectral bands to build on earlier computation. The authors prove a characterization result when memory read/write layers are input independent.

entry.title: DenseTwins: Dense Modality Decoupling for Multimodal Self-Supervision

author.name: Carlo Sgaravatti, Daniele Kopyshevskiy, Davide Secco, Giacomo Boracchi

entry.summary: DenseTwins is a multimodal self-supervised framework that learns dense representations by explicitly decoupling shared and modality-specific feature components, combining dense cross-modal correspondences with modality-specific objectives. It targets robotics and autonomous driving settings where modalities provide complementary cues.

entry.title: Found by Search, Broken by a Shortcut: Transfer and Tampering of Searched Intrinsic Rewards

author.name: Chase J. Metoyer

entry.summary: This pre-registered study searches over intrinsic rewards composed of four generic events using CMA-ES across 1,560 PPO runs, finding the searched reward transfers to a held-out task and beats task-only PPO, novelty, and random-search baselines. A tamper test then probes whether such searched rewards resist exploits absent during the search.

entry.title: Auditing a Model-Hub Benchmark: Data Quality, Training Budgets, and Side Information in HuggingBench

author.name: Michal Podstawski

entry.summary: This audit of the HuggingBench benchmark (SIGIR 2025) for recommending Hugging Face resources finds that three of four external knowledge graphs violate item-entity identity constraints despite passing basic validation. Correcting the join improves every KG-based method by up to 73% Recall@10 and reverses ten of 27 method comparisons.

entry.title: Ground-Wing: A Parametric 3D Wing-in-Ground-Effect Dataset for Benchmarking Neural Surrogate Models

author.name: Andrea Cenzato, Lukas Karch, Andre Luckow, Yoran Pichon, Francesco Pasqua, Abouzar Ghasemi, Rishikesh Ranade, Ira Shokar, Julia Kowalski

entry.summary: The paper presents a CFD dataset of 770 RANS simulations of 194 parametrized 3D wing configurations in ground effect, aimed at motorsport-relevant flow conditions. It benchmarks six neural architectures spanning convolutional, graph, transformer, and JEPA paradigms on aerodynamic prediction.

entry.title: Where Do Distilled Students Store Thinking?

author.name: Taeyeong Kim, Jaemin Jung, Ahhyun Kim, Unggi Lee

entry.summary: This mechanistic interpretability study examines where LoRA-adapted student models store reasoning behavior when distilled from large reasoning models, finding the adapter update subspace shifts most where the teacher stops thinking and solutions shorten. It identifies a shared adapter subspace tied to thinking-like behavior such as reflective markers and long solutions.

entry.title: Estimating "Realized" Skewness using Convolutional Neural Network

author.name: Haozhe Jiang, Ostap Okhrin, Michael Rockinger

entry.summary: The authors propose a CNN-plus-MLP estimator of monthly skewness exploiting 5-minute high-frequency data via a direct functional mapping. Monte Carlo experiments show reduced finite-sample bias versus existing realized-skewness estimators, and empirical results demonstrate temporal stability and cross-sectional performance in skewness-sorted portfolios, with consistency theory provided.

entry.title: IGSW: Multi-Weather Urban Scene Reconstruction with Intrinsic-Decoupled Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Zhongquan Wang, Long Cao, Peijia Xie, Senlei Ma, Jie Li, Guofa Li

entry.summary: Introduces a two-stage framework combining intrinsic-decoupled 4D Gaussian scene modeling with structure-preserving weather refinement for multi-weather editing of dynamic urban scenes, decomposing background appearance into weather-shared albedo and weather-specific components. Aims to support closed-loop simulation and training for autonomous driving without propagating generative-editing artifacts.

entry.title: VISTA: Vision-Language Integrated Semantic Triage Architecture for Online Face Clustering in Long Videos

author.name: Jiashu Liao, Joanne Garde-Hansen, Sanjay Sharma, Tanaya Guha

entry.summary: Presents VISTA, described as the first vision-language framework for online face clustering in long videos, leveraging semantic triage to handle appearance variations where geometric features and thresholding fail. Targets streaming human-centric video analysis where full data availability cannot be assumed.

entry.title: Self-governed access control in open robot swarms using a blockchain-based DAO

author.name: Raina Zakir, Alexandre Pacheco, Andreagiovanni Reina, Marco Dorigo, Volker Strobel

entry.summary: Proposes using a blockchain-based decentralized autonomous organization for governance of open robot swarms, where robots dynamically join or leave at runtime, providing access control and protection against Byzantine (faulty or malicious) robots. The work targets practical deployment concerns for collective robotic systems in domains like agriculture and disaster response.

entry.title: Physics-Based Plausibility Assessment of AI-Predicted Vehicle Parameters for Automotive Radar in Pre-Crash Scenarios

author.name: Rainer Engert, Patrick Zaumseil, Thomas Brandmeier

entry.summary: The paper addresses the gap between statistical accuracy and physical consistency in AI-based automotive radar perception by assessing plausibility of predicted object parameters (especially heading) against the underlying radar sensing physics in pre-crash scenarios. This targets safety-critical trajectory prediction and collision assessment where physically inconsistent estimates from data-driven models can be dangerous in unseen scenarios.

entry.title: Nested Field-of-View Barriers for Teleoperated Multi-Robot Relay Chains

author.name: Arthur Vangasse, Theo Cruz, Thales Soares, Andr\'e Cid, Vin\'icius Gon\c{c}alves, Gustavo Freitas, Luciano Pimenta

entry.summary: This paper presents a shared-autonomy framework for teleoperating a leader robot followed by an autonomous relay chain that maintains line-of-sight connectivity to a fixed base station in communication-denied environments. Connectivity is enforced geometrically using visibility-based Control Barrier Functions, with each agent solving a local quadratic program, and the work analyzes the tradeoff between strict visibility constraints (which can stall the leader) and relaxed variants that preserve mobility. This addresses a real operational problem for search-and-rescue and exploration missions.

entry.title: We Ran a Research Sprint With AI. The AI Worked. The Research Didn't

author.name: Anush Sankaran, Arijit Banerjee

entry.summary: This position paper argues that personal AI tools under deadline pressure create a consumption bottleneck, where generation outpaces team-visible evaluation, and AI-induced research silos, where private human-AI loops displace shared decision-making. It motivates the claims with a 100-minute sprint involving twelve researchers in three teams, where of 33 logged AI interactions only one was accepted outright.

entry.title: Exploit or conform? How norm utility prompting changes the way LLMs use community beliefs

author.name: Leon Klingborg, Theodor Cimpeanu, Alexander J. Stewart

entry.summary: This study examines how adding norm utility - the desire to conform to social norms - to prompts affects the strategic decisions of three open-weight LLMs in one-shot two-player social dilemmas. It matters for both alignment on prototypical social decisions and the validity of LLMs as simulators of human agents in social science studies.

entry.title: Interpretable Early Termination of Web Navigation Agents via Closed Sequential Pattern Mining

author.name: Sergio Talavera, Magdalini Eirinaki

entry.summary: The paper applies closed sequential pattern mining (BIDE+) to prefixes of web agent execution traces to build a small human-reviewable failure-signature library with a four-category failure taxonomy and repair recommendations, enabling interpretable early termination of doomed trajectories. This targets the common problem that open-weight web agents spend most tokens after failure becomes unrecoverable.

entry.title: Beyond Fine-Tuning: Evaluating Prompt Engineering and Prompt Tuning for Roman Urdu Hate Speech Detection

author.name: Toneema Zubair, Muhammad Junaid Asif, Faisal Kamiran, Hafiz Hassan Saeed, Rana Fayyaz Ahmad

entry.summary: Systematically compares zero-shot and few-shot prompting, structured prompting, and learnable prompt representations for hate speech detection in Roman Urdu, a low-resource, code-mixed, non-standardly-spelled setting. The work builds on prior PEFT research and asks whether prompt-based methods can substitute for fine-tuning where annotated data is scarce. It is relevant to content moderation in underserved language communities.

entry.title: HTCE: Homeomorphism-inspired Topological Cross-Scene Experience Canonicalization and Reuse for Object Navigation

author.name: Xiaoran Xu, Yupeng Wu, Tianyu Xue, Xuanran Dong, Yifan Xu, Xiaoshan Yang, Changsheng Xu

entry.summary: HTCE is a homeomorphism-inspired topological framework that lets embodied agents canonicalize and reuse navigation experience across scenes where semantic structure recurs but geometric trajectories differ. Feature and topology subdivisions with semantically constrained reductions produce comparable semantic sequences while preserving meaningful differences in anchors, branches, and endpoints.

entry.title: Development of tools for all-cause mortality prediction in heart failure patients: a systematic review

author.name: Erik Aerts, Annika Rosengren, Martin Lindgren, Martin Adiels, Yinan Yu, Helen S\"oland

entry.summary: A systematic review of all-cause mortality prediction models for heart failure published 2009 to early 2026, searching PubMed, IEEE, and Scopus, covering conventional statistical, machine learning, and deep learning approaches. It highlights how variation in populations, definitions, horizons, and development practices limits interpretation and applicability of the many existing prognostic models.

entry.title: Learning to read residual images for single-pixel photography

author.name: Hongjun An, Shuaizhe An, Tong Tian, Zhe Sun

entry.summary: This work recovers video from extremely sparse single-pixel measurements by computing residual images that approximate the gradient of a centered measurement loss, then lifting them through a pretrained video decoder. Video-latent inversion outperforms frame-wise image-latent reconstruction at roughly 0.24% of full pixel counts, enabling compact event-monitoring without full cameras.

entry.title: The role of injected noise in diffusion model generalization

author.name: Vincent Emmerling, Felix G\"unther, David Kappel

entry.summary: This study investigates why diffusion models trained on distinct datasets produce highly similar samples given the same noise input, showing that the injected noise during sampling plays a decisive role in this apparent generalization. Noise changes matter most in the intermediate sampling regime where broad structure exists but the sample identity is not yet determined.

entry.title: A Practical Causal Framework for Autonomous Mobile Robots: From Simulation to Real-World Human Environments

author.name: Luca Castri, Gloria Beraldo, Nicola Bellotto

entry.summary: The authors present a causal inference framework for mobile robots in human-populated environments, showing that high-level causal structures learned in simulation transfer to the real world by updating only model parameters with a small set of new observations. This enables safe, efficient robot decision-making without lengthy real-world causal data collection.

entry.title: When Model Complexity Matters in Cross-Subject Naturalistic fMRI Prediction

author.name: Junhao Zhao, Jacob Kang, Colin Kurniawan, David Simberg, Nan Xu

entry.summary: This study systematically examines when pretrained stimulus representations and nonlinear predictors improve cross-subject prediction of BOLD fMRI responses to naturalistic stimuli, evaluated across three datasets including HCP movie data with 154 subjects. It provides a shared protocol comparing linear and nonlinear models with and without BOLD history features.

entry.title: LIRA: A More Interpretable Dynamic Loss-Informed Rank Allocation for Low-Rank Adaptation

author.name: Sihao Wang, Bozheng Li, Xuemiao Xu, Haoxin Yang, Yujie Xu, Jie Tang

entry.summary: LIRA is a dynamic-rank LoRA method that scores each layer by the estimated magnitude of local loss perturbation associated with rank reallocation, aiming to make online rank allocation more interpretable than heuristic or first-order-signal approaches used by prior adaptive-rank variants.

entry.title: Large Language Models for Forecasting of Electricity Price Spikes

author.name: Liang Lin, Jianguo Zhu, Gang Lei, Allen Wang, Xin Lu

entry.summary: The study tests whether market notices read by a local LLM improve short-horizon electricity price spike forecasts across five Australian National Electricity Market regions. LLM-extracted notice features did not improve 60-minute Brier scores over numeric models, helped only at 24-hour horizons where rule-based features performed nearly as well, and attribution to notice content was not established.

entry.title: TAPES: Task-Aligned Joint Predictive Pretraining for Transaction Event Sequences

author.name: Ruobing Zuo, Weiyu Han, Huilin He, Haoyu Jiang, Ze Zhao, Jie Sheng, Xiao Tan, Shuai Chen, Tianyi Zhang

entry.summary: TAPES is a task-aligned joint predictive pretraining framework for transaction event sequences in online commerce and financial services, constructing candidate target sets from field-operator combinations and modeling conditional co-occurrence among prediction targets. It addresses the mismatch between predictability of targets and their downstream utility.

entry.title: UniFlow: Unified Multi-Scale Flow Matching for Time Series Generation

author.name: Shibo Feng, Wei Li, Min Wu, Chunyan Miao, Peilin Zhao

entry.summary: UniFlow integrates multi-scale representation learning with non-autoregressive generation for time series via a shared-semantic discrete interface, using a multi-scale tokenizer with shared-index voting and geometry-aware categorical flow matching. It captures dynamics across temporal resolutions without added generative complexity.

entry.title: Towards Automatic Heart Murmur Characterization from Multi-spot Phonocardiograms

author.name: Marcelo Nogueira, Jorge H. Oliveira, Carlos G. Ferreira, Miguel T. Coimbra, Al\'ipio M. Jorge

entry.summary: The authors formulate automatic heart murmur characterization as five patient-level classification tasks covering timing, shape, pitch, quality, and grade, moving beyond binary murmur detection. They compare per-location classifiers with late fusion against a synchronous multi-input CNN across four auscultation locations.

entry.title: CaRe-KT: Continuity-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning for Knowledge Tracing

author.name: Mehrnoush Mohammadi, Kamal Berahmand, Mohammad Morsali, Shazia Sadiq, Wojtek Tomaszewski, Hassan Khosravi

entry.summary: CaRe-KT addresses the retrieval-inference alignment gap in knowledge tracing with a query-adaptive framework that maintains relevance continuity between evidence retrieval and prediction, using an Evidence-Graph Cache combining persistent question-level relational compatibility with dynamic state-aware evidence. It improves adaptive learning by grounding predictions in cross-learner behavioral evidence.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Identification of Tensegrity Prestress across Taut-Slack Transitions

author.name: Sandesh Lamsal, Sumit Kumar, Rubi Bhandari, Subhamoy Sen, Andrzej Rutkiewicz, Leszek Ma{\l}yszko, Landolf Rhode-Barbarigos

entry.summary: This study formulates the inverse problem of identifying prestress, damping, and stiffness in tensegrity structures, including regimes where cables slacken and dynamics become nonsmooth. Neural networks trained on equation-of-motion residuals in constrained Cartesian coordinates recover force densities and physical parameters from sparse measurements, extending prior physics-informed work that only handled the taut forward problem.

entry.title: LENS: Reliability-Aware Stock Prediction via LLM-Extracted Priors and News-Driven Semantic Graphs

author.name: Hao Zhou, Tiejun Ma, Luis Felipe Costa Sperb

entry.summary: LENS is a static-dynamic graph framework for stock return prediction that treats relational reliability as a first-class signal, using LLM-extracted multi-relational company graphs with confidence weighting and news-driven dynamic graphs. It extends standard GNN pipelines by downweighting low-consistency edges.

entry.title: CAPSkip: Cancellation-Aware Prefix Skipping for Selective Backpropagation

author.name: Heejin Choi

entry.summary: CAPSkip improves selective backpropagation by accounting for cancellation between per-example gradients: among correctly classified examples, it skips the longest prefix whose vector sum of gradients stays within a relative budget of the batch gradient. This bounds the change to the final-layer gradient in exact arithmetic.

entry.title: Surrogate Models for Stochastic Al-Cu Phase-Field Solidification

author.name: Simon Savukoski, Tatu Pinomaa

entry.summary: The authors present a variance-preserving denoising diffusion bridge model for state-conditioned prediction of 2D Al-Cu alloy solidification, applied autoregressively from phase, concentration, and temperature fields. It outperforms deterministic U-Net and ConvNeXt baselines on long-horizon errors while retaining fine dendritic structure.

entry.title: Anomaly Detection on Resource-Constrained Devices with Reservoir Computing

author.name: Marco Angioli, Mathias Persson, Hiroto Tamura, Hadi Banaee, Amy Loutfi, Gouhei Tanaka, Alberto Giaretta, Denis Kleyko

entry.summary: This work optimizes Mahalanobis Distance of Reservoir States (MDRS), an unsupervised time-series anomaly detection method, for edge devices by replacing random reservoir connectivity with circular shift and computing scores from the final reservoir state alone. The optimizations substantially reduce computation and memory while preserving detection quality. Useful for practical always-on anomaly detection in IoT and embedded settings.

entry.title: Modulating Merging Strengths via Joint Loss Estimation for LoRA-based Continual Learning

author.name: Kun Gu, De Cheng, Zhipeng Xu, Lingfeng He, Di Xu, Nannan Wang

entry.summary: M2LE improves LoRA-based continual learning by replacing the shared scalar merge coefficient with elementwise modulation of the LoRA update, estimated through a joint loss that balances prior-task preservation and new-task adaptation. This finer-grained merging control addresses the mismatch in how different update components affect old versus new tasks. Relevant to parameter-efficient lifelong learning of large models.

entry.title: Dual-VaDE: Efficient and Robust Prototype Learning via Variational Dual-Domain Mixture Priors

author.name: Wugeng Zheng, Song Wang, Jian Wang

entry.summary: Dual-VaDE is an unsupervised generative framework that learns interpretable anatomical prototypes from unlabeled medical images using a dual-domain Gaussian mixture prior coupling spatial anatomy with phase-preserving Fourier spectral representations. It derives an exact closed-form variational lower bound and optimizes end-to-end via alternating EM, avoiding heuristic two-stage clustering. Useful for interpretable unsupervised analysis of medical imaging data.

entry.title: Fusing Earth observation embeddings and spaceborne terrain with meteorological forcing for flood peak depth prediction from high-water marks

author.name: Wen Zhou, Shaowen Wang, Upmanu Lall, Venkatesh Merwade, Dingqi Ye

entry.summary: The authors train deep learning models to predict flood peak depth from geospatial foundation-model embeddings, satellite terrain, and antecedent meteorological data, using 5689 USGS high-water mark surveys across 39 US flood events. This shifts flood depth prediction from hydrodynamic simulations to field observations, enabling pre-peak prediction with practical disaster-response value.

entry.title: On Discovering Algorithms for Adversarial Imitation Learning
