Proposes Difficulty-Aware CoT, a training-free framework that selectively triggers CoT based on input difficulty, using attention-map entropy as a reliable difficulty signal. Improves efficiency and accuracy by thinking only when needed.

entry.title: Know When the Equation Is Wrong: Structural Uncertainty for LLM-Guided Symbolic Regression under Extrapolation

author.name: Mostafa Cham, Bayu Adhi Tama, Jianwu Wang

entry.summary: LLM-SR-UQ is a framework for LLM-guided symbolic regression that quantifies uncertainty over equation structures by retaining competing functional forms and using their disagreement, since different equations can fit identically in-distribution yet diverge wildly under extrapolation. Experiments show standard conformal intervals fail under extrapolation while the proposed structural uncertainty improves reliability.

entry.title: Robust Learning of Multi-Index Models under Logconcave Distributions via Weak Partial Learners

author.name: Ilias Diakonikolas, Daniel M. Kane, Mingchen Ma

entry.summary: Develops a new boosting framework based on weak partial learners that yields faster robust algorithms for learning Boolean concept classes, especially multi-index models, under logconcave distributions. The framework extends to partial and testable learning and improves learners for functions of halfspaces and multiclass linear classifiers.

entry.title: Mechanistic Interpretability for End-to-End Self-Driving

author.name: Manav Gagvani, Benjamin Namikas, Sivamurugan Velmurugan, Nysa Kumar, Shrey Sharma, Thomas Peterson, Pratyush Mathur, Hyunseo Chang, Rohan Paleja

entry.summary: Trains sparse autoencoders on the internal activations of a single-camera end-to-end driving model, finding unsupervised latents aligned with route intent (98.3% recovery accuracy), vehicle speed, and braking. Counterfactual image edits show features are visually grounded in scene elements like traffic lights and stop signs, and steering latents causally alters driving behavior.

entry.title: Hybrid Computer Use: A Unified Programmatic, Semantic, and Visual Interface for General Agents

author.name: Haoqing Wang, Xiaoyi Zhang, Sicheng Fan, Zhexin Zhang, Xinjie Zhang, Jiahao Li, Bin Li, Yan Lu

entry.summary: HCU proposes a unified interface for computer-use agents combining three channels: programmatic interaction (code and command line), semantic interaction via accessibility trees, and visual GUI interaction, letting models choose and combine them instead of being forced through a human-like screenshot-and-mouse prior. This broadens the action space available to general agents and may substantially improve long-horizon workflow performance. It challenges the dominant GUI-only paradigm in computer-use research.

entry.title: Coupled or Independent? Fault Coupling in Agentic Medical Vision Systems

author.name: Nishi Kanta Paul, Md Shihabul Islam Shovo, Md Mostafijur Rahman, Jamil Fayyad

entry.summary: This study examines a safety assumption about tool-using medical vision agents: when the sensor input itself is corrupted, tool outputs and reasoning share a common visual fault. Using a dermatology agent, the authors define a fault-coupling taxonomy and show typographic injection produces detectable retrieval capture while physical corruption does not.

entry.title: TACO: Trajectory-Aware Curvature Observation for Memorization Localization and Mitigation in Diffusion Models

author.name: Ruxi Gu, Zilei Wang, Wei Wang

entry.summary: TACO provides a unified framework for detecting and mitigating localized training-data memorization in text-to-image diffusion models. It aggregates prompt-dependent curvature responses across denoising trajectories, since single-state curvature is transient, enabling spatially precise unlearning without disrupting prompt-relevant content.

entry.title: TwinPast: Benchmarking Historical Evidence Use in Streaming Video Understanding with Evidence Contrastive Video Pairs

author.name: Haotian Yang, Yong Chen, Cheng Peng, Haobo Wang, Zhongle Xie, Xuanru Li, Gang Chen

entry.summary: TwinPast tests whether streaming video models actually use visual history: the authors show recent frames suffice for 32% of historical questions in OVO-Bench and StreamingBench, and models often answer from question/options alone. They introduce 350 human-reviewed evidence-contrastive video pairs where history changes while context stays fixed, evaluating 34 model configurations including Qwen variants with a strict PairAcc metric.

entry.title: MoETok: Sparse Expert Routing for 1D Visual Tokenizers

author.name: Jiahao Guo, Bao Tang, Haoxiang Cao, Jingfeng Yao, Bo Li, Wenyu Liu, Kun Gai, Changqian Yu, Xinggang Wang

entry.summary: The paper analyzes query-based 1D visual tokenizers and finds that learnable queries spontaneously specialize into Content queries for semantics and Detail queries for fine-grained reconstruction. Building on this, MoETok routes tokens through sparsely activated experts matched to these heterogeneous roles, improving both understanding and generation performance.

entry.title: Confidence-Modulated Safety Filtering for End-to-End Policies

author.name: Javier Borquez, Jaime F. Fisac

entry.summary: This paper asks whether a learned policy's confidence should determine the conservativeness of its runtime safety filter, proposing a filter-agnostic pipeline that modulates filter strictness based on policy competence inside and outside the filter's operational design domain. The idea is to relax margins where the policy is reliable while preserving certified safety where the filter's assumptions hold. It is relevant to safely deploying robot foundation models and other end-to-end learned policies.

entry.title: A complete analytical characterization of optimal collision-free motion for two robots

author.name: Jan Kamm, Antonio Terpin, Raffaello D'Andrea

entry.summary: The authors derive a complete analytical characterization of optimal collision-free trajectories for two robots starting and ending at rest under double-integrator dynamics and a squared-acceleration objective, proving the trajectories fall into eight distinct contact families and determining which applies for each configuration. This is a rare closed-form result in a field dominated by numerical methods for nonconvex collision constraints. It complements the authors' large-scale contact-based optimization work.

entry.title: SketchMate: Agentic Geometric Reasoning for Zero-Shot Precision Insertion

author.name: Jiaming Wang

entry.summary: SketchMate enables zero-shot precision insertion of unseen parts by having a VLM agent build a sketch model of geometric primitives and mate frames, measured with geometric tools in multi-view depth, executed by a standard planner and compliant controller. A sketch memory with point-cloud registration transfers stored sketches to new placements, so the VLM is queried only once per task. This bridges the gap between coarse VLM spatial outputs and sub-millimetre industrial precision requirements.

entry.title: Capability-Grounded Agentic Planning

author.name: Shikha Shrestha, William Yeoh, Ning Zhang, Yevgeniy Vorobeychik

entry.summary: Presents CGAP, which compiles a tool catalog deterministically into a PDDL model, uses an LLM to translate natural-language requests into goals, and solves with a classical planner, guaranteeing executable plans at the abstract level. Because tool outputs are unknown in advance, the model tracks input availability rather than values, and an LLM adds entity-specific calls during execution.

entry.title: Experts Exhibit Structured Redundancy: Structure-Preserving Expert Pruning for Mixture-of-Experts Large Language Models

author.name: Tian Wang, Yongding Tao, Yihong Dong, Xiaoming Wu, Ying Guo, Ge Li

entry.summary: The paper shows that expert outputs in MoE layers exhibit structured redundancy, with stable and entropy effective ranks consistently far below the nominal expert count, and reformulates expert pruning as a structure-preserving subset selection problem solved greedily rather than by independent scoring. This reduces the memory overhead of storing all experts in deployed MoE models. Directly relevant to efficient serving of the dominant MoE architectures.

entry.title: What Should LLMs Forget: Reinforcement Unlearning of Knowledge Associations

author.name: Wutong Xu, Yun Qu, Haiyan Feng, Qi Wang, Xiangyang Ji

entry.summary: Reframes LLM unlearning by targeting Knowledge Associations, defined via conditional predictive distributions between query contexts and target knowledge, rather than optimizing entire responses, and applies reinforcement-based optimization for finer-grained forgetting. This enables selective removal of sensitive or copyrighted knowledge while preserving general capability. Directly relevant to privacy and post-training governance of LLMs.

entry.title: GenDSR: Transferring Representations from Video Generation Models for Dynamic Spatial Reasoning

author.name: Ke Yang, Zhenyu Zhang, Jun Li

entry.summary: GenDSR transfers intermediate representations from video generation models into vision-language models for dynamic spatial reasoning, using a raw branch for holistic generative context and a delta branch for temporal variation, combined via task-conditioned tokens. This exploits VGMs as rich sources of spatiotemporal dynamics rather than monolithic priors. It addresses a persistent weakness of VLMs in reasoning about evolving spatial relations.

entry.title: Frozen in Time: How a Physics Foundation Model Forgets Under Sim-to-Real Adaptation

author.name: Haaris Mian, Miles Cranmer, Alessandro Favero, Payel Mukhopadhyay

entry.summary: The paper studies catastrophic forgetting in Walrus-1.3B, a physics foundation model for continuum dynamics, during two-stage sim-to-real adaptation, finding that even brief finetuning rapidly degrades pretrained rollout performance. It provides one of the first systematic analyses of forgetting in scientific foundation models under distribution shift.

entry.title: Regret-Optimal Wasserstein-Robust Linear Regression

author.name: Sloan Nietert, Daniel Kuhn

entry.summary: Studies distributionally robust optimization for multivariate least squares under adversarial 2-Wasserstein distribution shift of size epsilon, characterizing the asymptotic complexity via a problem-specific condition number and proving DRO achieves instance-optimal rates as epsilon goes to zero and minimax rates for fixed epsilon. The paper exposes where DRO is and is not regret-optimal.

entry.title: Scout-Refine-Correct: Teaching Flow Models to Refine Their Own Samples

author.name: Sergey Karpukhin, Aibek Alanov

entry.summary: SRC gives flow-matching image generators inference-time refinement capability: at each step the model takes a scout rollout K steps ahead, extrapolates a full-sample estimate, and feeds it back as a self-conditioning signal, with correction losses applied during training. This improves quality beyond what fixed training budgets allow with step-count tuning alone.

entry.title: More Rules, Longer Lists? Benchmarking Self-Evolving Agents on a Hidden-Rule Curriculum

author.name: Chenjie Qiu, Boyan Xu, Shaobin Shi, Bingfeng Chen, Ruichu Cai, Dongsheng Luo

entry.summary: Introduces CLR-Bench, a curriculum benchmark where agents must infer hidden rules that accumulate across levels, testing whether self-evolving agents genuinely learn unstated rules rather than merely accumulating exception lists. The benchmark uses opaque labels tied to real-world groupings and probes whether base models actually know the underlying group members, distinguishing true rule generalization from rote exception-logging.

entry.title: QUAL: Quantile Alignment Improves Zero-Shot Time-Series Foundation Models

author.name: Junhyeok Kang, Sangjun Han, Jun Seo, Seunghan Lee, Jaehoon Lee, Dongwan Kang, Minjae Kim, Sungdong Yoo, Tae Yoon Lim, Hwanil Choi, Soonyoung Lee, Wonbin Ahn

entry.summary: QUAL is a label-free framework that improves zero-shot time-series foundation models by using a model pool as a probability reference to align quantiles of each member forecast before applying Huber aggregation and rearrangement. This addresses the variability of time-series foundation model accuracy across unseen datasets when no target labels exist for ensembling. It offers a simple, generally applicable post-processing improvement for a growing model family.

entry.title: CryoAtlas: A Large Curated Dataset and Unified Benchmark for Cryo-EM Atomic Model Building

author.name: Mingrui Li, Minzhang Li, Weichen Qin, Yufan Xie, Zhangzhi Xiong, Sixian Shen, Jiakai Zhang, Yuan Pei, Jingyi Yu

entry.summary: Releases CryoAtlas, a curated dataset of 17,809 map-model-sequence entries from EMDB and PDB (through March 2026) and a 618-target benchmark with a shared protocol assessing structural accuracy, map fit, and stereochemical validity for cryo-EM atomic model building. This fills a key resource gap limiting deep learning progress in structural biology. Enables standardized comparison of state-of-the-art methods.

entry.title: RECAST: REconstruction of Chain-of-Thought via Auditable Structured Traces

author.name: Qi Wang, Kang Xu, Chengcheng Wan, Jiangtao Wang

entry.summary: Shows that existing chain-of-thought extraction methods all return zero CoT tokens on Claude-Sonnet-5.5 via standard chat-completions APIs because the failures are structural (no reasoning field, filtered scratchpads), and proposes RECAST to reconstruct auditable structured traces. This highlights a transparency gap for closed-source reasoning models and offers a practical mitigation.

entry.title: Leaner Training, Lower Leakage: Revisiting Memorization in LLM Fine-Tuning with LoRA

author.name: Fei Wang, Baochun Li

entry.summary: Re-examines memorization in LoRA fine-tuning and finds surprising divergences from pre-training and full fine-tuning: model scale and data duplication, strong memorization drivers elsewhere, do not follow the same trend, and LoRA significantly reduces extraction risk under a relaxed similarity metric. This has direct implications for the privacy of fine-tuned models.

entry.title: AutoHebb: Self-Modifying Neural Networks that Zero-Shot Infer and Continually Learn

author.name: Daniel Levine, David van Dijk, Kenneth Kay

entry.summary: AutoHebb introduces autonomous Hebbian networks, online-learning feedforward networks whose learning rules are themselves parameterized and trained, enabling zero-shot inference and continual learning in novel circumstances. The approach aims to balance strong inductive biases for zero-shot generalization with autonomous control of learning for continual learning, while remaining tractable to analysis. It targets long-standing limitations of models of these cognitive abilities.

entry.title: STAR: Steering Action Representations during Inference

author.name: Guangyu Zhao, Yongchang Zhang, Haoxuan Ru, Kaichen He, Haoran Wen, Kun Zhan, Zeyu Zhang, Yin Li, Yiwu Zhong

entry.summary: STAR is a training-free inference-time method for vision-language-action (VLA) robot models that corrects a discovered late-layer grounding gap, where action representations near the output lose task-relevant visual grounding. By applying an exponential moving average over late-layer residual updates and adapting with recent proprioceptive states, STAR lets later action representations inherit object-aware directions from earlier layers without retraining or architectural change. This is significant because it offers a cheap, plug-in improvement for robotic manipulation policies.

entry.title: Accept Changes, Reject Attacks: Robust Memory Management for LLM Agents

author.name: Runze Zhao, Dongruo Zhou, Sumit Kumar Jha, Nathaniel D. Bastian, Ankit Shah

entry.summary: This work formalizes robust memory management for LLM agents, treating outdated-memory retention and memory poisoning as dual failure modes requiring opposite write decisions. It introduces evidence-conditioned accuracy (ECA), a metric that verifies the manager selects records containing supporting evidence rather than merely checking final answers. The framing unifies two previously separate memory-robustness problems for agent systems.

entry.title: When Safety Checks Become Privacy Risks: A Privacy-Preserving Paradigm for LLM Agent Safety Auditing

author.name: Yixiang Luo, Ziheng Ma, Ke Chang, Jian Wang, Jiqiang Liu

entry.summary: Identifies a tension where outsourcing LLM agent safety auditing to external providers exposes sensitive user data such as task descriptions and tool-call arguments. Proposes a paradigm that separates delegated audit computation from plaintext access and execution authority using a three-domain auditing model with encrypted computation and trusted execution interfaces. Addresses a practical gap in deploying safe and privacy-respecting agents.

entry.title: No Channels Left Behind: Understanding Diffusion Acceleration through Residual Gates

author.name: Junha Park, Jaemyung Yu, Jaehui Hwang, Jong-Seok Lee, Dongyoon Han

entry.summary: The paper finds that diffusion transformer acceleration methods like REPA and dispersive regularization substantially reorganize the AdaLN-Zero residual gate, suggesting acceleration arises partly from reshaping residual gating rather than from the auxiliary objectives' explicit feature-structure effects. Accelerated models show markedly higher sensitivity to gate perturbations, supporting this hypothesis.

entry.title: From WSIs to Bulk, Spatial and Single-Cell Transcriptomics via Multi-Scale Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Miguel Andrade, Jos\'e Almeida, Carlos Santiago, Catarina Barata

entry.summary: The work presents a multi-scale GNN that predicts bulk, spatial, and single-cell transcriptomics directly from routine histopathology whole-slide images, using features from the UNI2-h pathology foundation model and spatial graphs at patch and cell levels. This could make expensive spatial transcriptomics insights broadly available from standard pathology slides.

entry.title: ElTab: Elastically Looped Tabular Transformers

author.name: Mieszko Komisarczyk, Saurabh Mathur, Maurice Kraus, Sriraam Natarajan, Kristian Kersting

entry.summary: Proposes ElTab, a single looped tabular transformer trained with supervision at randomly sampled early exits so it can operate across multiple computational budgets at inference time. Across 30 OpenML datasets one ElTab model matches six depth-specific looped models at less than half the training cost and rivals a 12-layer TabPFN-style baseline with 25% fewer inference computations.

entry.title: Li$^{2}$SAO: Lifting Light Singl-Rollout Asynchronous RL Optimization via Group-Relative Actor-Critic Bootstrapping

author.name: Zichen Bai, Yanli Wang, Yang Liu, Junhao Shi, Xueqin Liu, Jinguo Sun, Muye Li, Shaoqiang Zheng, Xuefei Diao, Zhuwei Zeng, Nan Duan, Peng Cao

entry.summary: Analyzes asynchronous RL for LLM post-training and proposes a lightweight, open reproduction of Single-rollout Asynchronous Optimization (SAO) that replaces its closed-source pretrained value model with group-relative actor-critic bootstrapping. Evaluated on single-turn reasoning and multi-turn agentic tasks against GRPO.

entry.title: $\nabla$Mimic: Ultra-Efficient Humanoid Control with Differentiable Simulation

author.name: Weyl Lu, Yubei Chen

entry.summary: Grad-Mimic demonstrates that exact gradients from a differentiable physics simulator can make humanoid motion tracking far more sample-efficient than zeroth-order methods like PPO, once two obstacles are removed: rare unbounded gradient samples from non-smooth contact dynamics, and gradient computation cost. This follows up on world-model surrogate-gradient approaches but differentiates through the simulator itself.

entry.title: From Transcription to Reformulation: Defining and Benchmarking Grounded Generative Speech Recognition

author.name: Qing Wang, Qihan Hu, Hang Lv, Yan Yang, Boqing Liu, Xuechao Zhu, Zehan Li, Hongjie Chen, Jian Kang, Jie Li, Yongxiang Li, Lei Xie

entry.summary: The paper reformulates ASR as Grounded Generative Speech Recognition (GSR), where models produce semantically grounded text rather than a single fixed transcript, defining a reformulation space and a four-level hierarchy from literal transcription to semantic reformulation. This addresses the mismatch between single-ground-truth benchmarks and modern speech language models that generate readable, formatted outputs. It could reshape how speech recognition progress is measured.

entry.title: ReVEAL: Eliciting Role-Aware Latent Visual Evidence from MLLMs for Reasoning Video Object Segmentation

author.name: Zhongyuan Bao, Cunjie He, Lejun Zhang, Zenglin Xu, Yanwei Fu

entry.summary: ReVEAL is a decoupled thinking-with-video framework for reasoning video object segmentation that elicits role-aware Visual Evidence Tokens (target, background, distractor) from MLLM reasoning, aggregated by a Dynamic Attention Layer Router. It avoids costly cross-model alignment between the MLLM and segmentation model.

entry.title: VariaFlow: Uncertainty-Aware Flow Matching for Unsupervised Anomaly Detection

author.name: Arnela Hadzic, Martin Urschler, Cosmin I. Bercea

entry.summary: VariaFlow tackles the key ambiguity in reconstruction-based medical anomaly detection: distinguishing true pathology from healthy anatomical variation. It uses flow matching to estimate predictive variance, scoring residuals against the expected variability of healthy reconstructions at each location rather than against a single reconstruction.

entry.title: WorkIng: A Real-World and Synthetic Highway Work-Zone Benchmark Dataset for Autonomous Navigation

author.name: Xujun Xie, Dominik R\"o{\ss}le, Adithya Mohan, Daniel Cremers, Torsten Sch\"on

entry.summary: WorkIng is a dual-domain benchmark for autonomous driving in highway work zones: WorkIng-Highway provides 360-degree multi-modal real data (128-channel LiDAR, six cameras, RTK-GPS) over 32 km with 12,000+ annotated frames and 227,399 tracked 3D boxes, while WorkIng-CARLA adds simulation across 24 regulation-aware scenarios. It targets a critical edge case missing from existing benchmarks.

entry.title: Rethinking Asymmetry in Self-Supervised 3D Geometry Learning

author.name: Gyeongjin Kang, Freeman Cheng, Botao Ye, Weijie Lyu, Ming-Hsuan Yang, Eunbyung Park

entry.summary: The paper revisits how self-supervised 3D geometry learning from unposed images avoids trivial solutions, arguing the asymmetry should be imposed in 3D representation space rather than through input-space masking or separate branches. With geometric accuracy as the objective, a shared backbone processes all views while held-out views are excluded only from the reconstructed scene.

entry.title: WorldBridge: Bridging Video and Action for Task Generalization in World Action Models

author.name: Jun Cen, Yubo Guo, Hao Li, Liangkai Li, Yaoxu Lyu, Meng Wei, Zeqi Xiao, Sizhe Yang, Yuqiang Yang, Yifan Ye, Shanghang Zhang, Duo Zheng

entry.summary: WorldBridge studies World Action Models for robot task generalization, separating video generalization (predicting visual evolution of new tasks) from action generalization (a video-to-action bridge converting predictions into behavior). Experiments on RoboTwin 2.0 show that adding videos of out-of-distribution tasks without action labels substantially improves over video-action-only supervision (25.07% baseline success). This is significant because it quantifies how video supervision can substitute for scarce robot action data.

entry.title: ROOF: Learning Humanoid Fall Recovery under Overhead Constraints

author.name: Yidan Lu, Jiayuan Yu, Zongrui Cai, Jingwen Sun, Jinrui Han, Jing Wang, Ping Luo, Peng Lu

entry.summary: ROOF introduces a reinforcement learning method for humanoid fall recovery beneath overhead obstacles, rewarding incremental reduction of robot-obstacle overlap without prescribing an escape path. A learned motion prior plus posture-dependent support and joint-stall costs shape a single proprioceptive policy that decides when to clear the obstacle, establish support, and rise. It recovers in 88.5% of simulated trials under plates, addressing a coupled problem ignored by standard fall-recovery work.

entry.title: Instrumental Transfer Learning for Solution Operators

author.name: Tongyu Li, Zhuoyuan Li, Ruoxu Tan

entry.summary: This paper proposes a structured transfer learning method for learning solution operators of differential equations when target-system data is scarce, leveraging abundant data from related source systems. It models unknown sparse differences between governing equations via a candidate term library and uses the resolvent identity with a whitened instrumental variable approach to construct unbiased source estimating equations for the target operator. This matters for scientific machine learning where collecting physical observations is expensive.

entry.title: MEMIG: Self-evolving Memory Construction for Antibody Optimization

author.name: Yunhui Jang, Zach Wang, Jai Doshi, Kangway Chuang, Sidney Lisanza, Taylor Joren

entry.summary: MEMIG argues that agent memory for biomolecule optimization should be indexable, quantitative, and structured rather than free-form text, since scientific experience consists of oracle measurements under specific contexts that rewriting destroys. The system stores and retrieves quantitative intervention records to guide antibody optimization by self-evolving LLM agents. This is a thoughtful critique of text-based agent memory in scientific domains.

entry.title: Specification-Guided Generation for Large Language Models

author.name: Alessandro Previti, Konstantinos Vandikas, Mario Alviano, Mats Carlsson, Albin Larsson Forsberg, Alexandros Nikou, Athanasios Karapantelakis, Aneta Vulgarakis

entry.summary: Introduces a neuro-symbolic decoding framework that filters candidate tokens at each step against a formal specification, guaranteeing outputs satisfy the specification by construction in a forward-only variant, with a backtracking variant for revising earlier choices. It is model-agnostic and goes beyond syntactic constrained decoding. Addresses reliable generation of structured outputs against formal requirements.

entry.title: In-Model Context Compression with Agentic Soft Tokens for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

author.name: Xuning He, Kai Fan, Runyu Zhang, Binghuan Wang, Yuxiang Zhang, Xue Jiang, Yihong Dong

entry.summary: ASTC is a training-free method that compresses long-horizon agent contexts into soft tokens using the model's native recurrent dynamics to identify already-absorbed information, avoiding lossy external hard-token rewriters. It aims to cut computational cost while preserving decision-relevant evidence within the model's own representations. This targets a core scalability problem for sustained agent tasks.

entry.title: Aligning MLLMs with the Latent Structure of Human Cognition via Behavior-Derived Semantic Dimensions

author.name: Ning E, Changde Du, Yizhuo Lu, Huiguang He

entry.summary: Proposes aligning multimodal LLMs with the latent structure of human similarity judgments using a behavior-derived semantic embedding space with 66 interpretable dimensions built from 4.70 million human Odd-One-Out judgments. Converts the most salient decision dimension per triplet into dimension-grounded linguistic rationales for training. Aims to make MLLM decision criteria better match human mental representations.

entry.title: D2ML: Models for Direct-to-Biology Small Molecule Screening

author.name: AkshatKumar Nigam, Neri Amara, Hillary Dequina, Dyana Kenanova, Seth Malmersjo, Fiorella Ruggiu, Raymond V. Fucini, Jack Sadowsky, Stig K. Hansen, Imran S. Haque

entry.summary: Develops assay-aware ML models for direct-to-biology screening, predicting activity from single-point crude screens, relative potency from crude dose-response assays, and absolute potency from purified compounds. Key insight: potency ratios between targets tested from the same crude well retain selectivity information despite uncertain concentrations.

entry.title: When Depth Lies: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models on Mirror-Induced RGB-D Ambiguity

author.name: Hao Yin, Tianchen Guo, Heming Du, Yan Ke, Yanbin Liu, Xin Yu

entry.summary: The paper introduces a mirror-centric RGB-D benchmark of 1,011 images from 525 real-world reflective scenes to test whether VLMs treat depth readings as physical distance, which mirrors systematically violate. It exposes an unexamined failure surface where reflections look like objects but corrupt depth, misleading spatial reasoning.

entry.title: Learning from Physical Experience:Context-Space Adaptation for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Yihan Zeng, Yisu Li, Kaixin Huang, Marc WuDunn, Amelia Kovacs, Mikael Harseno, Kimmy Lin, Porter Hunley, Fred Shentu, Philipp Wu, Zhongyu Li, Zike Yan

entry.summary: This paper finds through real-world experiments that ChatGPT-6-Astra, an existing state-of-the-art general-purpose reasoner released in September 2026, can act as a physically actionable manipulation policy with fine manipulation and spatial reasoning. It then introduces LEXP, a harness combining task-level planning with an experience module that interprets execution evidence and retains lessons with applicability conditions for context-space adaptation. The work probes how frontier reasoning models can ground themselves in physical interaction.

entry.title: Confident Fools or Careful Searchers? A Behavioural Study of When LLMs Search Beyond Their Static Internal Memory

author.name: Nipun D. Pathirage, Kwan Srijomkwan

entry.summary: This paper audits the actual tool-use search decisions of deployed LLM assistants using a 400-question benchmark mixing inside-knowledge questions (which should be answered directly) and post-cutoff outside-knowledge questions (which should trigger search or abstention). It measures whether models over-search, under-search, or answer confidently without support. This is valuable for understanding when agentic systems waste latency and cost or produce unsupported answers.

entry.title: ImplicitHop: Evaluating knowledge integration across context and memory

author.name: Alexander Detkov, Dashiel Karish, Matthew Oleynikov, Matt Thomson

entry.summary: ImplicitHop provides two complementary benchmarks for evaluating deductive reasoning in LLMs as a function of inference depth: a formal graph benchmark with controlled topologies and a knowledge composition benchmark grounded in real-world knowledge graphs. It compares how models integrate facts from training (memory) versus in-context, testing whether models propagate long-range implications of new information. This matters for understanding a core reasoning limitation of LLMs.

entry.title: RECITE: Revising Eligibility Criteria Incorporating Textual Evidence

author.name: Russell Ro, Reza Abbasi-Asl

entry.summary: Presents RECITE, a framework that automatically discovers and implements evidence-based revisions to overly restrictive clinical trial eligibility criteria, built from a curated dataset of 11,913 instances across 5,735 ClinicalTrials.gov trials. It benchmarks fifteen LLM configurations under context-truncated and retrieval-augmented settings. This has direct potential to improve clinical trial enrollment.

entry.title: Prune Gradually, Adapt Sparsely: Efficient Pruning of Large Language Models at Extreme Sparsity

author.name: Jean Lucien Randrianantenaina, Hung Nguyen, Nasib Ullah, Jinbin Zhang, Nilesh Gupta, Inderjit S. Dhillon, Rohit Babbar

entry.summary: Proposes ETAPS, a pruning method that gradually tightens a global sparsity constraint while adapting only sparsely, achieving quality near the extreme-sparsity state of the art without the model-sized optimizer state and auxiliary variables required by direct mask optimization. It addresses the quality-cost trade-off in LLM pruning at high sparsity.

entry.title: Hear No Evil: Detecting Gradient Leakage by Malicious Servers in Federated Learning

author.name: Fei Wang, Baochun Li

entry.summary: Provides the first comprehensive defender-side analysis of malicious gradient leakage attacks in federated learning, showing a fundamental trade-off: attacks cannot be both highly effective at reconstruction and stealthy enough to evade detection, especially with normalization and federated averaging. This enables practical attack detection for FL deployments.

entry.title: A Theoretical Framework for Understanding and Building "Any-task inference" Capable Foundation Models

author.name: Matthew McDermott, Florent Pollet, Payal Chandak, Gregory Kondas, Liat Friedman Antwarg, Noa Dagan, Isaac Kohane

entry.summary: The paper provides a formal, interface-based mathematical definition of any-task inference (ATI) foundation models that map data samples and task specifications directly to predictions over a defined space of tasks, distinct from pre-train-then-fine-tune models. It shows all ATI foundation models decompose via a universal task reduction into encoder, model, and decoder components. This offers shared vocabulary and design principles across heterogeneous foundation model efforts.

entry.title: From Evaluation to Evolution: Benchmarking Image Editing and Evolving Image Models

author.name: Jun He, Canmiao Fu, Ying Zhang, Zhipeng Huang, Chenyu Mu, Yazhen Xie, Chen Li, Jing Lyu, Weijia Li, Xiang Zhang

entry.summary: WeGenEditBench is a large image-editing benchmark with 2,740 evaluation instances across 148 task types spanning single-image, text-intensive, and multi-reference editing. It uses shared pre-generated checklists to decompose requests into atomic requirements, deriving item-level deductions before summarizing into scores for execution, preservation, quality, and correctness, and translates failures into improvement priorities. It aims to move evaluation from aggregate scores toward actionable model evolution.

entry.title: When Steering Shifts Discourse: Identifying and Intervening on Discourse-Level Changes due to Activation Steering in LLMs

author.name: Shivam Adarsh, Hetianyu Huang, Lau Safin, Maria Maistro, Christina Lioma

entry.summary: Shows that activation steering in LLMs systematically and unintentionally changes discourse dimensions of generated text such as formality, use of evidence, and ambiguity, beyond the intended behavioral change. Moves beyond coarse perplexity-based measurement and proposes a corrective intervention to counter these side effects. Relevant to safe deployment of inference-time control techniques.

entry.title: There Is No Free Loop: When Does Looping a Trained Model Pay for Its Inference Compute?

author.name: Rhea Sanjay Sukthanker, Pashmina Cameron

entry.summary: This paper empirically examines whether adding recurrent loops to a pretrained transformer (re-applying layer blocks without increasing parameters) justifies the per-token inference cost, comparing against equally sized unlooped models and best compute-matched alternatives. It clarifies that loops learned in pretraining may pay off while post-hoc loops often do not.

entry.title: FARO: Function-Space Adaptive Return-to-Risk Optimization via Cross-Block Equal-Risk-Contribution Budget Allocation

author.name: Xiaojun Wu, Cehao Yang, Xuhui Jiang, Chengjin Xu, Jia Li, Jian Guo

entry.summary: FARO is a function-space adaptive LLM optimizer that treats parameter-block partitioning as a learned decision, assigning each block an update geometry based on realized counterfactual return and reallocating per-block budgets via equal risk contribution, a risk-parity principle borrowed from portfolio theory. It removes hand-designed optimizer recipes on GPT-style models.

entry.title: UpLoop: Training Looped Transformers via Upcycling at No Extra Pretraining Compute

author.name: Cheng Liang, Tengfei Zhang, Ya Zhang, Yanfeng Wang, Zhouhan Lin

entry.summary: UpLoop is a pretraining schedule that trains looped Transformers via layer upcycling while exactly matching a dense baseline in parameter count, tokens, and FLOPs: it starts shallow, grows depth by copying learned layers, and reinvests saved compute into repeated execution of a shared middle block. This makes the reasoning benefits of looped models available at no extra pretraining cost.

entry.title: Trainable Vector Quantization for Large Language Models

author.name: Anastasiia Prutianova, Alina Bogdanova, Mikhail Shutov, Dmitrii Poimanov, Anatoly Gorkov, Ilia Zharikov

entry.summary: Presents TVQ, a method enabling gradient-based optimization of vector-quantized LLM weights via straight-through estimation, moving beyond training-free layer-wise reconstruction approaches. This allows arbitrary objective minimization on quantized models, addressing performance degradation under extreme compression.

entry.title: Robust-by-Design Distributional Learning from Contaminated Samples

author.name: Nevena Gligi\'c, Arya Farahi

entry.summary: Studies supervised and unsupervised learning when the observed sample is a contaminated mixture of target and unknown contaminant distributions, a common situation in scraped and auto-curated datasets. The authors design estimators that provably converge to the correct target distribution using a clean reference sample plus noisy membership scores and a small audited subset.

entry.title: DAPS: Dependency-Aware Premise Selection for LLM Theorem Proving

author.name: Zixuan Chen, Wenyuan Jiang, Junling Wang, Mrinmaya Sachan, Yinya Huang

entry.summary: DAPS improves premise selection for LLM-based theorem proving in Lean 4 by exploiting mathematical dependency structure rather than pure semantic similarity, curating two underused dependency resources including a systematic mining of 53 Lean repositories. It addresses frequency-skewed retrieval, isolated pairwise ranking, and out-of-distribution degradation that plague existing neural selectors.

entry.title: DecisionRank: On-Policy Distillation for Decision-Model Rerankers

author.name: Yanran Wu, Dian Yu, Chongyang Bai, Jieyi Zhang, Rui Liu, Tianyi Chen, Shike Mei, Hang Cui, Frank Shyu, Sandeep Pandey, Luke Simon, Chunwei Liu, Xi Liu

entry.summary: DecisionRank trains decision-model rerankers through item-space on-policy distillation: the student's document scores are sorted into a ranked rollout that a generative teacher then supervises with conditional feedback, bridging the representational gap between ranking-by-decoding teachers and score-predicting students. This preserves the latency advantages of decision models while transferring generative ranking knowledge. The author list includes Meta AI researchers, suggesting industrial grounding.

entry.title: UFMF: Radar-Guided Kinematic Priors for Real-Time 4D Occupancy Forecasting

author.name: Zeping Zhang, Zhuoya Zhao, Robert Lagani\`ere

entry.summary: UFMF is a real-time 4D occupancy forecaster combining an attention-free diagonal state-space temporal core with radar-guided velocity-aware dynamic priors. It aims to bridge the gap between computationally heavy generative occupancy models and lightweight BEV forecasters that blur fast-moving actors.

entry.title: VoxLution: Evolving Voxels for High-Fidelity 3D Scene Generation

author.name: Daoyi Gao, Xinyi Zhang, Alexey Bokhovkin, Lei Li, Angela Dai

entry.summary: VoxLution is a coarse-to-fine transformer that generates high-fidelity indoor 3D scenes by formulating 3D super-resolution as sequence modeling over multi-resolution sparse voxel grids, using a training-free resolution-invariant tokenization scheme. It overcomes the overly smooth geometry typical of prior generative 3D scene models.

entry.title: Nereus: A Large-Scale Underwater Dataset for Fine-Grained Attribute Understanding and Grounded Counting Perception

author.name: Jingtao Deng, Zihao Jin, Yuehe Chen, Feixiang He, Shuiwang Li, Dan Zeng

entry.summary: Nereus is a large-scale underwater perception dataset with 88K images jointly supporting fine-grained object attribute understanding and grounded counting, going beyond the coarse labels and total-count supervision of existing underwater benchmarks. It enables organism-level ecological analysis with spatially grounded evidence.

entry.title: CaPtain: A Pipeline for Post-Training Code-as-Policy Robot Agents

author.name: Yijia Fan, Xilin He, Yilei Jiang, Dongming Wu, Jiaxu Wang, Xiangyu Yue

entry.summary: CaPtain is an open post-training pipeline (SFT followed by multi-turn RL) that turns a small open vision-language model into a code-as-policy robot manipulation agent, avoiding reliance on prompting closed frontier models or delegating to VLAs. The work applies the now-standard agent training recipe from coding and web tasks to robot manipulation. This matters because it demonstrates small open models can perform code-based robot control when properly trained.

entry.title: HIPC: Humanoid Iterative Planning and Control via Goal-Conditioned Motion Closure

author.name: Yi Han, Xingyu Chen, Zixuan Lang, Qianyang Wu, Yuhang Lin, Ji Ma, Liang Li, Dongting Li, Xinpeng Liu, Ruoli Dai, Hesheng Wang, Renjing Xu, Lei Han

entry.summary: HIPC is a real-time humanoid planning-and-control framework that unifies a generative motion model with tracking into a single closed-loop planner, addressing drift and inability to adapt to disturbances in open-loop motion-generator-plus-controller pipelines. It handles the distribution-shift problem that makes naive state feedback cause jitter or falls via a goal-conditioned motion closure. This targets a key gap between generative humanoid motion models and physical robustness.

entry.title: META-Robot: Self-Cognition and Capability Scaling in Agentic Robots

author.name: Xuanzhi Feng, Zeyu Liu, Weiheng Gao, Xinchen Li, Jiankun Tang, Fangqi Zhu, Quanxin Shou, Hao Chen, Zhengyang Yan, Hualei Zhang, Junhao Li, Zhiyao Wu, Jie Zhang, Song Guo

entry.summary: META-Robot is a framework for LLM-based robotic agents that couples self-cognition with capability scaling. Action-level predicates make execution outcomes explicit for LLM reasoning, allowing the agent to identify its own limitations, extend evaluation criteria, and guide structured skill expansion, with proprioceptive feedback as additional grounding. This targets the problem that LLM robot systems lack awareness of what they can and cannot do.

entry.title: Calibration of Large Model Quantization based on HiFloat4 Format

author.name: Jing Huang, Yu Cheng, Ziwei Yu, Lan Zhao, Sitan Li, Guangxiu Yao, Xin Wang, Yuanyong Luo, Hengyi Liang, Ting Li, Bo Liu, Hu Liu, Michael Bi Mi, Heng Liao

entry.summary: This work develops calibration methods for quantizing large language models to the emerging HiFloat4 (HiF4) block floating-point format, which uses a three-level scaling hierarchy for a larger dynamic range than MXFP4 or NVFP4. Calibration is shown to be essential for recovering the accuracy lost when moving to 4-bit precision. Efficient 4-bit inference is a major lever for deployment cost reduction.

entry.title: LEAP: Efficient LLM Inference Scheduling with Generalizable Length Prediction

author.name: Kwan Yan, Jialun Zhong, Yanzeng Li

entry.summary: Proposes LEAP, a length-prediction system for LLM serving that reuses prefill hidden states with a linear readout and updates online to handle domain and task shifts, running asynchronously on CPU. This improves latency-aware scheduling without costly predictor retraining. Relevant to practical efficiency of LLM inference infrastructure.

entry.title: CausalWAM: Learning the Causes of Actions in World Action Models

author.name: Juntao Cheng, Jinzhou Tang, Fan Feng, Henrik I. Christensen, Yujia Zheng

entry.summary: Proposes separating action-relevant latent causes from nuisance variables in world action models, proving that under a sparsity constraint the latents generating actions are identifiable, so actions derive from the actual causes of demonstrated behavior rather than entangled imitation. It connects causal representation learning with embodied policy learning.

entry.title: Kernel-based Interpolatory Methods for Context Compression of Attention Mechanisms

author.name: Michel Fabrice Serret, Laura Grigori

entry.summary: The paper formulates KV-cache compression in the Hilbert space of the attention kernel, representing attention as a ratio of two linear maps whose interpolant is the ratio of interpolants. From this formalism it derives two novel compression methods, GAIM and Q-DAIM, based on interpolation of the linear maps directly. This offers a mathematically grounded alternative to heuristic context compression.

entry.title: Where, When, and How Many Bits? Scaling Laws for SGD with Stochastic Rounding

author.name: Zhichao Wang, Michael W. Mahoney

entry.summary: This theoretical work derives matched upper and lower bounds on prediction error for stochastic rounding in low-precision SGD training, using a two-layer linear network with power-law data spectra. It analyzes how model size, training time, and precision schedules interact, deriving the smallest usable precision for fixed precisions and constant learning rates with parameter averaging. It provides a theoretical foundation for choosing bit-widths during low-precision training.

entry.title: KEEPER: Learning Control-Sufficient Textual Memory for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

author.name: Jinkyeong Choi, Chaebin Jeong, Junsung Jeon, Donghyeon Park

entry.summary: Studies self-consistency bias in recursive textual memory for long-horizon LLM agents, where incorrect claims persist through later memory updates despite corrective observations. Presents KEEPER, a comparative analysis of four auxiliary objectives along information-content and update-sensitivity axes, finding reward-related prediction yields the best task performance before and after offline reinforcement learning. Includes claim-level analysis documenting error persistence.

entry.title: Continual Reinforcement Learning Is an Integration Problem

author.name: Nis Meinert, Jakob Gawlikowski, Edward Grant, Max Cyprys, Nathan Schurr, Neil Boston, Alfredo Ibias, Milind Tambe, Janusz Marecki

entry.summary: The paper presents ten desiderata for reinforcement-learning agents that learn continually over a continuing lifetime and uses them to assess a representative selection of existing approaches and benchmarks. It argues that no published evaluation demonstrates integration of all ten properties in a single agent, reframing continual RL progress as fundamentally an integration problem.

entry.title: New Lower Bounds for Private PAC Learning

author.name: Prathamesh Dharangutte, Amartya Sanyal

entry.summary: Provides a framework for proving sample-complexity lower bounds for realizable PAC learning under approximate differential privacy, showing that VC and Littlestone dimensions do not determine private sample complexity even for improper learners. It introduces the Independent Class Packing (ICP) parameter and proves matching Omega bounds for DP-PAC learners.

entry.title: Coarse-Graining Optimal Transport for Rollout-Free Post-Training of Flow Matching

author.name: Soon Hoe Lim, Aditi Gupta, Michael W. Mahoney, N. Benjamin Erichson

entry.summary: Introduces ReCouple, a framework constructing coarse-grained optimal-transport couplings for rollout-free post-training of flow matching models, analyzing why making couplings more OT-like does not consistently help in the low-NFE regime given continuous sources and finite data and capacity. Includes extensions of the basic framework.

entry.title: Exact Theory and Optimal Stepsizes for Stochastic Gradient Descent in Smooth Convex Minimization

author.name: Benjamin Grimmer, Qining Shen

entry.summary: The authors provide an exact worst-case analysis of stochastic gradient descent with arbitrary (possibly nonconstant) stepsize schedules in smooth convex optimization, under conditionally zero-mean bounded-variance gradient noise. For problems with dimension d >= N+1, they derive matching lower bounds showing their guarantees are tight, and prove minimax optimality of the resulting stepsize schedules when the variance bound is sufficiently large. This offers rigorous, practical guidance on stepsize design for SGD.

entry.title: PathoJev: Efficient Pathology Decisions from Shared Visual Context

author.name: Chengyang Zhang, Wenchuan Zhang, Bo Li, Xinyu Liu, Jiaming Yang, Mengran Li, Jie Chen, Wei Ju, Yuhao Yi, Hong Bu, Jiancheng Lv

entry.summary: PathoJev is a 9B pathology model that encodes a whole slide once and predicts answer probabilities for multiple structured questions in parallel over the shared visual context, reusing a hybrid recurrent backbone's states to limit per-question computation. Across three whole-slide benchmarks it reduces latency between visual evidence and usable clinical decisions. This applies the decision-model paradigm to a high-stakes medical imaging workflow with clear practical payoff.

entry.title: Drone-PUR: From Visual Clue Discovery to Understanding and Reasoning in UAV Scenes

author.name: Jiahe Wu, Bing Cao, Xingyue Guo, Ruipu Zhao, Beiming Yu, Jiekang Feng, Qinghua Hu, Pengfei Zhu

entry.summary: Drone-PUR is a large UAV-scene dataset and benchmark organized around perception, understanding, and reasoning, requiring models to combine multiple visual clues into grounded conclusions. It provides 195k samples across 11 tasks including single images, sequences, and cross-modal data.

entry.title: TalkFlow: Structured Latent Flow Matching for Speech Driven Holistic Motion Generation

author.name: Xinmu Wang, Fumi Honda, Xiang Gao, Xianfeng Gu, Xiyun Song, Heather Yu

entry.summary: TalkFlow generates coordinated facial expressions, hand gestures, and body movements from speech using a structured three-stream latent flow-matching framework that preserves part-specific dynamics. It addresses instability of direct high-dimensional motion modeling and loss of detail in overly compact latent spaces.

entry.title: Defining Page-Centric Visual Document Retrieval and Evaluating Existing Benchmarks

author.name: Chongzhi Zhang, Yuqi Zuo, Aixin Sun

entry.summary: The paper formalizes page-centric Visual Document Retrieval (VDR), with pages as indexing units and document context available for relevance assessment, distinguishing page/document granularities and three retrieval paradigms. It then audits 42 existing benchmarks against this formulation.

entry.title: HandMimicX: Learning Human-Like Dexterous Manipulation via an Object-Centric Policy from Egocentric Videos

author.name: Zihan Gao, Yufei Liu, Yuhong Zhang, Zhen Yu, Xinhao Huang, Zhinan You, Kai W. Ho, Zipeng Ye, Peng Jiao, Haoqian Wang

entry.summary: HandMimicX learns dexterous skills from egocentric human RGB-D videos using an object-centric framework: the RL objective is defined in terms of object motion to decouple skill from specific hand trajectories, with constraints on hand-object interaction states to keep configurations anatomically natural. It aims to turn a single human demonstration into a spatially generalizable robot skill. This is a promising answer to the persistent human-video-to-robot transfer problem.

entry.title: Interaction-Aware Sampling-Based Motion Planning for Autonomous Surface Vessels in Urban Waterways

author.name: Elia Trevisan, Alejandro Gonzalez-Garcia, Jan Swevers, Javier Alonso-Mora

entry.summary: The authors present a decentralized MPPI-based motion planner for autonomous surface vessels that jointly computes the ego trajectory and predicts other vessels' trajectories to capture interactions. Traffic rules are encoded as discontinuous costs, which sampling-based MPC naturally handles without smoothing approximations. Evaluation on real Amsterdam canal maps demonstrates applicability to congested urban waterways.

entry.title: On Statistical-Computational Gaps in Graph Combinatorial Testing Problems

author.name: Ikjun Choi, Pratik Patil, Alessandro Rinaldo

entry.summary: This work studies high-dimensional hypothesis testing where a signal is supported on the edges of an unknown subgraph, characterizing sharp statistical and computational detection thresholds for various combinatorial graph alternatives under Gaussian observations. The analysis bounds second moments of full and low-degree likelihood ratios and compares against scan, average, and maximum tests, yielding hardness results under a low-degree conjecture. It contributes to the growing theory of statistical-computational gaps.

entry.title: Can Personal Requirements Become Supervision for Planning?

author.name: Junwei Wu, Runze Yan, Yuzhang Xie, Hanqi Luo, Ziwei Dong, Jiaying Lu, Xiao Hu, Carl Yang

entry.summary: Evaluates LLM agents on dietitian-approved weekly meal planning under joint disease- and medication-specific constraints, finding that thirteen models including GPT-6.1 Sol pass under 3% of complete plans via direct generation, and under 8% even with explicit rules and tools. Proposes Noura, which pairs LLM planning with executable personal specifications to substantially improve feasibility.

entry.title: When Should AI Agents Ask? Clarification Requests Under Limited Human Attention

author.name: Hanzhao Wang, Shengjie Liu, Zhengchao Wang

entry.summary: The paper formulates how multiple AI agents sharing one human with limited attention should coordinate decisions to search for missing information themselves versus asking the human for clarification, casting the problem as a dynamic program over search, ask, and continue actions. This addresses an increasingly common real-world scenario of one person supervising many delegated agents. The results clarify when an agent should ask versus proceed autonomously.

entry.title: Evidence-Guided Recovery for AI Agents with Ambiguous Tool Outcomes and Partial Execution

author.name: Genliang Zhu, Xiaobo Chen, Ziyuan Wang, Chu Wang

entry.summary: Formulates evidence-guided task recovery for AI agents facing ambiguous tool outcomes after timeouts, with an admissibility check covering authorization timing and residual effects, and a terminal certificate separating actual goal satisfaction from publicly supported safe completion. Evaluated in a finite study of 37 assignments. Addresses the underexplored safety problem of acting when prior tool executions may have partially committed.

entry.title: DAMI: Dual-Axis Memory Initialization for Enhanced Long-Context Retrieval in Gated Linear Attention

author.name: Zhangchi Feng, Harry Jiang, Yangyifei Luo, Ray Zhang, Richong Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces Dual-Axis Memory Initialization, which jointly configures A_log and dt_bias before training in gated linear recurrences, assigning geometric timescales across heads and a low-high-low input-sensitivity profile across layers, calibrated with a small activation sample. It improves long-context retrieval in linear attention through initialization alone.

entry.title: Different Models, Shared Failures: Auditing Frozen-Encoder Pools for Medical Segmentation

author.name: Eunseob Choi, Kyeonghun Kim, Hyuk-Jae Lee, Nam-Joon Kim

entry.summary: Introduces CoFailMed, an audit of correlated failures across pretrained-encoder pools for medical image segmentation, evaluating 11 public encoders with frozen features and controlled readouts across five 2D tasks. Finds that models from the same encoder family fail on overlapping cases, so nominally diverse pools have effective sizes far below their nominal count (1.56-2.92 for four-member pools). Highlights that model-count diversity does not imply failure diversity.

entry.title: Certified Behavioral Retention for Continual Adaptation with Held-Out Anchors

author.name: Ahanaf Hasan Ariq, Abrar Shahid

entry.summary: CABA is a candidate-agnostic post-update gate for continual adaptation that compares old and candidate policies on frozen representations and certifies the largest interpolation coefficient whose worst-anchor forward KL divergence stays within a declared behavioral budget, without needing action labels or full trajectories. It separates measured anchor retention from off-anchor guarantees.

entry.title: Locality-Controlled Out-of-Distribution Guidance for Robust Regulatory DNA Sequence Design

author.name: Dabin Jeong, Marwane Bourdim, Mo Lotfollahi

entry.summary: The paper addresses diffusion-based regulatory DNA sequence design, showing that single-reward evaluation can hide reward hacking and decomposing evaluation into property, novelty, and plausibility. It proposes locality-controlled out-of-distribution guidance, arguing guidance should be a matter of locality rather than just magnitude, and identifies an evaluation regime no existing baseline satisfies.

entry.title: Learning Stabilizing Latent Feedback Controllers via Multi-Step Backward Losses

author.name: Paul Lutkus, Lars Lindemann, Stephen Tu

entry.summary: Shows that for linear time-invariant systems, learning linear autoencoders with multi-step prediction-reconstruction (backward) losses provably recovers latent structure sufficient for stabilization. A long enough reconstruction horizon guarantees that an H-infinity controller designed on the learned latent model stabilizes the true system via output feedback.

entry.title: When Is a Game a Markov Decision Process? Correspondences Between Game Theory and Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Eduardo C. Garrido-Merch\'an

entry.summary: A monograph formalizing the correspondence between game theory and reinforcement learning, proving in what precise senses a game is an MDP: definitional identity, exact solution-preserving reduction, or structural analogy with known failure conditions. It upgrades folklore analogies between the two fields into theorems.

entry.title: CoFiBreak: A Coarse-to-Fine Diversity Reward for Effective Multi-Turn Jailbreak

author.name: Jialin Song, Xiaodong Liu, Weiwei Yang, Mingqian Feng, Chengquan Guo, Qiyao Ma, Carolyn Buractaon, Anson Ho, Wuyang Chen, Christopher White

entry.summary: Proposes CoFiBreak, a coarse-to-fine diversity reward for GRPO-based automated red teaming that prevents attacker LLMs from collapsing onto narrow prompt sets, preserving attack success while improving strategy and content diversity at low inference cost. Better diversity reduces bias in safety evaluations toward near-duplicate attack patterns.

entry.title: Prevented is Not Protected: What Attack Success Rate Hides about RAG

author.name: Chahana Dahal, Zuobin Xiong

entry.summary: This paper shows that attack success rate alone obscures the true security posture of defended RAG systems, introducing Aligned RAG Evaluation, a matched-query protocol jointly examining clean and poisoned responses with and without defense, LLM-judge endorsement, and retrieval-dependence controls. The framework separates prevented attacks from defense-introduced failures and surface target mentions from genuine model endorsement. This is a meaningful methodological upgrade for RAG security evaluation.

entry.title: MATS: A Multi-Agent Framework for Controllable and Reflective Tumor Synthesis

author.name: Zhongnan Shi, Keyang Zhou, Siyi Li, Qichao Ying, Xinchen Ma, Shuyi Gong, Wei Tang, Sheng Li, Zhenxing Qian

entry.summary: MATS is a multi-agent framework for text-controllable, cross-organ tumor synthesis on medical images that profiles morphological distributions to amplify underrepresented subtypes, localizes organs, and verifies generated tumors anatomically. It addresses controllability and quality-verification gaps in diffusion-based medical data synthesis.

entry.title: Cross-Embodiment Motion Planning by Coupling Body-Agnostic World Model with Differentiable Ego-Dynamics

author.name: Zhidong Wang, Zirui Li, Haoran Xu, Yujie Yan, Zitong Shan, Jingsong Liang, Han Yu, Chen Lv

entry.summary: Hourglass is an architecture that factorizes cross-embodiment motion planning into a body-agnostic world model and a differentiable ego-dynamics module, exploiting the insight that on flat ground embodiment affects planner observations only through camera ego-motion. This avoids both command-conditioned latent dynamics bound to one action space and per-robot training/distillation. It contributes a principled route to pooling data across different robot bodies.

entry.title: Stochastic Mirror Descent under Dependent Observations

author.name: Gersende Fort, Anatoli Juditsky, Jiaming Liang

entry.summary: This paper provides non-asymptotic convergence guarantees for stochastic mirror descent when the noisy first-order oracle produces dependent observations, replacing the classical i.i.d. assumption with a flexible forgetting condition covering geometric or polynomial dependence. It derives explicit finite-sample accuracy bounds recovering O(1/T) and O(1/sqrt(T)) rates, instantiated on dependent-regressor linear regression and drift estimation for functional data. This extends core optimization theory to realistic dependent-data settings.

entry.title: P-ContextBench: From Personal Fact Recall to Personalized Agent Behavior

author.name: Grant Nasir Brown, Abdul Basir Bari, Anmol Tadikonda, Isabel Song

entry.summary: Introduces P-ContextBench, a benchmark that evaluates safe and accurate use of personal context via population-structured synthetic digital humans whose traits are embedded as implicit evidence across fragmented, evolving mobile-app records. It assesses five capabilities from single-source fact recovery to personalized agent behavior, addressing privacy-constrained personalization evaluation.

entry.title: Counterfactual Pairwise Augmentation Improves Small Pointwise LLM Judges

author.name: Mohammad Zangooei, Peyvand Teymoori, Mohammad Robati Shirzad, Soroosh Shahtalebi

entry.summary: CPA improves small language model pointwise judges used to gate agentic system steps by synthesizing counterfactual responses to the same query that carry the opposite label, making the criterion's decision boundary explicit during fine-tuning. This addresses the underdetermination of boundaries by pointwise labels, where responses to different queries differ in many ways at once. Better small judges would make agentic gating cheaper and more reliable.

entry.title: scAnyOmics: Foundation-Model Distillation for Any-to-Any Completion of Multi-omics Virtual Cells

author.name: Zhaoqi Song, Ye Du, Yusuke Iwasawa, Yutaka Matsuo, Qian Niu

entry.summary: Introduces scAnyOmics, a generative framework distilling a frozen single-cell foundation model into a multimodal student that integrates scRNA-seq, protein markers, and scATAC-seq into a shared representation to predict and reconstruct missing modalities. Built on a large assembled dataset of 690 samples or more for limited-pairing scenarios. Advances AI for cellular state modeling in biology.

entry.title: Verify--Backtrack Loop: Structured Precondition Recovery for Long-Horizon Language Agents

author.name: Mingyang Liu, Qingcan Kang, Shixiong Kai, Tao Zhong, Mingxuan Yuan, Xin Li, Linqi Song

entry.summary: Introduces VBL, a training-free extension of ReAct that represents failure recovery as structured planning-state updates, maintaining task decomposition and explicitly linking terminal goals, active goals, and failure sources for precondition discovery and backtracking. This moves beyond free-form textual reflection for long-horizon agent recovery. Targets a core failure mode of language agents in interactive environments.

entry.title: TSBPO: Tree-Structured Branching for Policy Optimization in Interactive Language Agents

author.name: Rui Yu, Chong Mu, Jinchuan Zhang

entry.summary: Presents TSBPO, a tree-structured sampling-to-update paradigm for training interactive language agents that jointly handles continuation selection, credit assignment via sibling-segment and observation-group advantages, and token-level loss aggregation for multi-token actions. Addresses three coupled problems in outcome-based agent training within a single loop. Relevant to improving RL for agentic tasks.

entry.title: Dynamical Memory Transformer: Selective Recurrent Memories with Constant Cost Attention

author.name: Yannis Bendi-Ouis (Mnemosyne), Xavier Hinaut (Mnemosyne)

entry.summary: Proposes the Dynamical Memory Transformer, a hybrid architecture that encodes sequences with memory units implemented as dynamical systems with input-dependent leak rates, then decodes via attention over memory outputs rather than token history. This aims to combine the constant-cost memory of state space models with the addressability of attention.

entry.title: TAPE: Learning General Audio Effect Representations

author.name: Phillip Long, Yongyi Zang, Qihui Yang, Christodoulos Benetatos, Junfei Liu, Randal Leistikow, Julian McAuley, Perry R. Cook

entry.summary: TAPE estimates the audio signal processing chain applied to a reference recording from the processed audio alone, using an encoder covering eight effect families and a differentiable DSP chain that decodes an embedding into editable parameters in one forward pass. It achieves lower spectral error than DeepAFx-ST, the prior state of the art, and enables transferring effect chains to new recordings. This has practical value for musicians and mixing engineers.

entry.title: ARK: Avoiding Routing Collisions for KV Cache Transfer in Disaggregated LLM Inference

author.name: Hung-Chun Lin, Ting-Wei Hsu, Chung-En Ho, Ahmed Saeed

entry.summary: ARK addresses ECMP hash-collision congestion when massive KV-cache transfers between disaggregated prefill and decode GPU pools overload individual spine links. Because these elephant flows are long-lived, ARK amortizes lightweight one-to-all coordination so senders can choose source ports that map concurrent flows to distinct paths. This is a systems contribution to making disaggregated LLM inference faster and more predictable.

entry.title: With foundation-model features, aggregator complexity does not improve cross-hospital discrimination in gastric whole-slide image classification

author.name: Nheng Vanchhay, Ali Hussain, Khan Ziaullah, Moon-Il Joo, Md Ariful Islam Mozumder, Rashedul Islam Sumon, Won-Ae Lee, Min-Sun Cho, Hyeong-Chan Shin, Yujun Park, Baek Hwan Cho, Nam-Hoon Cho, Heejung An, Heung-Kook Choi, Haeyoun Kang, Hyunki Kim, Hee Cheol Kim

entry.summary: Using 5,036 gastric histopathology slides from five Korean hospitals with leave-one-hospital-out validation on frozen pathology foundation-model features, this study finds that a complex hierarchical graph aggregator (CHIME-MIL) reaches AUC 0.837 but does not beat simple attention or max pooling under a matched recipe. The negative result suggests aggregator complexity adds little once foundation-model features are strong. This is a useful caution for computational pathology architecture work.

entry.title: Latent-Lens: Visual Perception in Small Language Models Through Latent Communication

author.name: Mo Shahdloo, Faegheh Sardari, Mathew Salvaris

entry.summary: Proposes Latent-Lens, a lightweight codec that lets a frozen vision-language model communicate visual information directly in latent space to a separately pretrained text-only small language model, avoiding the lossy discrete-text bottleneck. Targets modular multi-agent systems where SLMs' limited capacity makes input signal quality critical. Extends latent-communication methods to cross-modal, cross-model pairs.

entry.title: Don't Just Impute, Detect: Task-Aware Diffusion Pipelines for Edge Anomaly Detection

author.name: Jeongsu Park, Taehyeon Yun, Geonwoo Kim, Yuji Lim, Moohong Min

entry.summary: The paper identifies imputation bias in IIoT anomaly pipelines, where MSE-trained imputers smooth anomalies back toward normality, and proposes TADR, a conditional diffusion refiner trained against the loss landscape of a frozen downstream detector using tractable task-aware objectives. This improves joint imputation-and-detection on edge sensor data.

entry.title: Near-Optimal First-Order Regret for Bandits with Feedback Graphs

author.name: Mengxiao Zhang, Yuheng Zhang, Haipeng Luo, Paul Mineiro

entry.summary: The paper closes a gap between worst-case and first-order regret guarantees for adversarial bandits with known directed feedback graphs, achieving an expected first-order regret bound matching the graph dependence of the minimax bound for strongly observable graphs. Strong author lineup in online learning theory (Luo, Mineiro).

entry.title: RetryRoute: Retry-Aware Model Routing for Agentic Image Editing Services

author.name: Hanshuai Cui, Zhiqing Tang, Zhi Yao, Jun Luo, Weijia Jia

entry.summary: The authors identify sticky failures in agentic image-editing pipelines: after a rejected edit, retrying the same model succeeds only 17-53 percent as often as a first attempt across six models and three benchmarks. RetryRoute is a retry-aware router that conditions success estimates on failure history to decide between retrying, escalating, or giving up, improving cost-quality tradeoffs.

entry.title: Gradient Descent on Two ReLU Neurons: Global Landscape and Bifurcation Dynamics

author.name: Binghua Li, Mengzhe Li, Denny Wu, Tianhao Wang

entry.summary: Analyzes gradient flow on a minimal two-neuron ReLU teacher-student model, showing dynamics organize along an easy bisector direction and a hard splitting direction, with a population loss landscape where all nontrivial critical points are global optima. The work characterizes multi-phase feature learning via landscape and bifurcation analysis.

entry.title: CalibCause: A Quality-Gated, Interpretable and Calibrated Deep Learning Framework for Diabetic Retinopathy Grading

author.name: Sohaib Sulman, Muhammad Atif Saeed, Akhtar Jamil, Alaa Ali Hameed, Roland Aydin

entry.summary: Introduces a quality-gated mixture-of-experts framework for diabetic retinopathy grading combining per-expert visual explanations, label-free image-quality conditioning, knowledge distillation, and calibrated confidence with deferral. Evaluated on 51,310 fundus images across three datasets with external testing on two more, including leave-one-environment-out experiments and bootstrap confidence intervals.

entry.title: PersonaChatBench: Evaluating Chat Assistants with Diverse Simulated Users

author.name: Zheyuan Deng, Taoran Li, Jingwen Zhang, Yuante Li, Dachuan Zhao, Fulei Zhang, Yunkai Zhang, Zhikun Xu, Yajie Liao, Haichao Zhang, Haodi Hu, Cong Wang, Chen Yang, Siyang Wu, Defu Cao, Xu Hu, Haoming Li, Haixin Wang, Robert George, Weizhi Zhang, Yuchu Wang, Zhejian Peng, Yueying Li, Wanting Jiang, Shushu Liang, Zhiyuan Yu, Yifan Wang, Jintao Huang, Yijun Wang, Yuexing Hao, Xiaomin Li

entry.summary: PersonaChatBench evaluates chat assistants by pairing a fixed task with multiple simulated users governed by private persona cards specifying distinct needs, preferences, and behaviors, isolating how assistant performance varies across user conditions. It assesses 20 language models across six domains. The benchmark targets a real evaluation gap: robustness of assistants to user diversity rather than a single cooperative user.

entry.title: Sparse Autoencoders for Expert-Assisted Interpretation of Histopathology Foundation Model Embeddings

author.name: \v{S}imon \v{S}m\'ida, Wanda Benesova

entry.summary: The paper applies sparse autoencoders to decompose histopathology foundation model embeddings (CONCH, UNI2-h) into interpretable latent features aligned with morphological concepts pathologists use, such as tissue architecture and staining artifacts. Vanilla and Batch-TopK SAE variants are trained and evaluated for expert-assisted interpretation.

entry.title: TADP: Dual-Branch Temporally Adaptive Differential Privacy for Expression-Aware Video Anonymization

author.name: Feng Xu, Xun Li, Lars Petersson, Yulei Sui, David Ahmedt-Aristizabal, Dadong Wang

entry.summary: TADP privatizes identity and expression representations in video with temporally adaptive Gaussian noise mechanisms, composing the joint release through adaptive Renyi DP converted to (epsilon, delta) guarantees. It enables expression-aware video anonymization with formal privacy guarantees rather than ad hoc face blurring.

entry.title: Open-Weight MLLMs Cannot Compare What They Cannot Name

author.name: Wenxin Su, Anna Kreshuk

entry.summary: This paper probes open-weight MLLMs with a deceptively simple baseline: comparing body-part sizes in synthetic ant images for biological phenotype analysis. It finds state-of-the-art open-weight models fail on some body parts but not others despite visually trivial comparisons, suggesting failures trace to naming rather than visual capacity.

entry.title: Capability-Conditioned Graph Control Barrier Functions for Zero-Shot Safe Navigation of Heterogeneous Mobile Robot Teams

author.name: Joonkyung Kim, Janghyun Cho, Jeehyun Lee, Changjoo Nam, Yiwei Lyu

entry.summary: CC-HGCBF extends graph control barrier functions to heterogeneous fleets by conditioning on robot capabilities in a shared second-order reference-point operational space, enabling state-dependent capability representation and zero-shot transfer to unseen robot models. This goes beyond prior work that only distinguishes known robot classes or assumes homogeneous dynamics. It enables scalable decentralized safety for diverse, previously unseen robots.

entry.title: MolmoSpaces-CommonSense: Evaluating Commonsense in Robotic Manipulation Policies

author.name: Arjun Guru, Max Argus, Jae Sung Park, Jiafei Duan, Ali Farhadi, Ranjay Krishna

entry.summary: This paper introduces a taxonomy of reasoning processes for robotic manipulation grounded in developmental cognitive science, and operationalizes it as MolmoSpaces-CommonSense, a benchmark with tasks requiring reasoning about occlusion, containment, support relations, and semantically appropriate actions in cluttered scenes. Existing benchmarks mostly test low-level execution in clean environments. It matters because commonsense gaps in current manipulation policies are largely unmeasured.

entry.title: Higher-Order Kinematic Derivatives for Aspect-Preserving Real-Time Numerical Inverse Kinematics

author.name: Steffan Lloyd

entry.summary: The paper derives higher-order numerical inverse kinematics solvers (QuIK4, QuIK5) with fourth- and fifth-order convergence, plus an aspect-preserving step limiter that predicts and avoids singularities by extrapolating the Jacobian determinant. A Hermite-interpolation certifier verifies solutions belong to the same aspect as the seed. This yields faster, more reliable real-time IK for serial robots.

entry.title: ChatGPT as a Surveillance Assistant? An Exploratory Case Study of AI-Assisted Surveillance Risks

author.name: Ayana Hussain, Nicholas Vincent

entry.summary: This paper presents an exploratory case study of how ChatGPT's public web interface may assist potentially harmful surveillance tasks, contributing a taxonomy of seven surveillance risk categories instantiated as 110 prompts, half of which are jailbreak attempts. The authors manually review model responses to characterize what AI-assisted surveillance assistance looks like in practice. It matters because it empirically probes dual-use risks of widely deployed consumer LLMs rather than treating misuse as purely hypothetical.

entry.title: CIRCE Divines LLM Task Complexity from Constraint Structure

author.name: Chenhao Hong, Jiakai Xu, Kaushiki Singh, Yusen Zhang, Eugene Wu

entry.summary: Introduces CIRCE, which estimates LLM task difficulty before solving by extracting a Constraint Intermediate Representation from the problem text and deterministically compiling it into a constraint graph whose structural properties predict complexity. Across seven reasoning settings, this structure-based signal supports model routing, test-time compute allocation, and tool-needs prediction.

entry.title: Verifying Text-to-SQL Queries under Changing Business Semantics

author.name: Genliang Zhu, Xiaobo Chen, Ziyuan Wang, Chu Wang

entry.summary: This paper addresses the gap between a text-to-SQL query executing successfully and it being semantically correct after business definitions change, such as refund attribution or tax treatment revisions. The authors propose an executable verification profile that binds revision requests and knowledge cutoffs to counterexample data and exact monetary comparison, evaluated across 192 query-definition cells. It matters because it targets a real failure mode in production analytics where stale queries silently produce wrong numbers.

entry.title: Ask on Demand: Targeted Peer Communication for Parallel Agentic Systems

author.name: Haofu Yang, Hongyang Yin, Ran Bi, Faguo Wu, Peng Xue, Feng Zhou, Han Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes AOD, a framework where parallel LLM agents actively request targeted information from peers when specific needs arise, rather than pre-sharing summaries, using a lightweight trained gate to decide when assistance is worthwhile. This helps preserve useful discoveries that are otherwise isolated in individual agent execution histories. Relevant to scaling multi-agent collaboration.

entry.title: Breaking Information Islands in Sparse Tuning via Small-World Connectivity

author.name: Xianchao Guan, Zijun Xiong, Yifeng Wang, Yubo Cui, Yaowei Wang, Guo-Sen Xie, Xin Li, Zheng Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes SWIFT, a sparse fine-tuning framework combining block-diagonal sparse updates with a fixed deterministic scattering permutation to create small-world-like connectivity, preventing isolated feature dimensions that restrict task-specific interactions. Addresses the topology, not just the size, of sparse updates for parameter-efficient adaptation. Offers a fresh structural perspective on efficient LLM adaptation.

entry.title: TradeWar: A Benchmark for Execution-Grounded Trade Negotiation with Adaptive LLM Agents

author.name: Xiangyu Kong, Ruirui Yang, Xia Hou

entry.summary: Presents TradeWar, a multi-country negotiation benchmark that translates LLM dialogue into concrete tariff and trade-share policies with enforced capacity constraints, evaluating via an Economic Health Index, plus TACTIC, an agent using theory-of-mind and iterative refinement. It moves negotiation evaluation beyond agreement rates toward executed value.

entry.title: RiskyPy: Toward Model-Calibrated Prompt Generation for Joint Security and Functionality Evaluation of LLM-Generated Code

author.name: Zacharie Chenail-Larcher, Daniele Lunghi, Melissa Tessa, Quentin Sti\'evenart, Jacques Klein, Tegawend\'e F. Bissyand\'e, Florent Avellaneda, Naouel Moha

entry.summary: This paper introduces RiskyPy, an automated pipeline for generating security-focused code-generation benchmarks that are calibrated to a target model's proficiency using functionality and vulnerability canaries. The authors instantiate the pipeline for Python, covering 18 CWEs from the 2025 CWE Top 25 across 101 prompts, and show on Qwen3-4B and Seed-Coder-8B that generated tasks remain functionally accessible (57-72% pass rates). This matters because security evaluation of code LLMs currently relies on expensive, static benchmarks that do not adapt to model capability.

entry.title: When Disclosure Is Compulsory: Evaluating Ride-Hailing Rebalancing Policies with Self-Interested LLM Driver Agents

author.name: Xinyu Wang, Andres Fielbaum

entry.summary: Motivated by the EU Platform Work Directive requiring platforms to disclose automated decision parameters, this paper studies how ride-hailing rebalancing policies perform when drivers delegate decisions to self-interested LLM agents.
